NAFDAC'S FIGHT AGAINST COUNTERFEITS: DATABASE LAUNCH AND CRACKDOWN ON FAKE PRODUCTS


As reported in December 2023 by some news media, NAFDAC has launched a database for registered and certified drugs for sale and distribution in Nigeria (NAFDAC Greenbook). NAFDAC’s DG, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, stated that over 6,400 registered pharmaceutical products are contained in the Data base. She also noted that the database would be made accessible to members of the public latest by January 2024.

The link to the NAFDAC Greenbook (Registered Drugs Database): https://greenbook.nafdac.gov.ng/. As stated on the site, the database is still undergoing update on daily basis to prevent errors, discrepancies, and missing records.

Prof. Adeyeye said members of the public could log into the website using their android mobile phone to verify any drug of their choice. Prof. Adeyeye also said that NAFDAC was planning to phase out production and sale of alcohol in sachet by the end of January 2024. This ban on sachet alcohol is now officially effected.

NAFDAC carried out several raids in various parts of the country, especially in the South-east and South-south, where counterfeit products worth millions have been recovered and seized. One of the raids that took place in December, was in the Eziukwu market in Aba, Abia state, where NAFDAC intercepted counterfeiters involved in the production of a variety of fake beverages including wines, soft drinks, and other products. They also uncovered unethical practices such as date revalidation for expired products like peak milk, powdered milk, ketchup, yoghurt, coca-cola products, and packaging of fake and substandard products, which are later sold to unsuspecting members of the public for consumption. The street value of the confiscated and destroyed fake products is estimated at over 750M naira.

The DG of NAFDAC encouraged consumers to always scrutinize branded drinks to distinguish them from counterfeits before consumption. She advocated that Nigerians should buy only NAFDAC registered drinks from reputable and licenced retailers, bars and supermarkets.

“If the product is being sold well below its normal price, or doesn’t seem to include normal taxes on liquors, then it is probably fake. Check for poor quality packaging, spelling mistakes and unusually shaped bottles. Look for the contact information and address of the manufacturer. If it is missing, the alcohol is fake. Inspect the seal on the bottle. If the seal is broken or damaged, then the contents might have been interfered with and are not safe to drink. Check for fake bar codes. If you have an app on your mobile that scans bar codes, scan it and see if it’s listed as the correct product and beware of bad smells! If it smells like paint stripper or nail polish remover, then it probably is!”

She assured that NAFDAC will continue to ensure that the level of counterfeit products nationwide is brought to the nearest minimum so that Nigerians will continue to consume only healthy and safe products. She also encouraged the public to report any suspicious activity of illegal producers of adulterated products or similar activities to the nearest NAFDAC office nationwide.

*TOOTHACHE DAY, 2024*


Good dental health is not only about preventing toothaches; it’s also crucial for one's overall well-being. Poor dental health can lead to more severe health issues, including gum disease, heart disease, and diabetes. Regular dental care is an investment in health and quality of life.

*Toothache Day* is dedicated to raising awareness about dental health and the prevention of toothaches. It serves as a reminder of the importance of oral hygiene and dental care. It encourages individuals to take proactive steps to prevent toothaches and other dental issues. Toothaches can be incredibly painful and are often caused by dental problems such as cavities, gum disease, or tooth infections. The day emphasizes the significance of regular dental check-ups and good oral health practices.

Preventing toothaches and maintaining good oral health is essential. Some tips for dental health include:

1) Brushing the teeth twice daily (for at least 2 minutes per brushing) using a fluoride toothpaste.

2) Flossing daily helps to remove food particles and plaque from between the teeth and along the gum line.

3) Scheduling regular dental check-ups and cleanings with the Dentist. The appointments can help detect and prevent dental issues before they become painful or develop to more severe dental pathologies and complications.

4) Reducing consumption of sugary and acidic foods and drinks, since they can contribute to tooth decay.

5) Using fluoride toothpaste and mouthwashes.

6) One should protect the teeth if one plays contact sports. A mouth guard can be worn to protect the teeth from injury.

7) Using the teeth for stuffs such as opening a soft drink bottle among other improper practices is not healthy.

*The AFCON: LESSONS & POSITIVES from NIGERIA and the TOURNAMENT*


The Confederation of African Football (CAF), the CAF President (Patrice Motsepe), and all the officials that officiated in the tournament, must be commended. I'm totally impressed. With the officiating blunders (including VAR errors) that we do see in the EPL and other leagues in Europe, I never expected Africa to do better at football officiating than Europe. The Referees were fantastic, the Video Assistant Referees (VAR) was excellent. This is the best ever officiating I've witnessed in the world of football. Infact, the leagues in Europe have to learn from Africa and this tournament. In the words of Gary Neville, a former Manchester United player and current Sky News Pundit – "The standards of officiating set by this year's AFCON are honestly staggering. It's like they invented it. The Premier League and all of Europe have a lot of learning to do."

We learnt a lot from Nigeria's AFCON journey. I'll commend the team character, starting with the coach, José Peseiro. He faced a lot of criticism before the start of the tournament. A lot of Nigerians had even called for his dismissal some months ago. However, he stayed focused and persistent, and did his job excellently. One of the stand out decision he made that contributed to our AFCON success was changing the starting GK to Stanley Nwabali. Stanley changed everything about the team, and brought confidence to the defenders, other players, and to Nigerians. Having an excellent goalkeeper in a tournament is gold! Only this can change everything about the team.

Our Team Captain, Ahmed Musa, must be commended. He is the most capped Nigerian player in history with at least 108 caps (appearances). His leadership skills and aura was influential. Coach Peseiro described Musa as his adviser whom he always listens to, and who played a significant off-field role in the team. The atmosphere in the camp was impressive. There was unity and understanding. I was surprised to see the team singing and praying together, despite the religious and ethnic differences. Outside what our guys achieved football wise in the tournament, there is a lot of lessons that Nigerians should learn from their unity and team spirit. It's truly impressive. William Troost-Ekong did excellently as well, as the captain on the field during the matches. Fantastic leadership from him. Infact, the team is made up of a lot of leaders!

This year's AFCON came with a lot of lessons generally. One of them is to be consistent and not lose focus or energy at any point, or be over confident. Senegal (the defending Champions) had the best record of 3/3 wins in the group stage. They were tipped to go very far, but they got knocked out by the worst team that qualified from the group stage (the host, Côte d'Ivoire) just at the R16 stage! Cote d'Ivoire taught us the lesson of never writing off a team. They miraculously made it to the knockouts, and after they replaced the coach that coached them during the group stage, the team changed. Senegal may have probably thought they would easily beat Côte d'Ivoire in that R16 encounter, but it shocked them. Côte d'Ivoire surprisingly persevered and made it to the AFCON finals.

Another lesson learnt from the AFCON is that, the group stage is totally different from the knockouts, and won't dictate the outcome of the knockouts. All the 6 Group Winners after the group stage, got knocked out from the tournament before the semi-finals. Normally, one may have expected the finalists to be 2 Group Winners, but in a tournament, anything can happen. The finalists this year were from the same Group A, the runner-up and the best loser. Equatorial Guinea (EQG) who topped Group A with incredible performance and with a 4–2 and 4–0 wins in their last 2 games of the Group stage, got knocked out in the R16 by another best loser (Guinea), to everyone's surprise!

Africa have great leagues and great footballers. It must not be Europe always. South Africa have a great league. The starting 11 of the SA team constantly had about 8 players who played for the same team in the South African Premiership, Mamelodi Sundowns, who are the best in the league. The 8 teammates have been playing together for long, and this contributed to the coordinated football we witnessed from them. Our own Stanley Nwabali, who keeps for Chippa United in SA, was formally a GK for some clubs in Nigeria (Enyimba, Lobi Stars, Katsina United). This should be a challenge to football leagues in our African nations, including the NPFL. It's fantastic to see players from our local leagues perform highly in the International stage.


_What other lessons did you learn from the tournament?_

These are challenging times for everyone. Our depreciating naira and the rising cost of commodities and services creates some unhappiness in the hearts of people. This is a time to care, encourage, stay positive, and be sensitive to our environment as well as people's emotional and psychological health. It's a time to be sensitive in our communication and in our interaction with others. We have to stay optimistic and watch our mental health as we take measures that helps us guard our sanity. We'll push through these challenges as we stay optimistic to creating solutions and tackling them from the root cause.


Let's remember these mental health tips:

- Self-Care: Prioritize "Me Time"
- Set Boundaries. Work-Life Balance
- Talk It Out. Share Feelings
- Stress Relief. Exercise & Meditate
- Stay Informed, Not Overwhelmed
- Seek Support. Reach Out for Help
- Breaks Are Vital. Refresh & Recharge
- Learn to Say "No". Manage Workload
- Embrace Mistakes. Growth Mindset
- Celebrate Small Wins. Stay Positive!

*LEADERSHIP DAY, 2024*


Leadership Day is observed on February 20 each year. It is aimed at inculcating the values of leadership in each one of us. It reminds us that there is a leader within all of us. With encouragement and perseverance, we can all become leaders in our respective communities. If we all took up responsibilities and lead in our communities, the world would be a much better place. A good leader not only leads but inspires those around him to be the best versions of themselves. Anyone can be a leader — you just have to show up and encourage others to do the same.

Leadership is not just defined by a position of authority. Leadership is defined by influence and the impact you make around you. Leadership involves one showing up when necessary, contributing his/her ideas, skills/talent, and other resources, to make positive impact in a group, community or the society, and at the same time, influencing others around to show up in their unique ways and capacities. Growth, progress, and positive sustenance (in any sphere of life including one's personal life) cannot be experienced without leadership.


Today, *we celebrate every leader* (past and present) – in the Young Pharmacists Group (YPG), in the Pharmacy space, in every organization, in the society, in Nigeria, and in the World – who have made positive impacts and keep making positive impacts, to ensure growth, progress and positive sustenance.

Let us all keep learning about leadership, and keep growing as leaders. We can create the world we desire, and make an infinite impact of positivity.

Today, February 20, also marks the birthday of a renowned leadership expert, *John C. Maxwell* (born in 1947). Happy 77th Birthday to John Maxwell🎉. John Maxwell is an American author, speaker, and pastor, who has written many books, primarily focusing on leadership. His Impact in leadership is incredible! He's an inspiration.


Among all the Qualities of a leader, let's see these 2:

1) A leader creates a positive system and is only fulfilled when successors work to maintain the positive standards and even improve on them. A leader is unfulfilled if the standards set during his active leadership depreciates. To this effect, a leader ensures that he develops great successors. *The true goal of leadership is creating more leaders, and growing followers into leaders*.

2) A leader shows up first. A leader leads by showing his people how they should follow. A leader sets the pace. Followers are more likely to follow what a leader does than what a leader says. If you want to be positively impactful as a leader, show up first and set an example. If I desire my people to show up on any occasion or in any positive social or personal attributes, I have to show up first.

A leader is unfulfilled if the standards set during his active leadership depreciates. 2) A leader shows up first. A leader leads by showing his people how they should follow. A leader sets the pace. Followers are more likely to follow what a leader does than what a leader says. If you want to be positively impactful as a leader, show up first and set an example. If I desire my people to show up on any occasion or in any positive social or personal attributes, I have to show up first.

‎[22/02/2024, 08:35:24] ~ Dr. Favvy☺️: DIAPER RASH IN BABIES

Diaper rash is the most common skin condition seen in infants. More than half of them between the ages of 4-15 months have a diaper rash at least once in two months.

In mild cases, the skin may be red and tender but a more severe diaper rash would be painful and have open sores. Mild cases clear up within 3-4 days with home treatment but severe cases may need medical treatment.

Learn all you need to know about diaper rash👇🏼

*UPDATE ON LASSA FEVER*


Lassa fever is an acute viral hemorrhagic (excessive bleeding) illness that is transmitted to humans through contact with food or household items contaminated by infected rodents or contaminated persons. Symptoms include: fever, headache, sore throat, general body weakness, cough, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, muscle pains, chest pain, and in severe cases, unexplainable bleeding from ears, eyes, nose, mouth, and other body openings.


The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) has said Nigeria recorded *411 confirmed cases and 72 deaths* from Lassa fever across 21 states of the federation from week one to week six of 2024. The NCDC in its latest situation report for week six spanning 5 to 11 February, revealed that the number of new confirmed cases increased from 70 in week 5 to 83, with nine deaths in the reporting week.

According to the situation report, 65% of all the confirmed cases were from Ondo, Edo, and Bauchi while 35% were reported from 17 states. The report noted that the number of suspected cases in 2024 (2,122) decreased when compared to that reported for the same period in 2023 (8280).

According to the NCDC, the predominant age group affected by Lassa fever is 21–30 years, and 2 new health workers were affected in the reporting week. NCDC added that the National Lassa fever multi-partner, multi-sectoral Incident Management System has been activated to coordinate response at all levels at the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC).

NCDC also enumerated some of the challenges in its fight against Lassa fever across the country, listing; late presentation of the cases leading to an increase in CFR, and poor health-seeking behaviour due to the high cost of treatment and clinical management. Other challenges are poor environmental sanitation conditions and poor awareness reportedly observed in high-burden communities.

*LASSA FEVER PREVENTION*


1) Primary transmission of the Lassa virus from its host to humans can be prevented by avoiding contact with mastomys rodents. Putting food away in rodent-proof containers and keeping the home clean help to discourage rodents from entering homes. Transmission to humans normally occurs through contamination of broken skin or mucous membranes via direct or indirect contact with infected rodent excreta on floors, home surfaces, in food or water. Transmission is also possible where rodents are caught and consumed as food.

2) When caring for patients with Lassa fever, further transmission of the disease through person-to-person contact or nosocomial routes can be avoided by taking preventive precautions against contact with patient secretions. Such precautions include wearing protective clothing, such as masks, gloves, gowns, and goggles; using infection control measures, such as complete equipment sterilization; and isolating infected patients from contact with unprotected persons until the disease has run its course.

3) Further, educating people in high-risk areas about ways to decrease rodent populations in their homes will aid in the control and prevention of Lassa fever.

*Ribavirin*, an antiviral drug, has been used with success in Lassa fever patients. Patients should also receive early supportive care with rehydration and symptomatic treatment.

*PSN Commends PCN and NAFDAC For Sealing the Sabongeri Open Drug Market in Kano.*
By Fabian Anawo 

The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria, PSN, has commended the Pharmacists Council of Nigeria and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC for sealing the Sabongeri Drug Market in Kano

It was shut down to enforce the relocation of all operators to the Coordinated Wholesale Centre, CWC, which has been inaugurated for operation in Kano since 2023.

In a statement, the President of PSN, Professor Cyril Usifoh said that the action of the two regulatory agencies was commendable because the Coordinated Wholesale Centre was built to discourage sales of medicines in open markets.

Professor Usifoh said that the National Drug Distribution Guidelines, NDDG, that was approved in 2015 incorporates the concept of CWCs for genuine pharma players currently in Open Drug Markets and has come to stay going by the Kano experience.

He said that the closure of open drug markets in the country was the only way to redress the problems in the drug distribution channels which he described as monumental

The PSN therefore called on the State Governments in Lagos, Anambra, Abia, Enugu, Oyo and Borno to give speedy building plan approvals as well as other requisite logistics support to pave way for the construction of CWCs in their States.

 He said that building CWCs would facilitate the smooth relocation of those who presently operate in Idumota, Lagos; Headbridge, Onitsha, Anambra; Ariaria, Aba, Abia; Ogbete, Enugu; Agbeni, Ibadan, Oyo and Gamboru, Maiduguri in Borno.

According to Professor Usifoh, the full implementation of the NDDG will allow full integration of committed players to run their business within the purview of existing statutes that drive the enforcement activities of the PCN and NAFDAC..

The PSN also called on the National Assembly to formally complete the amendment bill of the Fake Drug Act currently before it. 

"For us at PSN, we must formalize the PCN and NAFDAC relationship through more legislative actions beyond the existing windows in the NAFDAC Act and PCN Act 2022 which both provide for representation of key personnel of each of the agencies on the board of the partnering agency.

"The historic joint team action of Saturday, February 17, 2024 remains a water shed which we must make sustainable through the instrumentality of the Federal and State Task Forces on Fake, Counterfeit Drug and Unwholesome Foods in a well packaged and robust Act of Parliament.

"We solicit amongst other reforms increases in the penalties provided for first offenders who violate the Fake Drug Act, while subsequent trespasses must attract jail sentences without an option for fine. 

"The National Assembly must also look at the possibilities of factoring in appropriate security squads to aid the responsibilities of the State Taskforces as the recent Kano operation of Saturday February 17, 2023 confirms the need for maintenance squads of law enforcement agents to sustain and ensure fruitful outcomes when the Taskforce, PCN or NAFDAC embarks on their routine regulatory functions.

"It is also imperative to call on the PCN and NAFDAC as we congratulate them for shifting attention to unregistered pharmaceutical premises to complete the cycle by tackling the plethora of illegal and unlawful drug stores in hospital facilities especially at private sector level."

Stakeholders in pharmacy practice have always lamented that while PCN and NAFDAC maintains frequent surveillance, monitoring and control of registered pharmaceutical premises, it obviously closes its eyes on unregistered pharma premises including those located in the plethora of private hospital facilities. 

They have always accused hospital facilities of carrying drug stock far in excess of regular pharmacy facilities irrespective of whether the drugs are registered or not by NAFDAC.

"The impunity with which these brazen acts of hospital facilities are conducted encourages them to sell drugs at exorbitant prices far in excess of community pharmacies at private sector level and public pharmacies in government hospitals," the statement says.

A WHO report puts the cost of drugs in private hospitals at 184% above base

[26/02/2024, 21:18:15] ~ .: Highlights of Federal Executive Council decisions on Monday 26 February

Here are some of the highlights of the far reaching decisions taken today at the Federal Executive Council meeting, chaired by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

1. FEC approved construction of Lagos-Port Harcourt-Calabar Coastal Superhighway to Messrs Hitech Construction Africa. The First phase made up of 47 kms will begin in Lagos.
2. Social security payments to the vulnerable households to begin immediately. Recipients will be those with NIN and BVN.

3. Social security payments to be extended to graduates from NCE and upwards

4. Consumer Credit to be established very urgently. Chief of Staff to lead a committee that includes Budget Minister, Attorney-General, Coordinating Minister of the Economy and Finance, to make the scheme a reality.

5. The Council in order to enhance efficiency in the Federal service, and reduce the cost of governance, decided to implement the recommendations of the Steve Oronsaye panel on the restructuring and rationalisation of Federal agencies, parastatals and commissions.

The implementation involves merging, subsuming and scrapping agencies with similar functions.

The Oronsaye report was submitted in 2012 to the Jonathan administration. In 2014, the Jonathan government released a white paper on the report. The Buhari administration after re-examining the white paper also released a second white paper in August 2022, but did not implement the report.

However, the Tinubu administration has decided to confront the monster of high governance cost by implementing elements of the report.

An eight-man committee has a 12-week deadline to ensure that the necessary legislative amendments and administrative restructuring needed to implement the reforms are effected in an efficient manner.

The committee comprises Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Head of the Civil Service, Attorney General and Justice Minister, Budget and Planning Minister, DG Bureau of Public Service Reform, Special Adviser to the President on Policy Coordination, Special assistant to the president on National Assembly. The Cabinet Affairs Office will serve as the secretariat.

Key recommendations for implementation:

National Salaries, Income and wages Commission to be subsumed under Revenue Mobilisation and Fiscal Commission. The National Assembly will need to amend the constitution as RMAFC was established by the constitution.

Infrastructure Concession and Regulatory Commission to be merged with Bureau of Public Enterprise and be rechristened as `Public Enterprises and Infrastructural Concession Commission

National Human Rights Commission to swallow Public Complaints Commission

Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate(PTAD) to be scrapped and functions to be taken over by Federal Ministry of Finance

NEMA and National Commission for Refugees to be fused to become National Emergency and Refugee Management Commission

Border Communities Development Agency to become a department under National Boundary Commission

NACA and NCDC to be merged

SERVICOM to become a department under the Bureau for Public Service Reform(BPSR)

NALDA to return to the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security.

 Federal Ministry of Science to supervise a new agency that combines NCAM, NASENI and PRODA

 National Commission for Museums and Monuments and National Gallery of Arts to become one entity that will be known as National Commission for Museums, Monuments and Gallery of Arts.

National Theatre to be merged with National Troupe.
13. Directorate of Technical Cooperation in Africa and Directorate of Technical Aid Corp to be merged under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

 Nigerians in Diaspora Commission to become an agency under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

 Federal Radio Corporation and Voice of Nigeria to be one entity to be known as Federal Broadcasting Corporation of Nigeria

 National Biotechnology Development Agency(NABDA) and National Centre for Genetic Resources and Biotechnology to be emerged into an agency to be known as National Biotechnology Research and Development Agency(NBRDA).

National Institute for Leather Science Technology and National Institute for Chemical Technology to become one agency.

 Nigeria Natural Medicine Development Agency and National Institute of Pharmaceutical Research and Development to become one agency.

The National Metallurgical Development Centre and National Metallurgical Training Institute will be merged.

 National Institute for Trypanosomiasis to be subsumed under Institute of Veterinary Research in Vom, Jos.

The list is not exhaustive.

Bayo Onanuga
Special Adviser Information and Strategy to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu

[27/02/2024, 09:51:59] David Ypg Edo PRO: *WORLD NGO DAY, 2024*


Every year on February 27, the *World NGO Day* is celebrated. The day is celebrated in more than 96 countries and over 6 continents. The International day is dedicated to recognize, celebrate and honour all non-governmental and nonprofit organizations, and the people behind them that contribute to the society all year around. The day was first celebrated in 2014. There are over 10 million NGOs and nonprofits worldwide, with over 50 million staffs/workers.

The theme for 2024 World NGO Day is: “Building a sustainable future; the role of NGOs in achieving the SDGs”.

According to AllAfrica, there are *over 46,000* NGOs registered in Nigeria. These NGOs often collaborate with government agencies, international organisations, and local communities to create lasting positive change in Nigerian society.

The types of NGOs/areas of
NGOs in Nigeria are: Youth development, Democracy and good governance, Environment, Health, HIV/AIDS, Education, Research and Policy, Poverty, Human Rights, Religion, Agriculture.

NGOs in Nigeria play a crucial role in addressing various social, economic, and environmental issues. Here are some of the key roles of NGOs in Nigeria.

1) Frequently fight for policy changes and raise awareness about issues affecting Nigerian society.

2) Primarily assist in the building and operation of infrastructure.

3) Do research and contribute to the advancement of knowledge on contemporary concerns. They create research-based, innovative solutions to social challenges.

4) Provide critical services to communities, particularly in underserved or marginalised areas. These services include healthcare, education, clean water, sanitation, and vocational training.

5) Implement poverty alleviation programs that aim to improve the economic well-being of disadvantaged and vulnerable populations.

6) Active in the healthcare sector, working to improve access to quality healthcare services, combat diseases, and promote public health awareness.

7) Work on peacebuilding initiatives, reconciliation, and conflict resolution programs in regions affected by conflict or violence.

8) Dedicated to promoting gender equality and empowering women and girls. They provide training, support, and advocacy for women's rights and economic empowerment.

9) Partner with communities to identify their needs and priorities and facilitate community-led development projects and initiatives.

10) In areas where the government cannot reach out to people, NGOs help disseminate information about government schemes, policies and programs.

*5 FACTS ABOUT SMELL*


1) Your smell is renewed every month. Your scent cells can regenerate and are renewed every 30 to 60 days.

2) A human's nose can detect at least one trillion distinct scents.

3) Boy, dogs can smell you! Dogs can distinguish non-identical twins based on odor, and they have more scent cells than humans, almost 44 times more.

4) Age-related anosmia is linked to race. According to research, African-Americans and Hispanics experience age-related loss of smelling earlier than Caucasians.

5) Smelling is unique. Everyone has their unique identity odor similar to a fingerprint, which means no two people can smell things the same way.

What causes no smell in the nose? The most common causes of anosmia include nasal congestion, allergy, sinus infection, or air pollution. However, there are many factors that cause anosmia.

Anosmia Awareness Day encourages and motivates people to take care of their ENT Health. It also motivates researchers to study more about olfactory dysfunction.
‎[27/02/2024, 13:59:22] David Ypg Edo PRO: ‎image omitted
[27/02/2024, 13:59:23] David Ypg Edo PRO: ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬
*⚕️PHARMACEUTICAL SOCIETY OF NIGERIA*
*YOUNG PHARMACISTS GROUP*
*EDO STATE CHAPTER*

*MEDIA/PUBLICITY/EDITORIAL COMMITTEE*
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬


*ANOSMIA AWARENESS DAY, 2024*


*Anosmia Awareness Day* is observed annually on February 27. It is a day to spread awareness about anosmia, which is the loss of the sense of smell, or as some people call it, nose blind. Loss of sense of smell (olfactory function) is not to be taken lightly, and people need to be educated to prevent anosmia. Anosmia has been found to be associated with Alzheimer's disease in the future (hyposmia is a partial loss of the sense of smell).

Smell helps people to detect danger in their environments, such as smoke and noxious fumes. Smell is also useful in eating and keeping overall good health. By celebrating Anosmia Awareness Day, people can explore the reasons for anosmia and the different treatments that can bring relief and recovery.

Anosmia Awareness Day was established by *Daniel Schein* in 2012. Schein was diagnosed with anosmia in the fifth grade. But it was not until 2011 that he started his research about anosmia and decided to create an organization called Anosmia Awareness. He created a Facebook community for this cause.

Anosmia affects over 200,000 people in the U.S. alone, and there is no real cure or treatment for it at this time. However, many of these patients have found ways to work around their condition.

Those who suffer from Anosmia need to stay cautious at all times as they are unable to detect gas leaks, wildfires, or spoiled food with their sense of smell. Moreover, some people also find it hard to eat food without their sense of smell. Numerous studies reveal that those who suffer from olfactory disorders are more likely to suffer from depression and anxiety. Therefore, when a day is solely dedicated to people suffering from Anosmia, it helps people understand the mental and physical difficulties that are associated with olfactory disorders.

*RARE DISEASE DAY, 2024*


*Rare Disease Day* takes place annually, on the last day of February, to raise awareness among policymakers and the public about rare diseases and its impact on patients' lives. The European Organisation for Rare Diseases established the day in 2008 to raise awareness for unknown or overlooked illnesses. This year, it falls on *February 29*, the rarest day of the year (leap year). Over 300 million people are affected by rare diseases globally. About 7000 rare diseases have been identified.

In the United States, a *Rare disease* is one that fewer than 200,000 people live with. (In other words, 60 per 100,000 individuals). Around the world, rare diseases are identified and addressed differently. The European Union considers a disease rare if it affects no more than 50 per 100,000 people. The World Health Organization, on the other hand, defines a rare disease as one that strikes fewer than 65 per 100,000 people.

A rare disease is often genetic. Other rare diseases could be the result of an infection or allergy. In many cases the exact cause is unknown. Some cancers are also rare diseases. Rare diseases tend to appear in childhood. Approximately two-thirds of those living with a rare disease are children. They are, unfortunately, usually incurable. About 95% of all rare diseases do not yet have treatments, according to the National Organization of Rare Diseases.

Here is a link to the Rare Disease Database by the National Organization of Rare Diseases (NORD):
https://rarediseases.org/rare-diseases/

Some Rare Diseases include:

1) Stoneman Syndrome (frequency: one in 2 million people)

2) Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS) [frequency: one in 4 million. More than 130 cases reported in scientific literature globally since 1886]

3) Chronic Focal Encephalitis (Rasmussen’s Encephalitis) [frequency: In Germany, it is 2.4 cases per 10 million people, and in the UK it is 1.7 per 10 million people]

*INTERNATIONAL REPETITIVE STRAIN INJURY (RSI) AWARENESS DAY, 2024*


International Repetitive Strain Injury Awareness Day, observed on February 29th each year, aims to raise awareness about RSI and promote prevention strategies. The day was first established in 2000 by the International RSI Awareness Day Committee, a group of healthcare professionals, educators, and activists dedicated to addressing the growing problem of RSI.

The significance of this day lies in its ability to bring attention to the importance of early intervention, proper ergonomics, and workplace safety. It serves as a reminder for individuals and organizations to prioritize the prevention of RSI and take proactive measures to create a healthier and safer work environment.


Repetitive strain injuries are very common. They lead to many conditions, including: Tendinitis, Carpal tunnel syndrome, Tennis elbow, Trigger finger and trigger thumb, Osgood-Schlatter disease, Back strains and sprains, Shin splints.

*Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI)* is a condition that affects millions of people around the world. It is a type of musculoskeletal disorder that occurs as a result of repetitive movements, forceful exertions, or awkward postures. RSI can affect various parts of the body, including the hands, wrists, arms, shoulders, neck, and back. A repetitive strain injury is damage to your muscles, tendons or nerves caused by repetitive motions and constant use. They’re also sometimes called repetitive stress injuries.

The primary cause of RSI is the repetitive nature of certain activities. Jobs that involve repetitive motions, such as typing, assembly line work, and using vibrating tools, put individuals at a higher risk of developing RSI. In addition, poor posture, working in the cold, inadequate rest breaks, and lack of ergonomic equipment can contribute to the development of this condition.

Symptoms of RSI may include pain, stiffness, swelling, numbness, and tingling in the affected area. These symptoms can range from mild to severe and may worsen over time if not addressed. It is important to recognize the early signs of RSI and seek appropriate treatment to prevent further damage.


*How can you prevent RSI?*

The best way to avoid a repetitive strain injury is to avoid overusing your body.

During sports or other physical activities:

1) Wear the right protective equipment.

2) Don’t “play through it” if you feel pain during or after physical activity.

3) Give your body time to rest and recover after intense activity.

4) Stretch and warm up before playing sports or working out.

5) Cool down and stretch after physical activity.

Improving your posture will help avoid extra stress on your body.

And that reminds me:
Please if you live in Nigeria,
Before you believe any genotype or blood group result, kindly ensure you do the test in at least 2 places - INCLUDING one government teaching hospital and one ‘reputable’ private laboratory.

I have seen relationships ruined due to fake genotype results. I have seen children’s lives destroyed due to wrong genotype of parents. I have seen marriages threatened and wrecked over wrong genotype problems.

Do NOT be quick to assume repeated “malaria” is equal to AA. Do NOT make this mistake- it can be very costly.

Don’t get me wrong. People with AA genotype are prone to having more malaria infections compared to AS or SC or SS. Sometimes the reason you have repeated malaria is because you have terrible drainage in front of your house which breeds mosquitoes repeatedly and you never use mosquito nets or insecticides before you sleep. This is possibly why you get a lot of malaria infections- not that you are AA.

Anyway pls don’t just assume you are AA without elaborate testing at two reputable medical centers including one government teaching hospital and one reputable medical laboratory.

You should get the exact same result from the two places if it is done rightly and appropriately. IF you do your genotype test and one place is telling you one thing and the other place is telling you something else, FIRST check where the tests were done. IF you know it was done at one substandard place, please go and repeat it in a proper standard reputable medical centre. And then double check the result from there by doing it in one more other reputable centre.

Most likely, IF you do your genotype in two reputable medical centers, you will get the same result. This is your true genotype.

Now in the rare exceptional circumstance, where you have done the genotype in two reputable centres and you get different results, pls go to a specialist hospital and ask to speak with a haematologist (this is a specialist who expertly handles genotype problems). They will resolve the issue for you.

I am sorry but I have to admit this. There are a lot of unchecked quack “labs” in Nigeria giving people wrong, fake and misleading blood group and genotype results.

People have lost the love of their lives because some quack lab somewhere told them they are AS when they are actually AA (so they broke up with their AS partner not knowing they are infact AA).

And equally, some people have married someone they should not have married because one lab told them they are AA when they are actually AS. (and the other person too is AS).

I really hope this little writeup will help someone somewhere do that genotype test today and know exactly where you stand. Kindly repost and retweet to help someone out there.

Pls share your stories or any one you know who has been a victim of fake genotype results as well.
Thank you.

*WORLD BIRTH DEFECTS DAY, 2024*


Every year, about 3–6% of infants worldwide are born with a serious birth defect. This means that life-altering conditions such as spina bifida and congenital heart defects affect millions of babies and families.

March 3 is recognized annually as World Birth Defects Day. Birth defects affect infants regardless of birthplace, race, or ethnicity. They are a leading cause of death for infants and young children globally. Those who survive and live with these conditions are at increased risk for lifelong disabilities.

The most common birth defects are: heart defects, cleft lip/palate, Down syndrome, spina bifida.

Most birth defects are caused by genetic or environmental factors or a combination of the two (multifactorial birth defects). In most cases, however, the cause is unknown. An environmental cause can include drugs, alcohol, or a disease the mother has that can increase the chance for the baby to be born with a birth defect. An agent that can cause a birth defect is known as a teratogen. *Multifactorial birth defects* are caused by a combination of genes and environmental exposures. In other words, a person can inherit a gene that increases sensitivity to an environmental trigger. Examples include cleft lip or palate, certain heart defects, and neural tube defects.

A mother-to-be can *lower the chances of having a kid with birth defects* through:

1) Staying healthy before deciding to become pregnant.

2) Stop smoking. Babies born to mothers who smoke tend to be lower birth weight; in addition exposure to secondhand smoke can harm the fetus.

3) Eating healthy diet.

4) Maintaining healthy weight.

5) Medical management of preexisting conditions such as hypertension, diabetes.

6) Taking 400 micrograms of folic acid each day can help lower the risk of neural tube defects, or birth defects of the brain and spinal cord. The vitamin is also found in some green leafy vegetables, nuts, beans, citrus fruits, and fortified breakfast cereals.

7) Avoiding exposure to alcohol and drugs during pregnancy. Be sure to inform the physician of any medications and herbal supplements one is taking, since they can all have adverse effects on the developing fetus.

8) Avoid exposure to harmful substances. These include lead, pesticides, and radiation (i.e., x-rays), which may harm the developing fetus.

9) Lower your risk for infection. Pregnant women should avoid eating undercooked meat and raw eggs and avoid all contact and exposure to cat feces and cat litter, which may contain a parasite, toxoplasma gondii, that causes toxoplasmosis. Other sources of infection include insects that have been in contact with cat feces.

10) Take a daily vitamin, that contributes to one's health as well as the health of the foetus.

11) Dealing with domestic violence. Women who are abused before pregnancy may be at risk for increased abuse during pregnancy. This can contribute to birth defects.

*WORLD OBESITY DAY, 2024*


World Obesity Day (4 March) 2024 is themed: *'Let's Talk About Obesity And...'*, and it seeks to leverage the power of World Obesity Day to start cross-cutting conversations. Looking at health, youth, and the world around us to see how we can address obesity together. As such, the Global Obesity Coalition – consisting of UNICEF, WHO, and the World Obesity Federation – is hosting *a global youth-led webinar* to unlock conversations about how this topic affects the lives of young people around the world and the concrete change young people are demanding. The online global event will serve as a moment for those decision-makers working in UN agencies, academia, civil society, and government to listen up. The webinar is on Monday, 4 March, by 2pm CET.

Register for the Webinar here: https://events.blackthorn.io/en/0N1cK1X7/obesity-and-youth-young-people-catalysing-change-4a3OP33dPp/overview


At the individual level, one may be able to *reduce their risk of Obesity by* adopting preventive interventions at each step of the life cycle, starting from pre-conception and continuing during the early years. These include:

1) ensuring appropriate weight gain during pregnancy;

2) practicing exclusive breastfeeding in the first 6 months after birth and continued breastfeeding until 24 months or beyond;

3) supporting behaviours of children around healthy eating, physical activity, sedentary behaviours and sleep, regardless of current weight status;

4) limiting screen time;

5) limiting consumption of sugar sweetened beverages and energy-dense foods and promote other healthy eating behaviours;

6) enjoying a healthy life (healthy diet, avoid late night eating/snacking, physical activity, sleep duration and quality, avoid tobacco and alcohol, emotional self-regulation);

7) limiting energy intake from total fats and sugars and increasing consumption of fruit and vegetables, as well as legumes, whole grains and nuts;

8) engaging in regular physical activity.


*Health practitioners* need to:

1) assess the weight and height of people accessing the health facilities to evaluate BMI;

2) provide counselling on healthy diet and lifestyles;

3) when a diagnosis of obesity is established, provide integrated obesity prevention and management health services including on healthy diet, physical activity and medical and surgical measures;

4) monitor other noncommunicable disease risk factors (blood glucose, lipids and blood pressure) and assess the presence of comorbidities and disability, including mental health disorders.


The *food industry* can play a significant role in promoting healthy diets by:

1) reducing the fat, sugar and salt content of processed foods;

2) ensuring that healthy and nutritious choices are available and affordable to all consumers;

3) restricting marketing of foods high in sugars, salt and fats, especially those foods aimed at children and teenagers;

4) ensuring the availability of healthy food choices and supporting regular physical activity practice in the workplace.

‎[04/03/2024, 09:31:29] ~ Dr. Favvy☺️: Have you ever heard of the fifth disease?🤔

Also known as Erythema infectiosum or Parvovirus B19 or ‘Slapped cheek disease’, it is a fairly mild viral disease that commonly affects children.

It spreads through contact with infected respiratory secretions, and can also be passed from a mother to her unborn child.

And it is listed as the fifth of the five common viral rash diseases of childhood, hence it is called the ‘Fifth disease’...

Learn more...👇🏼

[05/03/2024, 09:20:27] St. Pharm  Yp Justine: PHARMACY COUNCIL OF NIGERIA HAS CHANGED IT'S PAYMENT PORTAL.

BELOW IS THE NEW PROCEDURE FOR PAYMENT ON THE NEW PCN PAY PORTAL

*i.	Guideline for Creating an Account as a Stakeholder (Licensed Pharmacist).*

a.	Access the portal by visiting https://pay.pcn.gov.ng/Identity/Account/Register?returnUrl=%2F

b.	Enter your PCN full registration number

c.	Your details would pop up after some seconds to a minute

d.	Enter and confirm a password of your choice

e.	Login with your new login details (username: pharmacist full registration number and your new password)

*ii.	Guide to Making Payments on the New PCN Pay Portal*

a.	Visit https://pay.pcn.gov.ng/ and login with the details generated in (i) above.

b.	Click on Make Payment

c.	Click on Generate New Payment

d.	Select the Appropriate Payment Category

e.	Select Revenue and Payment years

f.	Select the Appropriate Payment Type. (The amount to be paid will automatically display; however, in cases where the amount does not automatically display, please get in touch with the PCN office for clarification.)

g.	If you are making a single payment, you can click on “Pay Now” at this point, but if you are making multiple payments, you should click on “Add to Payment Cart” till you have selected all the payments you are making before clicking “Pay Now.”

h.	Select “Online Payment” as the preferred payment method.

i.	Click on the “Remita” icon

j.	At this point, you can make payment online using your ATM Card via the “Card Option” or obtain the RRR Code to take to the bank via the “Bank Branch” option.

*iii.	General Payment Option for Non-Stakeholders and Those Without Accounts.*

a.	Visit https://pay.pcn.gov.ng/

b.	Click on “Make General Payment”

c.	Select the appropriate payment category

d.	Select the appropriate payment type. (The amount to be paid will automatically display; however, in cases where the amount does not automatically display, please get in touch with the PCN office for clarification.)

e.	Enter the appropriate payment description

f.	Select the appropriate State Location

g.	Select Payer’s Name, Phone, and Email

h.	Click on “Pay Now."”
i.	Select “Online Payment” as the preferred payment method.

j.	Click on the “Remita” icon

k.	At this point, you can make payment online using your ATM Card via the “Card Option” or obtain the RRR Code to take to the bank via the “Bank Branch” option.

[05/03/2024, 14:55:53] ~ Helen Ibemesim: *#HEARTBEAT2024 COUNTDOWN: 69 DAYS AWAY...*

*Igue festival* (also known as King's Festival) is a celebration with its origin in the Benin Kingdom of Edo State, southern Nigeria. 
The Festival was initiated in the 14th century during the reign of Oba Ewuare 1
One tradition states that the festival date coincided with the marriage of Ewuare to a wife named Ewere.
The festival however now consists of several other festivals put together by the Oba Akenzua II. This is because he wanted the festival to last for couple of days due to the current movement of people and the Igue festival has become a terminal for many other festivals celebrated by the Benin people between Christmas and New Year, the festival includes the Oba's blessing of the land and his people.

 During the Igue ritual season, the Oba is prohibited from being in the presence of any non-native person.

The 16th ALPs biennial National Conference holds in Benin City Edo state in 69 days' time.

[06/03/2024, 23:35:29] Stet Ypgdd: Good evening MOH... Please someone should assist me on how to pay my license fee.
[07/03/2024, 00:06:42] David Ypg Edo PRO: PHARMACY COUNCIL OF NIGERIA HAS CHANGED IT'S PAYMENT PORTAL.

BELOW IS THE NEW PROCEDURE FOR PAYMENT ON THE NEW PCN PAY PORTAL

*i.	Guideline for Creating an Account as a Stakeholder (Licensed Pharmacist).*

a.	Access the portal by visiting https://pay.pcn.gov.ng/Identity/Account/Register?returnUrl=%2F

b.	Enter your PCN full registration number

c.	Your details would pop up after some seconds to a minute

d.	Enter and confirm a password of your choice

e.	Login with your new login details (username: pharmacist full registration number and your new password)

*ii.	Guide to Making Payments on the New PCN Pay Portal*

a.	Visit https://pay.pcn.gov.ng/ and login with the details generated in (i) above.

b.	Click on Make Payment

c.	Click on Generate New Payment

d.	Select the Appropriate Payment Category

e.	Select Revenue and Payment years

f.	Select the Appropriate Payment Type. (The amount to be paid will automatically display; however, in cases where the amount does not automatically display, please get in touch with the PCN office for clarification.)

g.	If you are making a single payment, you can click on “Pay Now” at this point, but if you are making multiple payments, you should click on “Add to Payment Cart” till you have selected all the payments you are making before clicking “Pay Now.”

h.	Select “Online Payment” as the preferred payment method.

i.	Click on the “Remita” icon

*INTERNATIONAL WOMEN'S DAY (IWD), 2024*


*International Women's Day* (March 8) is a global day celebrating the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women. The day also marks a call to action for accelerating women's equality, raising awareness about discrimination, and taking action to drive gender parity. International Women's Day (IWD) has occurred for well over a century, with the first IWD gathering in 1911 supported by over a million people.

The campaign theme for International Women's Day 2024 is *Inspire Inclusion*. When we inspire others to understand and value women's inclusion, we forge a better world. When women themselves are inspired to be included, there's a sense of belonging, relevance, and empowerment. Collectively, we can forge a more inclusive world for women.

Organizations, groups, and individuals worldwide can all play a part - in the community, at work, at home, and beyond. To truly include women means to openly embrace their diversity of race, age, ability, faith, body image, and how they identify. Worldwide, women must be included in all fields of endeavour.

Organizations and groups can inspire Inclusion through action in areas such as:

• forging women's economic empowerment

• recruiting, retaining and developing diverse talent

• supporting women and girls into leadership, decision-making, business and STEM

• designing and building infrastructure meeting the needs of women and girls

• helping women and girls make informed decisions about their health

• involving women and girls in sustainable agriculture and food security

• providing women and girls with access to quality education and training

• elevating women and girl's participation and achievement in sport

• promoting creative and artistic talent of women and girls

• addressing further areas supporting the advancement of women and girls

*INTERNATIONAL WOMEN'S DAY, 2024*


In *Emzor*'s X (Twitter) space event (today) for the International Women's Day, *Yimika Oguns* and *Adeola Ayoola* were the speakers on _Empowering Women to Champion Transformation and Innovation_.

*Yimika Oguns* is currently the Senior Brand Manager of Emzor Pharmaceuticals. She is the *first female National Coordinator* of the PSN-Young Pharmacists Group (2020). She made fantastic points in her speech. In Yimika's speech... If you don't show up, no body will know what you have to offer. Empower yourself, build your confidence, volunteer. Be prepared for every opportunity. Volunteering gives you room to identify areas where you are not very skilled at, which you can work on and improve on. Always put in your best. Also, be open to taking risk. If you want to advance, you have to be open to taking educated and calculated risks. For a lady, *confidence* is probably the strongest quality needed in leadership. Leverage on your experiences. Volunteering and Leadership helps you to grow and develop yourself. Attend events, conferences, health tech events, etcetera. Always celebrate yourself.

*Adeola Ayoola*, the CEO/Cofounder of Famasi Africa, emphasized on continuous learning. One have to keep learning, be emotionally resilient, and ask questions. Stereotypes and obstacles will always come, but you have to always stay grounded. Show that you can get it done. Challenge yourself. Develop competence. As you seek to obtain value, also learn to provide value at the same time.

[09/03/2024, 17:37:23] Daniel Adulphus Ypgd: *ANNOUNCEMENT!!!*

With the increasing rate of hackers taking over our WhatsApp account. Its very important we secure our account with these steps 👇

*Enable two-step verification*

1. Open WhatsApp Settings.
2. Tap Account > Two-step verification > Enable.
3. Enter a six-digit PIN of your choice and confirm it.
(This you must always remember)
4. Provide an email address you can access or tap Skip if you don’t want to add an email address. 
We recommend adding an email address as this allows you to reset two-step verification, and help safeguard your account.
5. Tap Next.
6. Confirm the email address and tap Save  or Done.

If you forgot your PIN, you’ll need to wait 7 days before you can reset it. Alternatively, if you’ve previously added your email address, WhatsApp will  send reset instructions to your email. Ensure the email you are using  is accurate and accessible.

[11/03/2024, 09:07:18] Daniel Adulphus Ypgd: Good morning my people,
I believe we already know that our profession has almost always been under threat. 
Let's try as much as possible not to contribute to the denigration of our dear profession. 
Not everything is “content”. We need to know where and when to draw the line. I understand that lately content creation has proven to pay the bills better than our traditional pharmacists roles. 
I saw a video yesterday of a lady accusing a pharmacy (I know why I used the word pharmacy and not pharmacist because I’m not sure if the medication she was recommended to have was done by the pharmacist on duty).
Some months back, there was a trend of our colleagues making jokes on the internet about being “given target”, taking generics instead of branded meds etc…
A good majority of us have found ourselves in community pharmacy practice and understand the workings of up selling, cross selling etc. We also know how sometimes generic medications don't get the job done - we could preach bioequivalence until we're blue in the face. 
Let's also try not to be greedy and impose certain brands on people who can't afford them in a bid to make sales. The country is hard. People are struggling. 
Not everyone who walks into your premises with a symptom must walk out with a medication. There are nonpharma treatments that are tried and tested. That's how you build trust. That customer can and would recommend more people. 
We all know how word of mouth is important for businesses. A customer with a bad experience is worse than a missed sale. 
Some months back, @⁨Isa Muhammad 🐾⁩ did a mini demonstration on how to improve sales with non-medical products. 
I beg us all with all things we hold dear. This profession is all some of us have. Let's not sacrifice our profession on the alter of clout. 
Thank you and happy Monday ❤️

*WORLD GLAUCOMA WEEK/WORLD GLAUCOMA DAY, 2024*


World Glaucoma Day takes place every year on March 12. This year, World Glaucoma Week is March 10–16, 2024.

This year’s theme *“Uniting for a Glaucoma-Free World”* focuses on bringing communities worldwide to fight together against glaucoma blindness. Become involved and be a part of the activities organized over the globe. Help us raise awareness worldwide and learn more about glaucoma.

World Glaucoma Week (WGW) is a global initiative of the World Glaucoma Association (WGA) that puts a spotlight on Glaucoma (a group of eye diseases that damages the optic nerve) as the leading cause of preventable irreversible blindness worldwide. To mark the Week, many Ophthalmologists/Optometrists will be highlighting the importance of early detection in slowing the progression of Glaucoma and that regular eye tests are the only way to detect ‘symptomless’ glaucoma early. At a late stage, glaucoma is irreversible and results in sight loss and blindness. Early detection of glaucoma is key to preventing later sight loss, as is the importance of sight tests to detect possible Glaucoma so that it can be diagnosed by an eye doctor and treated in the community where possible.

Glaucoma is a disease that damages the optic nerve, the part of our eye that carries the images we see to our brain. In the healthy eye, a clear liquid circulates in the front portion of the eye. To maintain a constant healthy eye pressure, the eye continually produces a small amount of this fluid and an equal amount which flows out of the eye. If one have glaucoma, the fluid does not flow properly through the drainage system. Fluid pressure in the eye increases and this extra force presses on the optic nerve in the back of the eye, causing damage to the nerve fibres. Glaucoma is an extremely serious eye disorder which can cause blindness if not managed early.

Glaucoma can affect anyone, but some people have certain risk factors that make them more likely to develop the condition. These risk factors include:
– Having high intraocular pressure (IOP)
– Being 40 years of age or older
– Having a family history of the condition
– Having diabetes
– Having thin central cornea tissue
– Having heart disease or high blood pressure
Different types of glaucoma can also come with additional risk factors, including race/ethnicity, refractive errors, other eye and systemic conditions, long-term steroid use, eye injury and more. Knowing your risk of developing glaucoma is important because there is currently no cure for the disease. One should schedule an annual comprehensive eye exam to get screened for glaucoma and encourage friends and family to do the same.

*WORLD KIDNEY DAY, 2024*


Our kidneys play a silent yet vital role in keeping us healthy. From filtering waste products to balancing our fluids, these bean-shaped organs are unsung heroes in our body. World Kidney Day shines a spotlight on kidney health, urging global awareness and preventive measures against kidney diseases.

World Kidney Day is celebrated annually, *every second Thursday of March*. In 2024, this special day falls on March 14. It’s a day marked by global events, health screenings, and educational campaigns, all focused on kidney health.

This year 2024, World Kidney Day theme is *”Kidney Health for All – Advancing Equitable Access to Care and Optimal Medication Practice”*. This year theme aims to raise awareness of the inequalities in kidney disease treatment and encourage collaborative efforts to improve access to appropriate treatment for everyone affected by kidney disease.


How to Get Involved –

*Health Screenings:* Undergo regular screenings if you’re at risk. Early detection can prevent severe complications.

*Educate and Share:* Learn about the functions of kidneys and share that knowledge with your community. Education is the first step to prevention.

*Adopt a Healthy Lifestyle:* Drink plenty of water, exercise regularly, and maintain a balanced diet to support kidney health.

*Engage on Social Media:* Use the official hashtags to share stories, spread awareness, and encourage others to prioritize their kidney health.

*Support Research:* Contribute to or support organizations that fund kidney disease research. Every bit helps in the fight against kidney-related ailments.

*WHAT AFFECTS THE KIDNEYS NEGATIVELY?*


1) High Blood Pressure (uncontrolled hypertension).

2) Diabetes (uncontrolled blood glucose levels).

3) Smoking (damages blood vessels, leads to slower blood circulation around the body and to the kidneys, also increases risk of cancer for the kidneys).

4) Heart Disease.

5) Obesity (Obesity and Overweight increases risk of other health conditions that can affect kidney health).

6) Dehydration (poor fluid intake; the kidneys need water to function properly and clear out toxins. Kidney stones can also be prevented by adequate water intake).

7) Medications (taken regularly, large amounts of over-the-counter pain medications, like the NSAIDs).

8) Illegal/Illicit drug use including use of anabolic steroids. Also self medication and improper drug use (the use of cocaine, heroin, or methamphetamine (not a good idea for a host of reasons) can cause kidney damage in different ways).

9) Physical Inactivity (Exercise decreases chances of kidney diseases, and also improves blood pressure and cardiovascular health).

10) Excessive Alcohol consumption.

11) Poor diet/nutrition (a healthy diet low in sodium (salt), saturates fats, processed meats and other kidney damaging foods can reduce risk).

12) Poor hygiene encourages development of urinary tract infections, which can affect kidney health.

13) Stress, overtraining (or excessive exercising).

*⚕️PHARMACEUTICAL SOCIETY OF NIGERIA*
*YOUNG PHARMACISTS GROUP*
*EDO STATE CHAPTER*

*MEDIA/PUBLICITY/EDITORIAL COMMITTEE*
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬


It's *WORLD ORAL HEALTH DAY, 2024!*


Enjoy these Oral Health information from a Health Lecture delivered almost a year ago by Dental Therapist Abdul Rekiya Ruth, an ex-corper with the Medical and Health Services CDS Group in Oredo LGA (Edo State).


1) Oral health is the state of the mouth, the teeth and the orofacial structures, that enables individuals to perform essential functions such as eating, breathing and speaking, and encompasses psychosocial dimensions such as self-confidence, well-being and the ability to socialize and work without pain, discomfort and embarrassment.

2) There is no dental condition that happens suddenly. Dental issues usually develops over time. Most oral health conditions are largely preventable and can be treated in their early stages. Most cases are dental caries (tooth decay), periodontal diseases, tooth loss and oral cancers.

3) Oral health is also linked to whole-body health. For example, if an infection is present in one's mouth, the bloodstream can carry the bacteria to other areas of the body, leading to other health concerns like heart disease and stroke. Keeping the teeth and gums healthy is an important part of long-lasting overall health.

4) Some Oral conditions such as gingivitis and periodontitis can contribute to cardiovascular diseases, stroke, endocarditis, pneumonia, and some pregnancy complications. Conversely, health conditions that can have negative impact on the teeth and gums include: Diabetes, Osteoporosis, HIV/AIDS.

5) Signs of poor oral hygiene include: Bleeding gums, Tooth decay, Chronic bad breath, Loose teeth, Gum recession, Mouth sores that don’t go away, Toothache, Swelling of the jaw, Gingivostomatitis (an infection of the mouth caused by certain bacteria or viruses).

6) Continuous high intake of free sugars, inadequate exposure to fluoride and a lack of removal of plaque by toothbrushing can lead to caries, pain and sometimes tooth loss and infection.

7) Most Oral diseases and conditions share modifiable risk factors such as tobacco use (tobacco smoking), alcohol consumption, an unhealthy diet high in free sugars and poor oral hygiene.

8) It is very important to brush twice daily – last thing at night, and after breakfast in the morning. Brushing at night is the most important one. Within the day, the mouth can be rinsed and gaggle with water.

9) Brushing at night helps to prevent the development of dental caries which can develop when the normal bacteria in the mouth feed on the refined carbohydrates and food particles on the teeth, resulting in acid production which gradually destroys the layers of the teeth (the Enamel, Dentine, Pulp).

10) Brushing generally helps to keep the teeth healthy, and to remove dental plaques which can cause tooth decay and gum disease. A fluoride toothpaste should be used. Fluoride is what protects teeth from tooth decay (cavities). It prevents decay by strengthening the tooth’s hard outer surface, called enamel.

11) The right pattern of teeth brushing involves brushing away from the gums and not towards the gums. This prevents damage to the gums in the long run. Brushing the tongue is also very important. Brushing is not aimed to change the colour of one's teeth, but to remove food particles from the teeth.

12) We should brush with a medium texture toothbrush, not a hard or soft toothbrush. Some toothbrushes may be marked as "medium", but may not be really ideal for brushing. Some recommended toothbrushes include: Colgate, Oral-B, Close-up toothbrushes.

13) Cleaning between teeth to remove plaque (flossing) is also part of a good oral hygiene routine. If plaque is not removed, some of it can harden below the gum line and irritate the gums. The gums become red, swollen, and may bleed easily. These are signs of gingivitis. Gingivitis is a mild form of gum disease, and one can usually reverse it with daily brushing and flossing.

14) If plaque stays on the teeth for too long (about 24 hours), it can harden, resulting in the formation of a Calculus or Tartar. The only way to remove tartar is to have the teeth cleaned by a Dentist or Dental hygienist. If tartar is not removed, severe gum disease and teeth issues can develop as the consequences.

15) Bad breath (Halitosis) may occur temporarily in persons who are fasting or who do not talk for long hours. If one doesn't brush the tongue while brushing, it can result to this as well.

16) It is advisable not to use toothpicks. Dental floss is more healthy and advised. One should change toothbrush every 3 months, or before 3 months (even after a month) if the bristles of the toothbrush is scattered.

17) The Tips to improve Oral hygiene include: 1) Proper and regular brushing, 2) Daily flossing, 3) Eating well balanced diet and limiting sugars and sweets, 4) Avoiding Smoking and use of herbs which stains the teeth, 5) Avoiding the use of the teeth in opening bottle drinks and chewing very hard bones and other substances..

18) The Tips to improve Oral hygiene include: 6) Dental checkups should be done by a woman intending to get pregnant and before the pregnancy. During pregnancy, it is especially important to practice good oral hygiene to maintain the health of the gums, 7) Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers should avoid the use of antibiotics (especially tetracycline) except in life threatening conditions because excessive use of antibiotics discoloure the baby's teeth. The baby's teeth usually starts developing at about 5–6 months of pregnancy, and are usually buried inside the gums..

19) The Tips to improve Oral hygiene include: 8) Habits that mothers should discourage when noticed in their children include: thumb sucking, lip sucking, nail biting, tongue thrusting, bruxism, prolonged use of pacifiers, etcetera. Prolonged practices of these habits causes malocclusion, 9) Mothers should take care of their baby's teeth with either a soft toothbrush or a clean wet cotton cloth if the use of toothbrush is not conveniently at the early stage.

20) One should visit the dental clinic for routine dental check ups, if one is at a higher risk for tooth decay (for example, if one have a dry mouth because of medicines been taken and if one is at a higher risk for gum disease because of a medical condition (for example, diabetes).

21) It is important to maintain a child's dentition. In some children, the primary teeth is already out by 4–6 months. The primary teeth is very important as it helps the permanent teeth, and also controls the dentition (teeth arrangement). A tiled floor may be dangerous for infants/children as they can damage their teeth/jaw bones in the instance of an accident.

22) Fluoride toothpastes for Adults have higher fluoride concentrations than those of children. That's why there are toothpastes which are marked for children and could have age ranges. Too much fluoride is unhealthy for the teeth, and causes fluorosis.

23) Diastema (gap teeth) is an abnormality in Dentistry. Artificial dentition can be achieved using Dentures, Crowns and Implants. Braces are used to correct malocclusion.

24) The advantages of Good Oral hygiene are: 1) healthier teeth and gums, 2) a beautiful smile, 3) a fresher breath, 4) a reduced need for dental work such as fillings, crowns, bridges, implants or dentures, 5) a lowered risk of heart disease, stroke, diabetes and other health concerns, 7) a reduced risk of oral cancer.

25) Normally, everyone is expected to visit the Dental Clinic every 6 months for routine Dental checks, and for a scaling and polishing procedure if that is required. Scaling removes plaques, calculus, stains. It doesn't not change the teeth colour.

26) Not everyone has normal white teeth colour. In some persons without white teeth colour, it is normal. Teeth Whitening is a cosmetic procedure, that is specific to whiten the teeth's colour. It is much more expensive than Scaling and Polishing.

27) Preventative dental care is more affordable than restorative or emergency dental care. So, Good Oral hygiene can save time, worry and money in the long run.

*WORLD DOWN SYNDROME DAY, 2024*


*World Down Syndrome Day (WDSD)*, 21 March, is a global awareness day which has been officially observed by the United Nations since 2012. The date for WDSD being the 21st day of the 3rd month of the year, was selected to signify the uniqueness of the triplication (trisomy) of the 21st chromosome which causes Down syndrome.

*Down Syndrome (or Trisomy 21)* is a genetic condition that causes mild to significant physical and developmental problems. It is a condition in which a person has an extra chromosome. Chromosomes are “packages” of genes in the body. They determine how a baby’s body forms and functions as it grows. Around 1 in every 800 babies will be born with Down syndrome. Down syndrome occurs naturally – there is no known cause. Down syndrome usually causes varying degrees of intellectual and physical disability and associated medical issues. Down syndrome is named after John Langdon Down, an English doctor who was the first person to publish an accurate description of the condition in the 1860s.

Around the world, people with Down Syndrome are treated in a negative way – denied quality education, good healthcare, job opportunities, not allowed to make decisions about their own lives, and their voices are not heard. This day is to create a single global voice advocating for the rights, inclusion and well being of people with Down syndrome.

*Down Syndrome vs Autism*

Down syndrome – Genetic disorder, usually with physical traits. They are often social and friendly. Their language development is similar to that of more typical children.

Autism – Neurological disorder (dysfunction in the brain and nervous system) with no physical characteristics. They often prefer to be alone and not socialize. Their language skills might be delayed or not develop.

The similarities between both Down Syndrome and Autism are: they prefer routine, have developmental delays, avoid eye contact, enjoy repetitive play, show challenging behaviors (trouble managing feelings when frustrated, lack of impulse control, etcetera).

This is for football⚽ lovers! Have you ever wondered how the FIFA/Coca-cola World Rankings (FWR) is calculated? It's actually mathematical. The note below will explain it. At the end, you can calculate the points yourself😃


The *FIFA World Rankings* usually gets updated regularly. Nigeria who was number 42 (1474.44 points) before the 2023 AFCON, moved 14 places upwards to number 28 (1522.26 points). Have you ever wondered how the Rankings is calculated? Today, we share briefly on it.

The current model of the FWR, called the *SUM*, took effect in August 2018 after approval by the FIFA Council.

In this model, less importance to friendly matches and more importance to final round competitions, such as the FIFA World Cup Finals is given. More importance to knock-out stage matches than group stage matches in final competitionsis also given. Also, losses in knock-out rounds of final competitions are excluded from the calculation.


The formula for the SUM algorithm is as follows:
*P = Pbefore + I * (W – We)*

Where:
*Pbefore* is points before the match;
*I* is importance of the match;
*W* is result of the match;
*We* is expected result of the match.

The result of the match (*W*) can either be a win (1), a draw (0.5), or a defeat (0).

The expected result of the match (*We*), is computed with this formula:

*We* = 1/(10^(-dr/600) + 1)

Where dr= difference in ratings of the two playing teams, i.e. dr = [Pbefore of Team A – Pbefore of Team B]

The Importance of the match (*I*) has these points values:

I= 05 for friendly matches played outside of Int'l Match Calendar windows
I= 10 for friendly matches played during Int'l Match Calendar windows
I= 15 for Group phase matches of Nations League competitions
I= 25 for Play-off and final matches of Nations League competitions
I= 25 for Qualification matches for Confederations and FIFA World Cup final competitions
I= 35 for Confederation final competition matches up until the QF stage 
I= 40 for Confederation final competition matches from the QF stage onwards; all FIFA Confederations Cup matches
I= 50 for FIFA World Cup final competition matches up until QF stage 
I= 60 for FIFA World Cup final competition matches from QF stage onwards


Let's take this example.

Team A has 1300 points before the match and wins a continental qualifier against Team B that has 1500 points.

For Team A, the formula is:
P = 1300 + 25 * (1 – *We*)
*We* = 1/(10 exp (–(1300–1500)/600) +1) = 0.3172
P = 1300 + [25 × 0.6828]
P = *1317.07 points*

For Team B, the formula is:
P = 1500 + 25 * (0 – *We*)
*We* = 1/(10 exp (–(1500–1300)/600) +1) = 0.6828
P = 1500 + [25 × –0.6828]
P = *1482.93 points*

Team A gains 17 points, while Team B loses the same amount of points after the match.

Now, you can calculate Nigeria's FWR points after their next game😃


There are a few *additional conditions* included within the new SUM formula to address specific issues in International football.

• Matches decided in a penalty shootout (PSO) are treated as a draw for the losing team (W = 0.5) and as "half a win" for the winning team (W = 0.75).

• Teams that earn negative points in the knock-out round of a final competition (e.g. as a result of losing, or even winning after PSO against a weaker team) do not lose any points:

If (W – We) < 0, then P = Pbefore

This condition was introduced in order to protect the point totals of teams that have progressed to the knock-out round.

This may explain why Senegal didn't drop lower, but rather gained 3 places on the FWR despite exiting the AFCON tournament at the R16 stage.


You've learnt something unique, right?

[22/03/2024, 13:14:31] David Ypg Edo PRO: World Water Day is an annual United Nations (UN) observance day held on 22 March that highlights the importance of fresh water. The day is used to advocate for the sustainable management of freshwater resources. The theme of each year focuses on topics relevant to clean water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), which is in line with the targets of Sustainable Development Goal.

A well managed water cycle underpins progress across the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, particularly in relation to hunger, gender equity, health, education, livelihoods, sustainability and ecosystems.

Water is also at the heart of adaptation to climate change, serving as the crucial link between the climate system, human society and the environment.

World Water Day 2024 focuses on the theme, *‘Leveraging Water for Peace’*.
