‎[02/07/2024, 18:48:30] Sir Prof  Pharm Abu Dantani John: ACPN NATIONAL CHAIRMANSHIP ELECTION 2024 - WHOM THE CAP FITS
Community pharmacy is and remains the face of the Pharmacy profession in Nigeria and even globally. It is not just the aspect of Pharmacy that accommodates all Pharmacists irrespective of their primary area of practice, it also offers a bigger prospect of employment, opportunities, prosperity, fulfillment, value, relevance and indispensability to Pharmacists (and even prospective pharmacists) across board. It is also the area of Pharmacy which largely validates the Pharmacist as a health care practitioner or a care provider.
Sadly, Community Pharmacists have largely been unable to take a chunk of the bounty of wealth that lies there in their practice even though they are supposedly the frontliners. The problem of interlopers, professional shortchanges, poor policy implementation, internal sabotage and several other issues continue to press down the community Pharmacist making them be like strangers in their own turf. ‎image omitted

TO: *PHARMACEUTICAL SOCIETY OF NIGERIA (PSN), Edo State.* 

*Appreciation Message to the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN), Edo State Chapter.*

On behalf of the Pharmaceutical Association of Nigerian Students (PANS) Uniben Chapter, we extend our heartfelt gratitude to PSN Edo State for the generous provision of solar lights in our lecture theatres.
 This thoughtful initiative will significantly enhance our study environment, enabling us to read and prepare for our examinations more effectively, even at night.

Your unwavering support and commitment to improving the educational experience of pharmacy students in University of Benin are deeply appreciated. The installation of these solar lights is a testament of your dedication to fostering a conducive learning atmosphere, promoting academic excellence, and ensuring the well-being of future pharmacists.

We are excited about the positive impact this will have on our studies and overall academic performance in this time of distress of electricity supply on campus. Your investment in our education not only empowers us to achieve our academic goals but also inspires us to contribute meaningfully to the pharmacy profession.

The solar lights have been installed and attached to this message are pictures and videos of the already installed lights in the lecture theatres.

 We are indeed grateful for this generous contribution to the growth and success of PANS UNIBEN.
As we look forward to more collaborations and initiatives aimed at uplifting the standards of pharmacy education in Nigeria, we want to express our sincere appreciation once again.

 Thank you for your continuous support and for believing in the potential of Uniben pharmacy students.

Yours-in-service

*CLARA IKEBOH*

*Do you know that* ADHD affects 5% of children and 2.5% of adults worldwide, its incidence reports to be 7.6% in children aged 3-12 years and 5.6% in teenagers aged 12-18 years...🤔

This statistics shows the prevalence of ADHD in our world today, and the increasing demand to know about this medical condition, so we can know how best to care for our children...

We are glad to announce that PSN-YPG 'Pharmacist of the Week (POTW)' is back! 

It's our little way of acknowledging Excellence, rewarding innovative ideas and encouraging young pharmacists who are contributing enormously to the growth of other young pharmacists and to our Association at large.
POTW holds every Tuesday and will be publicized across all PSN-YPG social media platforms(Instagram, Linkedin, Facebook, Telegram and Twitter)

This week, we are excited to shine the starlight on Pharm. Rukevwe Amos Oghenejakpor(R.A.O)  the Co-founder of Pharmacist In Tech(PIT) Africa which is a platform that has served to educate young pharmacists on #health skills, #tech skills and #digital skills.

His dedication towards the upskilling of pharmacy professionals and mentorship of young pharmacists has earned him several awards and international recognitions and that is why he is our young Pharmacist of the week.

Congratulations Pharm Rukevwe Amos Oghenejakpor(R.A.O) 🎉

John, the beloved apostle said in his gospel, that the light came into the world but unfortunately, humans loved darkness rather than light. They chose darkness over light for various reasons. But is there really any justifiable reason to choose darkness over light?

Come 26th July, 2024, CPs across the country will be at the AGM in Ibadan to choose the next leadership of ACPN National. Of those jostling for the seat of the National Chairman, one man has verifiable antecedents. Of all the agendas released so far, his is the only one that speaks to the challenges CPs are facing now. Of them all, he is the only one who is not making generic promises but talking of specific deliverables. Among the pack, he stands head and shoulder above all! The difference between him and others in terms of antecedents, capacity and clarity and relevance of vision is the difference between darkness and light.

As someone who has worked with each of the candidates at different times and in various capacities, I can say without any fear of equivocation that each is experienced, loyal and has served the profession at different levels of engagement over the years. Hence, these should not be the talking points of this campaign as I have seen some emphasising. We should be looking now at capacity to tackle the challenges bedevilling CPs at this time in our journey; antecedents; intelligence and energy. While it is obvious that some possess one or two of these attributes in some measures *I can say that only one candidate possess all of these attributes in sufficient measures to address the collective challenges of CPs at this time and set us on the trajectory for prosperity.* 

May it not be said of CPs that for whatever reasons, they chose darkness rather light! Colleagues, the choice for the next National Chairman of ACPN is clear. That choice is Pharm. Duke Otite, MAW, DCPharm!

*Never* used an emoji in communicating on WhatsApp or other social media platforms?

*WORLD EMOJI DAY* is celebrated annually (since 2014) on July 17

It’s a fun and lighthearted occasion to recognize how emojis enrich communication by adding colour and universality across languages and cultures.

The word emoji comes from the Japanese: 絵 (“e,” picture), 文 (“mo,” write) and 字 (“ji,” character). 
*e* (絵) refers to *picture*
*mo* (文) refers to *write*
*ji* (字) refers to *character*
An Emoji is therefore to write picture character.

Emojis are small digital icons used to express emotions and ideas in texts and on social media. They convey emotions and ideas succinctly and have become integral to digital interactions.

Emojis were invented in 1997 by *Shigetaka Kurita,* a Japanese designer, who created 176 different emojis representing various objects, expressions, and weather conditions for an online messaging service. These icons quickly gained popularity in Japan, adding emotional depth and expressiveness to digital messages. From text messages to social media, emojis add a layer of emotion and clarity that words alone often cannot achieve. Billions of emojis are exchanged daily, illustrating their universal appeal and versatility.

Over time, emojis have evolved to become more diverse and inclusive. Modern emojis offer various skin tones, genders, and a wide range of professions, activities, and objects. This inclusivity allows more people to see themselves represented in digital communication. The Unicode Consortium regularly updates the emoji library, continually expanding the range of available icons.

You can join the 2024 celebration by any of the following fun ways:

1) Emoji Conversations: Challenge yourself to have a conversation with your friends and loved ones using only emojis.

2) Emoji Design: Get creative and design your own emoji.

3) Wear Emojis: Wear clothes or accessories featuring your favorite emojis.

More@ https://www.journee-mondiale.com/en/day/world-emoji-day/

Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Liverpool and AS Roma competes the top 5.

The club coefficients are based on the results of clubs competing in the *five previous seasons* of the UCL, UEL and UECL. A club's five-season coefficient is the cumulative total of the previous five seasons' coefficients.

The rankings determine the seeding of each club in relevant UEFA competition draws. Example, if the top 8 are involved in the UCL (using the former format), they would be seeded in Pot 1 and will each be in the 8 different groups.

‎[22/07/2024, 08:38:15] ~ Dr. Favvy☺️: *COLIC IN BABIES: CAUSES, SYMPTOMS AND TREATMENT* 

It is a normal phenomenon when babies do cry. Still, when a healthy baby cries inconsolably and excessively for no apparent reason, pediatricians might suspect colic, which can start just as early as 2-3 weeks after birth.

Using the ‘rule of three’ description, babies who cry for more than 3 hours a day at least 3 days per week for more than 3 weeks might have colic. Sometimes, there’s nothing that can be done to ease a baby’s cries as a parent.

It's pertinent to know that colic is very common, with research suggesting it affects approximately 20% of babies worldwide.

*Learn more...👇*

*INTERNATIONAL SELF-CARE DAY, 2024*


Every year on July 24th, International Self Care Day promotes self-care as a vital foundation of health. It’s also a day for people around the world to prioritize self-care and make it a part of their lifestyle.

Self-care is any action that an individual takes to look after their own health, based on the knowledge and information available to them. This practice can also occur in collaboration with healthcare professionals when needed. Actively managing your own health and well-being through self-care has numerous benefits, including better choice between healthcare options, better care for individual wellbeing and better value for governments and health systems worldwide.

When you take care of yourself to stay well, you are practicing self-care. Staying well includes taking care of your whole self: physically, mentally, and emotionally. For some, self-care also includes taking care of themselves spiritually. Examples of self-care include: having a regular sleep routine, maintaining a healthy weight, keeping a reflective journal, practicing gratitude, getting a massage, listening to relaxing music, reading a good book, learning to say no, asking for help when necessary, etcetera.

1. Last Friday (July 19), the 2024 *League Bloggers Award* held in Lagos State. Enyimba of Aba star, *Chijioke Mbaoma* was awarded the 2023/24 NPFL Player of the Season award. He finished as NPFL's top scorer (17 goals). Akwa United's *Sani Suleiman* won the Rookie of the Season award. He impressed for his club, contributing 11 goals and 2 assists in 19 apps. *Fidelis Ilechukwu*, who coached Enugu Rangers to the 2023/24 NPFL title, was awarded the Coach of the Season award. *Emem Essien* of *Edo Queens* was awarded the NWFL (Women's) Player of the Season, while Edo Queen's coach, *Moses Adiku*, was awarded the NWFL Coach of the Season award. *Amas Obasogie*, the goalkeeper of *Bendel Insurance* of Edo State, was awarded the 2023/24 Goalkeeper of the Season award. In total, about 18 awards were given that night.

2. The *2024 Paris Olympic Tournament* is currently ongoing. In football, *Nigeria Women* kicked off their games yesterday vs Brazil. They lost (1–0) to Brazil. They will play Spain (on Sunday) and Japan (on Wednesday) to conclude the group stage. If they finish top 2 in Group C, they will progress to the knockout stages.

3. Here is an inspirational story of *Nico Williams* (Spain's attacking winger in the Euros) and his family. Iñaki & Nico's parents - María and Felix, travelled from Ghana in search of a better future. They used their life savings to pay a human trafficking gang to take them to the UK, but they left them stranded halfway. They had to walk the entire Sahara desert without shoes. María was pregnant with Iñaki. Many of them passed away and were buried along the way, but they kept walking. They were arrested in Melilla (Spanish colony) and a lawyer told them to lie and say they had come from a war affected country, Liberia. They were introduced to a priest who helped them get the documents to stay in Spain, and found them work too. Iñaki was born soon after. The family moved to Pamplona (in the nearby Navarra) and that is when Nico was born. Both brothers only found out about their parents' journey when they became adults. Both brothers won the 2024 Copa Del Rey Trophy together with Athletic Club. FC Barcelona is about to sign Nico Williams.

4. Earlier this week, *Real Madrid* football club became the first to surpass *€1 billion* in revenue. Their revenue increased by 27% more than the previous season.

5. In less than a month time, most of the European leagues will be resuming for the *2024/25 season*. The dates of resumption of the La Liga, EPL, Ligue 1, Serie A, and Bundesliga are: 15th, 16th, 16th, 17th, and 23rd of August, respectively.

6. In the history of football – 471 players have won the FIFA World Cup. 80 players have won both the FIFA World Cup and the UEFA Champions League. 9 players have won the FIFA World Cup, UEFA Champions League, and the Ballon d'Or. Only 2 players (Lionel Messi and Gerd Müller) have won the FIFA World Cup, UEFA Champions League, Ballon d'Or, and Golden Boot. However, only *Lionel Messi* have won all plus the FIFA World Cup Golden Ball.

[26/07/2024, 12:57:07] Wellington: DRIVING  GUIDE ON THE NEWLY DESIGNED KADA ROUTE

Please adhere to the following driving rules to avoid being apprehended;

1. Coming from sapele road wheeling to 3rd east circular road has no traffic light signal, as it is free drive - way.

2. Coming from sapele road heading ring road? do not enter the small lane as it is basically for those motorist going to ikpokkpan.


3. When heading to Ikpokpan from sapele road, use the small lane to ur left and wait for the traffic light signal 

4. Coming from sapele road and u wanna make a U-TURN? Also use the small lane to ur left and watch the signal carefully. Do not enter the major lane leading to ring road if u wanna wheel to ikpokpan or make a U-TURN back to sapele road.

5. It is very important to note that there is a stop line at the kada axis now hence note the following, 
(a)   STOP at the STOP line wen the traffic shows the  ambar light to avoid being apprehended.

(b)   DO NOT encroach  the STOP LINE/ ZEBRA crossing for any reason  whsn waiting for the traffic light to turn green as it's an infringement on the right of pedestrians 

6. Coming from ring road, the lane leading to ikpokpan is a free lane (emergency lane) hence, u shouldn't obstruct it for any reason. However it has no traffic light signal.

7. Be mindful of the road markings and ensure to comply to the sign - arrows  or traffic information appropriately. 

8. You wanna wheel to your left (3rd east circular road) or make a U-TURN back to ring road when coming frm ring road axis? enter the small lane to your left and observe ths traffic light signal.

9. Always stop when  pedestrians are crossing through the zebra crossing.

10. Mind your lanes when driving or waiting for traffic signal as there is a traffic offence called "lane hopping" etc...

‎[28/07/2024, 08:06:23] Bernard Tsz Ypgd: *THE ROLE OF PHARMACISTS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF HEPATITIS* 

📌 *By working as part of the multidisciplinary health care team , Pharmacists have a critical role in the prevention, screening and management of hepatitis* 

📍 *Patient information and education* 
•	 Educational activities aimed at increasing public and 
individual awareness on the transmission mechanism 
of hepatitis A, B ,C D and E how to prevent their infection.
•	 Provision of educational material on the different types of  hepatitis and 
visible posters in the pharmacy encouraging patients to 
ask for medical advice about their health problems.

📍 *Vaccine supply* 
Provision of vaccination service including vaccines against the different types of
hepatitis and other vaccines that may be necessaryin patients with chronic liver disease.

📍 *Harm reduction services* 
Key services to prevent sexually transmitted infections 
in at-risk population groups such as injecting drug users

📍 *Hepatitis screening* 
Provision of rapid Hepatitis tests followed by a counselling or 
referral to a physician process depending on the test result.

📍 *Administrative support* 
Collecting information on the patient’s baseline clinical 
parameters (laboratory results, clinical 
notes made by the medical staff) and sociodemographic 
data to complete pre-authorization records required by 
insurance companies, the health system or health care providers.

📍 *Procurement and distribution of drugs* 
Besides the usual medication procurement and dispensing 
process, pharmacists can identify patients at risk of nonadherence based on their medication refill history. They 
can also ensure that patients get their prescribed medications on time.

📍 *Drug dispensing* 
The drug dispensing process may be carried out during the 
follow-up consultation with the pharmacist by arranging with 
the patient whether the medications will be dispensed at the 
nearest pharmacy and ensures adequate follow- up

📍 *Pharmacovigilance*  Pharmacists provide interventions 
such as monitoring, dose reduction, change or prescription 
of medications, and recommendation of non-pharmacological measures for symptomatic management, to avoid early 
treatment discontinuation or lack of patient adherence.
Pharmacists conduct this review usually during follow-up 
visits or at the time of dispensing the drugs, when patients 
are asked about the adverse effects commonly associated 
with antiviral treatment, and lab tests are reviewed to monitor the occurrence of adverse drug reactions. Then, any 
detected reaction is reported to pharmacovigilance systems 
with complete information of the drug.

📍 *Research* This item includes taking part in the development of clinical trials on novel therapies and writing research articles on 
the use of antiviral drugs in different patient populations. 
Pharmacists may actively collaborate with other health care 
providers in several types of research, such as efficacy and 
safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacoeconomics studies.

📍 *Other support services* (Development of information and 
clinical decision support systems, Support and activities during the 
transition of patients from one level of 
care to another , Support Group, Sending motivational letters and 
emails, Provision of training to health 
professionals)

*WORLD HEPATITIS DAY, 2024*


World Hepatitis Day, observed on 28 July, raises awareness of viral hepatitis, an inflammation of the liver that causes severe liver disease and cancer.

This year’s theme is: *It’s time for action*. With a person dying every 30 seconds from a hepatitis-related illness, we must accelerate action on better prevention, diagnosis, and treatment to save lives and improve health outcomes.

There are 5 main strains of the hepatitis virus – A, B, C, D, and E. Together, hepatitis B and C are the most common infections and result in 1.3 million deaths and 2.2 million new infections per year.

Despite better tools for diagnosis and treatment, and decreasing product prices, testing and treatment coverage rates have stalled. But, reaching the WHO elimination goal by 2030 should still be achievable, if swift action is taken now.

Hepatitis prevention can be achieved through – vaccination, avoiding unprotected sex, using condoms and discarding properly, not sharing sharp objects, practicing good personal hygiene such as proper hand washing with soap and clean water, never using an infected person's personal items, applying all necessary precautions when getting a tattoo or any body piercings, drinking well packaged water especially when travelling, and taking strict precautionary measures when travelling to an endemic area.

*"HEPATITIS CAN'T WAIT!"*

Today marks *World Hepatitis Day*. A global Campaign aimed at combating the devastating impact of viral hepatitis. *Hepatitis* is a leading causative agent of a number of ailment such as *Liver Cancer, Cirrhosis,* and *Liver failure* to mention a few, affecting over 350 million people worldwide.

*The Burden of Hepatitis:*
- 1 in 10 people worldwide live with viral hepatitis,
- 1.34 million deaths annually, surpassing HIV/AIDS and malaria combined,
- 90% of people unaware of their infection,
- Hepatitis B and C are the main causes of liver Cancer, and so on.
Walk with ADMAP/PH as we expose the burden of Hepatitis.

[28/07/2024, 16:37:43] Pharm Dr Allen Iboi: VICTORY IN SOLIDARITY - a tale of OLUYOLE 2024.

My dear Colleagues, 

I write to express my heartfelt gratitude to the Edo ACPN family, the Edo PSN and Indeed all the Pharmacists and non Pharmacists within and outside of Edo State who were part of the Project Duke Otite, for your immense contributions towards our collective aspiration to emancipate community pharmacy practice in Nigeria - a vision championed by Pharmacist Duke Otite which was tested at the polls in the just concluded ACPN National Conference in Ibadan.

Unfortunately, we could not achieve our target at this time. However, there is no loss because we made a strong statement.

We showed great solidarity
We showed desire
We fought gallantly
and despite the manipulations and gimmick from the establishments, the people showed belief in our message of emancipation and the desire to align as displayed by the bold, courageous and impressive 273 votes garnered by our principal. In the end it came down to tiny details.

If we had turned up as we solicited we would have been home and dry but then we have a great momentum to build on.

We will not give up until we achieve our dream of a liberated and prosperous Community Pharmacy Practice in Nigeria. 

So let us brace up and re-strategize to Go Again and take it one step better.

Special thanks to the 97 delegates from Edo State who queued behind me to be counted. You are the real heroes.

*METHODIST BOYS HIGH SCHOOL ORON*
_Nigeria's Oldest High School?_

Being close to the sea means Akwa Ibom was a landing site for early merchants and missionaries to Nigeria.  Methodist Boys High School Oron was established by missionaries in *1897*, same year Benin was invaded. However, due to clashes with colonialists, the school had to be moved and reestablished in 1905 at Oron.

The school has produced many outstanding citizens like Senator Bassey Ewa-Henshaw etc.

Please, when was your school established? If it wasn't before 1897, you have no reason not to be in Uyo!

[30/07/2024, 23:28:11] David Ypg Edo PRO: *Protest: PSN urges dialogue amidst national hardship.*

The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has called for a cautious approach to the ongoing calls for protests amidst the prevailing economic hardship in the country.

The PSN expressed concerns over the potential for violence and further economic setbacks if protests escalate while acknowledging the legitimate grievances of Nigerians, the PSN emphasised the need for constructive dialogue between the government and citizens.

The President of the PSN, Pharm. Prof. Cyril Usifoh, who spoke in Lagos, said Nigeria is paying for defective planning of over 60 years of nationhood which has manifested in hardship like never before within the short life of the incumbent administration.

Usifoh further proposed a roadmap for reform, including youth inclusion in governance, constitutional amendments, and a reduction in government spending.

“In the face of the abundance of mischief in high places, the calls for protests are justifiable especially because conventional propriety in a democracy allows the people to exercise liberties provided for in the constitution,” he said.

Usifoh said: “Moving forward, the PSN calls for reconsideration rather than a protest that can be vulnerable to becoming a consuming evil of unimaginable destructive magnitude based on the listed conditionalities as the way forward.

He said there was a need to promote rules of engagement in constructive dialogue with the Government and Representatives of the people to benchmark the attainment of meaningful reforms for the Nigerian people.

“Establishing wide-based consultations which reposition the youths such that their voices or desires are accommodated in our change agenda and Government at all levels must consciously cut unnecessary expenses.

“We must pave the way for a collective bargaining template for agitators and other patriots to negotiate with the Government at the highest level.

“There must be conscious efforts to discourage the activities of political influencers. This becomes important in the quest to balance an ardent need for stability and public safety.”

He said there was also the need to draw lines in political activism because the Nigerian political leadership epitomises polyandry, adding that all the major political parties are married to the same unproductive political system.

Usifoh criticised the current leadership for insensitivity and mismanagement of the economy, citing examples of extravagant spending by public officials while the majority of Nigerians grapple with poverty.

“Insensitivity and high-handedness characterise the attitude of the leadership with NASS members improving on the impunity of their predecessors with state-of-the-art SUVs which cost an average of N200 million while also not disguising their posh and luxurious living to the chagrin of a poverty-stricken followership.”He also called for an end to the influence of political godfathers and the adoption of a more inclusive political system.

The PSN proposed a framework for negotiations between the government and various stakeholders, including agitators, to address the nation’s challenges. The organisation warned against the dangers of allowing protests to degenerate into violence and property destruction, urging protesters to maintain peace and order.

The PSN further advocated for a transformative agenda that would address the root causes of the nation’s problems.

The organisation expressed hope that the current situation would catalyze positive change and a new era of good governance in Nigeria.

Usifoh said: “Nigerians especially the more vulnerable who live below the poverty level should begin to resist the tendency to be used for selfish political gains against national interest.”

INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL ADVERTISEMENT
VACANCY
Application is hereby invited from suitably qualified candidates for the underlisted positions in University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital, Ilorin, Kwara State. 
1.	INTERN PHYSIOTHERAPIST
Candidates must possess a degree in Physiotherapy.
Must have registered with the Medical Rehabilitation Therapists Registration Board of Nigeria.
		SALARY: CONHESS 08 Step 2 (N1,670,384.00 P.A)

2.		INTERN PHARMACIST
Candidates must possess a degree in Pharmacy.
Must have registered with the Pharmacist Council of Nigeria (PCN).
		SALARY: CONHESS 08 Step 2 (N1,670,384.00 P.A)


3.	INTERN MEDICAL LABORATORY SCIENTIST
Candidates must possess a degree in Medical Laboratory Science.
Must have registered with the Institute of Medical Laboratory Science of Nigeria.
		SALARY: CONHESS 08 Step 2 (N1,670,384.00 P.A)

4.	INTERN IMAGING SCIENTIST
Candidates must possess a Degree in Radiography
Must have registered with the Radiographers Registration of Nigeria (RRBN)
		SALARY: CONHESS 08 Step 2 (N1,670,384.00 P.A)

5.		INTERN OPTOMETRIST
Candidates must possess a Degree in Optometrist
Must have registered with the General Optical Council (GOC)
SALARY: CONHESS 08 Step 2 (N1,670,384.00 P.A)

6.		INTERN NURSE
Candidates must possess a Degree in Bachelor of Nursing Services
Must have registered with Nursing Council of Nigeria
SALARY: CONHESS 08 Step 2 (N1,670,384.00 P.A)

OTHER CONDITION OF SERVICE:
As obtained in other teaching Hospitals in the Federation.

METHOD OF APPLICATION
The Application forms are to be downloaded from the University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital website (www.uithilorin.org.ng) pay five thousand naira (N5,000.00) non-refundable fee into University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital Account with the CBN through CBN e-payment gateway REMITA.

SUBMISSION /CLOSING DATE
Duly completed application forms in which all photocopies of credentials and passport photograph must be attached, should be forwarded submitted to: 
The Chief Medical Director
University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital
P. M. B. 1459
Ilorin
Not later than six (6) weeks from the date of this advertisement.

*Sports Update*⚽🏀🧘🏻‍♂️🏊🏻‍♀️♟️🏆
_Sports Information from the Week_
02.08.2024


1. 🏊🏻‍♀️ Who is the most successful and most decorated Olympian (Olympic athlete) of all time? 39 years old *Michael Phelps*, an American former competitive swimmer with a total of *28 medals*! Phelps also holds the all-time records for Olympic gold medals (23), Olympic gold medals in individual events (13), and Olympic medals in individual events (16).

2. ⚽ Last Saturday, *Canada’s Olympic Women’s football team* were deducted 6 points and their coach, *Beverly Priestman*, along with 2 other officials, suspended for a year after using a drone to spy on a rival team private training session. Canada was also fined 200,000 swiss francs, and have also decided to cut off fundings for the suspended officials for the 1 year duration. They broke FIFA's regulation on the prohibition of flying drones over any training sites. This placed Canada in a tight spot to qualify. Canada won all 3 group stage games, finished on 3 points after the 6 points deduction, and *still qualified as runner-up* in the group!

3. 🏀 No African Nation had won a game in the Olympic Men's Basketball since 1996. Guess what? *South Sudan* broke that record in their first ever Olympic game appearance. They defeated Puerto Rico 90–79 in their game last Sunday.

4. 🥊 Last Sunday, Nigerian boxer, *Cynthia Ogunsemilore*, was removed from the Paris Olympics Women's tournament after testing positive for a banned doping substance. The 22-year-old African Games lightweight champion tested positive for the diuretic furosemide in a sample taken last Friday. Furosemide is a masking agent that can hide the presence of other drugs. Ogunsemilore is provisionally suspended and cannot take part in the Olympics. This is the second positive doping test announced at the Paris Olympics, after Iraqi Judoka Sajjad Sehen tested positive for two anabolic steroids. Another Olympian also tested positive for furosemide.

5. 🏓 Earlier this week, a Nigerian table tennis player, Offiong Edem, advised Nigerians to offer more support and not criticisms to athletes representing the country at the ongoing Paris Olympic Games, following the exits of *Quadri Aruna* and *Omotayo Olajide* in the men’s singles on Saturday. Nigeria had a bad start in the table tennis event with both Aruna and Olajide, crashing out after just one game each. While Olajide’s 4–1 defeat to Iran’s Noshad Alamiyan didn’t come as a surprise, Aruna’s ouster was shocking as the African champion threw away a three-set lead and lost 4-3 to Romania’s Eduard Ionescu.

6. 🏀 On Monday, *Nigeria's female Basketball Team* pulled off a famous shock win against Australia as they won 75–62 in their opening game of the Women's Olympic Basketball Tournament. It was a sensational performance as they capitalized on Australian turnovers to take victory in front of another huge crowd in Lille. The game was described as the biggest upset of the Olympics on Monday, as Australia Women are a heavyweight in Basketball.

7. 🏃🏻‍♀️ Nigerian sprinter, *Favour Ofili*, expressed her frustration on Tuesday, revealing that she will not compete in the 100-metre race at the ongoing Paris Olympics due to administrative failures by the Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN) and the Nigerian Olympic Committee (NOC). Her post read: “It is with great regret that I have just been told I will not be competing in the 100 metres at this Olympic Games. I qualified, but those with the AFN and NOC failed to enter me. I have worked for four years to earn this opportunity. For what? Please remember, in the last Olympic Games (2020), I was not able to compete because AFN, NADC and NOC failed to release funds for athletes to be tested, which made 14 Nigerian athletes that qualified to not compete. Now this.. If those responsible are not held accountable for taking this opportunity from me, neither organisation can ever be trusted in the future! Next one is the 200 metres. I hope I’m entered.”

8. ⚽ In a new development last weekend, it was reported that *Beyond Limits*, one of the football clubs that got promoted to the NPFL from the NNL, have sold their spot to *Heartland FC* (for 350 million naira), who got relegated to the NNL from the NPFL in the just concluded 2023/24 season. It is said that both Beyond Limits and Remo Stars (who is already in the NPFL) have the same Owner, and according to the regulations, 2 or more clubs with the same owner isn't allowed in the NPFL. Some persons are of the opinion that the NPFL would have passed on the spot to the next qualified team rather than allowing Beyond Limits sell their spot.

9. 🇳🇬 On Wednesday, 46-year old *Eric Chelle*, the former coach of Mali, emerged the new coach of *Nigeria's Super Eagles*.

10. ⚽ *Nigeria’s Super Falcons* on Wednesday, suffered a 3–1 defeat to Japan in their final group match to crash out of the Women’s football event at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris. The team needed victory with a two-goal margin to advance from Group B. The loss implies that the Super Falcons lost all 3 group stage games in the Olympics.

10. ⚽ The maiden edition of *Bright Osayi-Samuel male U-13 Football competition* kicked-off in Benin City, Edo State yesterday (August 1). It is sponsored by Fenebache and Super Eagles defender, Bright Osayi-Samuel and family, in conjunction with the Edo Football Association (EFA). A total of 39 U-13 teams will vie for honours in the tournament. The teams are made up of 29 from Edo south and 5 each from Edo central and Edo north respectively. Coaches and club administrators have been admonished to avoid falsifying their players, as eligible players are children born from January 1, 2012. Each team is allowed to register a max of 20 players at the start, and no player can play for 2 different teams in the tournament. Winners will go home with ₦1 million, the 1st and 2nd runners-up will receive ₦750,000 and ₦500,000 respectively, while the 4th place will go home with ₦250,000.

11. In the current Olympic medals table, *China* is ahead with 12 Gold medals so far. The *United States*, however have the highest number of medals in total (38), with a lot of Silver and Bronze medals, than China with a total of 26 medals. *Nigeria* have won 0 medals so far.

12. 🤣 José Mourinho: “I remember a game in Siena, with Maicon. They said he always got a fifth yellow to be suspended at Christmas, so he could go on vacation to Brazil. I went to him and said that if he got a yellow he wouldn't be going on vacation, I'm not an idiot. He asked if he scored, could he go? I said 'No, only if you score two.' In the game, he scored two goals, received a yellow card for taking his shirt off and he went on vacation. I also gave him an extra week off."😂

[04/08/2024, 11:31:06] Dr Maurice GSK: Take note of these👇🏾

1. Apply for jobs with only PDF format CVs, unless stated otherwise (which is very rare). PDF only, please.

2. Your CV must carry the address of the location of the job you are applying for. Stop wasting your time using a CV with a Lagos address to apply for a job in Abuja.

3. Remove personal information like age, state of origin, religion, language, gender, full home address, and referee from your CV. They are not needed unless requested. Including this information can expose your CV to unfair treatment. Nobody will give you a job because you put the name of someone in Ekiti, Delta, or Abuja on your CV. Referees are for documentation when you have already got the job.

4. Use keywords in your CV to aid ATS (Applicant Tracking System) reading. Ensure your CV is ATS compliant.

5. Your CV should not be more than one page or a maximum of two pages. No recruiter will read a three-page CV; it's very irrelevant.

6. NYSC is not a certificate; it is normal work experience.

7. When asked, "How many years of work experience do you have?" stop saying, "I just finished NYSC" or "I'm still serving." NYSC is not the beginning of work experience. All experience counts, whether before or after NYSC, SIWES, or internships.

8. A picture is not needed on your CV unless you are a graphic designer or you want to use your appearance to replace skills.

9. Some people are still snapping paper CVs to apply for jobs. You are stuck in 1997. Your case is not for today.

10. Always fill in the body and subject of the email when applying for a job. Never leave them empty. Don't just send an empty email with only the CV attached.

11. Don't forward CVs from one email to another; it will always carry all previous emails. Always attach the CV fresh when applying.

12. Name your CV with your real name, e.g., "Taiwo Emmanuel Oluwaseun CV."

13. Most importantly, revamp your CV today.

‎[09/08/2024, 07:32:34] Wellington: *8* Things Visitors Are Forbidden To Do At *Oba Of Benin Palace*


1. Pointing: Pointing fingers at either Oba or his Chiefs are not allowed at the Oba’s palace.

2. Whistling: Whistling might seem like a simple and harmless act, but when in Benin City, especially at the Palace, this is considered rude and not allowed.

3. Open Umbrella during festivals: If you are visiting Benin and you plan to attend a festival at the palace, be prepared to stand through any condition the weather throws at you without protection.

4. Black apparel: Anyone wearing black attire is not allowed entrance into the palace, especially if the person has the intention of gaining an audience with the Oba or there is a high chance of the person crossing paths with the Oba.

5. Women at the Alaka area: Till date women are not allowed entrance into this area.

6. Male visitors to the royal harem: No male visitor of any kind is allowed near the royal harem. The royal harem includes the Queen as well as other wives and concubines belonging to the Oba.

7. Banga (palm oil fruits) on the head: While Banga soup is notably consumed by people in Benin City, carrying its source – the palm oil fruit – on your head in or around the palace is strictly prohibited.

8. Dogs: Dogs are not allowed into the palace or run around it while playing.

_*BREASTFEEDING WEEK*_


World Breastfeeding Week is held annually in the first week of August. It's supported by WHO, UNICEF and many Ministries of Health and civil society partners. The 2024 theme is “Closing the gap: Breastfeeding support for all”. The campaign is to celebrate breastfeeding mums in all their diversity, throughout their breastfeeding journeys, while showcasing the ways families, societies, communities and health workers can have the back of every breastfeeding mum.

Breastfeeding is one of the most effective ways to ensure child health and survival. However, contrary to WHO recommendations, fewer than half of infants under 6 months old are exclusively breastfed.

Breastmilk is the ideal food for infants. It is safe, clean and contains antibodies which help protect against many common childhood illnesses.

Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months has many benefits for the infant and mother. Chief among these is protection against gastrointestinal infections which is observed not only in developing but also industrialized countries. Early initiation of breastfeeding, within 1 hour of birth, protects the newborn from acquiring infections and reduces newborn mortality. The risk of mortality due to diarrhoea and other infections can increase in infants who are either partially breastfed or not breastfed at all.

Breast-milk is also an important source of energy and nutrients in children aged 6–23 months. It can provide half or more of a child’s energy needs between the ages of 6 and 12 months, and one third of energy needs between 12 and 24 months. Breast milk is also a critical source of energy and nutrients during illness, and reduces mortality among children who are malnourished.

Children and adolescents who were breastfed as babies are less likely to be overweight or obese. Additionally, they perform better on intelligence tests and have higher school attendance. Breastfeeding is associated with higher income in adult life. Improving child development and reducing health costs results in economic gains for individual families as well as at the national level.

Longer durations of breastfeeding also contribute to the health and well-being of mothers: it reduces the risk of ovarian and breast cancer and helps space pregnancies–exclusive breastfeeding of babies under 6 months has a hormonal effect which often induces a lack of menstruation. This is a natural (though not fail-safe) method of birth control known as the Lactation Amenorrhoea Method.

Inappropriate marketing of breast-milk substitutes continues to undermine efforts to improve breastfeeding rates and duration worldwide.

‎[09/08/2024, 17:32:38] Sir Prof  Pharm Abu Dantani John: *8* Things Visitors Are Forbidden To Do At *Oba Of Benin Palace*


1. Pointing: Pointing fingers at either Oba or his Chiefs are not allowed at the Oba’s palace.

2. Whistling: Whistling might seem like a simple and harmless act, but when in Benin City, especially at the Palace, this is considered rude and not allowed.

3. Open Umbrella during festivals: If you are visiting Benin and you plan to attend a festival at the palace, be prepared to stand through any condition the weather throws at you without protection.

4. Black apparel: Anyone wearing black attire is not allowed entrance into the palace, especially if the person has the intention of gaining an audience with the Oba or there is a high chance of the person crossing paths with the Oba.

5. Women at the Alaka area: Till date women are not allowed entrance into this area.

6. Male visitors to the royal harem: No male visitor of any kind is allowed near the royal harem. The royal harem includes the Queen as well as other wives and concubines belonging to the Oba.

7. Banga (palm oil fruits) on the head: While Banga soup is notably consumed by people in Benin City, carrying its source – the palm oil fruit – on your head in or around the palace is strictly prohibited.

8. Dogs: Dogs are not allowed into the palace or run around it while playing.

*Sports Update*⚽🏀🧘🏻‍♂️🏊🏻‍♀️♟️🏆
_Sports Information from the Week_
09.08.2024


(1–13)

1. 😁 *Football is back!* The 2024/25 league season starts with the FA Community Shield tomorrow (August 10) between the 23/24 EPL champion (Man City) and the FA Cup winner (Man United). The UEFA Super Cup comes up on Wednesday (August 14), between the 23/24 UCL champion, Real Madrid and the UEL champion, Atalanta.. On Thursday (August 15), La Liga commences. On Friday (August 16), Ligue 1 resumes for the season. The *English Premier League (EPL)* also kick-starts same Friday. On Saturday (August 17), Serie A resumes. The German Bundesliga resumes on August 23. On August 29, the UCL draw for the 24/25 season will take place. The UCL Group stage games resumes by September 17.

2. ⚽ The 2024 *Summer Transfer Window* has been a busy period as expected. Most leagues in Europe opened their windows on July 1, while the general deadline for closing is on Friday, August 30. Clubs in all leagues will still be able to sign players as “free agents” after the deadline, and as long as they are not officially attached to any club on August 30. Some clubs have made some great signings so far. *Arsenal* signed in Riccardo Calafiori (from Bologna). *Aston Villa* who will be playing UCL football this season, have signed in Ross Barkley, Cameron Archer, Jaden Philogene, Amadou Onana, Iaan Maatsen, among others. *Chelsea* have signed in Marc Guiu, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Filip Jorgensen, Tosin Adarabioyo, Samuel Samu Omorodion (a 20-year old spanish striker with Nigerian parents, most likely Edo State of Origin)..

3. ⚽ ...*Fulham* signed in Emile Smith Rowe (from Arsenal) and Ryan Sessegnon (from Tottenham). Nigeria's Kelechi Iheanacho (Senior man) is now a Sevilla player, having left Leicester City. Wilfred Ndidi remains at Leicester. While *Liverpool* is yet to sign in any player (the only EPL club that haven't yet), *Man City* have signed in Savinho. Julian Alvarez is about becoming an Atletico Madrid player in a big money deal that will be the most expensive outbound transfer in City's history. The likes of Anthony Martial, Raphael Varane, Donny van de Beek, Mason Greenwood, are no more *Man United* players. United have signed in Joshua Zirkzee and Leny Yoro. *West Ham* have impressed with their signings, having signed in Niclas Fullkrug, Crysencio Summerville, Maximilian Kilman, Guido Rodriguez, Wes Foderingham. See more on: www.premierleague.com/transfers

4. ♟️ ...In Ojodu Berger, a bustling, densely populated district that borders Lagos from Ogun State, *Mohammed Azeez* sits down on rented chairs and makeshift tables in his parents’ house, teaching children and teenagers how to play chess. There are at least a dozen children who come around in the evenings and on weekends for extracurricular lessons, all registered under his nonprofit *Milverton Chess Academy*. He accepts donations from parents but has kept the academy free-to-attend since he started it, informally, in 2004... “I find it difficult to have the knowledge of something and not share. That was why I started the academy. I wanted people to benefit from it, because chess teaches a lot.”... “While I was reading about chess, I discovered that it is a game that teaches logic, philosophy, psychology and mathematics, and if you play chess your level of reasoning would be higher. Chess can bring lots of good to kids and even adults.”... read more on: www.aljazeera.com/features/2024/8/7/young-nigerians-find-pawns-of-purpose-after-local-chess-prodigys-success

5. 🏃🏻‍♂️ On Monday, Nigeria's *Ezekiel Nathaniel* became the first Nigerian athlete in 12 years to reach the semifinals of the *400m hurdles* at the Olympics. He secured his spot by finishing 2nd in heat 4 with a time of 48.32 seconds, earning an automatic qualification. Another Athlete, *Samuel Ogazi*, shattered a 24-year record by advancing to the semifinals in the men’s 400m. Ogazi ran a new personal best of 44.50 seconds, finishing 2nd behind USA’s Quincy Hall, who won the race in 44.28 seconds. Ogazi’s impressive performance marked the first time in 24 years that a Nigerian male quarter-miler qualified for the 400m semifinals at the Olympics..

6. 🏃🏻‍♂️ ..In the semifinals on Wednesday, 21-year old *Ezekiel Nathaniel* failed to advance to the final of the men’s 400m hurdle as he finished 6th with the time of 48.65sec. The World record holder and defending champion, *Karsten Warholm* of Norway won the heat with 47.67secs, advancing to the finals which takes place today (Friday).. In the 400m semifinal, *Samuel Ogazi* made history as *the first Nigerian man since 1988 (36 years ago)* to qualify for the Olympic 400-metre final. The 18-year-old achieved this feat with a third-place finish in Heat 3 of the semifinals, clocking a new personal-best time of 44.41 seconds at the ongoing Paris Olympics. However, in the finals on Wednesday, he finished 7th (44.43s), and couldn't finish among the top 3 medalist.

7. 🥈 28-years old *Annette Nneka Echikunwoke*, a Nigerian-American hammer thrower, was to represent Nigeria at the 2020 Summer Olympics, but was disqualified along 9 other athletes due to the negligence of the Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN). She changed allegiance and represented the *United States* at the ongoing Paris Olympics. Now, she can call herself an Olympic medalist after winning *Silver medal* in the Women's Hammer Throw. She holds the African area record in hammer throw, with a throw of 75.49 m in Tucson in 2021.

8. 🏃🏻‍♀️ On Tuesday, Star Girl *Favour Ofili*, missed out on winning a medal in the 200m final, succumbing to the supremacy of USA's Gabby Thomas, who won her first individual Olympic Gold medal. Ofili gave her best on the night from lane 9, one of the most challenging lanes to run, having a good start as she stormed round the bend with the field on the home straight. However, the strength and speed endurance of Thomas was unmatchable, storming to the finish line in an impressive time of 21.82s. Newly crowned Olympic 100m champion, Julien Alfred, won her second medal in Paris with an astounding finish for the silver medal in 22.08s, while USA's Brittany Brown gave her all to finish third in 22.20s. Great Britain's Dina Asher-Smith was fourth in 22.20s, ahead of her countrywoman Daryll Neita in 22.22s, edging Ofili who settled for the sixth position in 22.24s. Despite the loss, Ofili can take solace in the fact that she became *the first Nigerian to make an Olympic 200m final in 28 years* and she did that in her maiden Olympic appearance.

9. 🏃🏻‍♀️ On Wednesday, World record holder, *Tobi Amusan*, qualified for the 100m hurdles semi-finals in the ongoing Paris Olympics (her third consecutive semi-finals at the Olympics). She led the pack of eight athletes with 12.49 seconds, followed by America’s Alaysha Johnson with 12.61s and Jamaica’s Janeek Brown with 12.84s. Amusan is certainly among the favourites for the Gold medal, but that won’t come easy, contending with a strong field that includes the Bahamas’ Devynne Charlton, USA’s Alaysha Johnson, world champion Danielle Williams and reigning Olympic champion Jasmine Camacho-Quinn of Puerto Rico. The semi-finals holds today (August 9), while the final holds tomorrow.

10. 🏀 Nigeria's female Basketball Team, *D’Tigress*, became the first African side – male or female – to reach the quarter-finals of an Olympic Games after beating Canada in their final group game last Sunday. They registered a win on their Olympic debut in Athens in 2004 but had to wait 20 years for their second victory.. “I'm really proud of them putting Nigeria on the map again after 20 years,” Mfon Udoka, a member of the 2004 squad, told BBC Sport Africa.. The glue binding this team together is *Rena Wakama*, the 32-year-old whose journey with the team has been remarkable. In just over a year in charge, as *the first female head coach of D’Tigress*, Wakama won AfroBasket last year and then secured qualification for the Olympics in February.. “I believe her resilience, her hunger to make a name and also prove a point to critics who didn't feel she was good enough to take the job has [made] an impact,” basketball commentator and analyst Queen John-Moseph told BBC Sport Africa.. On Wednesday, D’Tigress unfortunately lost to USA (88–74) in the Quarter finals. It was however, a good Olympic campaign for the team. 

11. 🇳🇬 Nigeria’s long jump trio of *Ese Brume*, *Prestina Ochonogor*, and *Ruth Usoro*, competed for places on the podium in *the final of the women’s long jump event* of the Paris 2024 Olympics yesterday (Thursday). This made them the first Nigerian trio to make the final of an individual event at the Olympics (the last time Nigeria had more than one athlete in an athletics Olympic final was in Atlanta in 1996 when Falilat Ogunkoya and Fatimat Yusuf both made the women’s 400m final). The 3 jumpers made the final as part of the top 12 athletes in the event on Tuesday, with Brume and Usoro qualifying from the qualifying Group A, while Ochonogor qualified from Group B. Prestina Ochonogor began her journey as a long jumper at *Main bowl of the University of Benin* (UNIBEN), Edo State.. However, they all lost out on a medal in the finals yesterday, with Ese Brume finishing 5th (6.70m), Ruth Usoro finishing 10th (6.58m) and Ochonogor finishing 12th (6.24m). The Gold medalist, T. Davis-Woodhall (United States) hit 7.10 metres.

12. The ongoing *Paris Olympics* is set to come to an end this Sunday (August 11). The closing ceremony is scheduled to be held at Stade de France. It's been a great tournament. The programme for the Olympics featured 329 events in 32 sports, encompassing a total of 48 disciplines. This includes the 28 "core" Olympic sports contested in 2016 and 2020, and 4 optional sports that were proposed by the Paris Organising Committee. The various Sports that have been witnessed in this Olympics: Aquatics (Artistic Swimming, Diving, Marathon Swimming, Swimming, Water Polo), Archery, Athletics, Badminton, Basketball, Boxing, Breaking, Canoeing (Slalom, Sprint), Cycling, Equestrian, Fencing, Field hockey, Football, Golf, Gymnastics, Handball, Judo, Modern Pentathlon, Rowing, Rugby sevens, Sailing, Shooting, Skateboarding, Sport climbing, Surfing, Table Tennis, Taekwondo, Tennis, Triathlon, Volleyball, Weightlifting, Wrestling.

13. 🥇 On the Olympic Medals table (as at 9pm yesterday – Thursday), the top 5 are: *United States* (total of 103 medals: 30 gold, 38 silver, 35 bronze), *China* (total of 72 medals: 28 gold, 25 silver, 19 bronze), *Australia* (total of 45 medals: 18 gold, 14 silver, 13 bronze), *France* (total of 53 medals: 14 gold, 18 silver, 21 bronze), *Great Britain* (total of 51 medals: 13 gold, 17 silver, 21 bronze). 6th place *Korea* had a total of 28 medals, a huge distance from 5th placed Britain. *84 countries* have won at least 1 medal in this ongoing Olympics. *Nigeria* haven't won any medal yet (0 medals). Can Tobi Amusan make us proud today? See more on: https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/medals

‎[10/08/2024, 21:02:25] Sir Prof  Pharm Abu Dantani John: *Pharm. (Prof.) Cyril Odianose Usifoh*, FPSN, FNAPharm, FPCPharm, an Academic Pharmacist, obtained his B.Pharm from Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU); his MSc from Sussex University, Brighton; and his PhD from Westfalischen Wilhelms University, Münster, Germany. He joined the services of the University of Benin (UNIBEN) and was promoted to a Professor in 2003. He was also made the Head of Department (HOD) of Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Dean, Faculty of Pharmacy (2006–2010). Most recently, he was elected as the President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) in 2021.

Prof. Usifoh has served and chaired in various committees and sub-committees in UNIBEN and the local community. He has served as an External Examiner to some Nigerian and Foreign Universities and Reviewer to several National and International Journals. His scholarly works have earned him a number of awards, including the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), the Tetfund National Research Grant as Principal Investigator in “The use of Pesticides in food preservation’’ and the 2017 May & Baker Professional Service Award in Pharmacy.

Prof. Usifoh is a Member of – The European Association of Pharma Biotechnology; Quantitative Structural Activity Relationship Society; International Society for the Study of Xenobiotic; International Society for the Development of Natural Products; International Society of Pharmacoeconomics and Outcome Research, and Royal Society of Chemistry. He is also a Fellow of several Pharmaceutical Groups in Nigeria. He is happily married to Professor (Mrs) Stella Usifoh and is a father of three.

*INTERNATIONAL YOUTH DAY, 2024*


Today, there are 1.2 billion young people aged 15 to 24 years, accounting for 16% of the global population. By 2030 – the target date for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) that make up the 2030 Agenda – the number of youth is projected to have grown by 7%, to nearly 1.3 billion.

As youth are increasingly demanding more just, equitable and progressive opportunities and solutions in their societies, the need to address the multifaceted challenges faced by young people (such as access to education, health, employment and gender equality) have become more pressing than ever.

Youth can be a positive force for development when provided with the knowledge and opportunities they need to thrive. In particular, young people should acquire the education and skills needed to contribute in a productive economy; and they need access to a job market that can absorb them into the labour force.

‎[13/08/2024, 21:25:07] Pharm Osakponmwen Oviasogie: *Edo state government in collaboration with BEDC Edo State Launches Mass Metering Program to Boost Electricity Supply.*

In a bid to revolutionize the power sector and improve the lives of its citizens, the Edo State Ministry of Mining and Energy has partnered with the Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC) to launch a mass metering program. This initiative aims to provide electricity meters to households and businesses across the state, promoting transparency, efficiency, and economic growth.

The mass metering program is a significant step towards addressing the long-standing issue of estimated billing, which has been a source of concern for electricity consumers in the state. By providing meters, consumers will have accurate readings, reducing the likelihood of disputes and ensuring that they only pay for the electricity they consume.

The mass metering program is expected to have far-reaching benefits for the people of Edo State, including:

- Improved electricity supply and reduced power outages
- Accurate billing and reduced estimated charges.
- Increased access to reliable and affordable electricity
- Support for economic growth and development
- Enhanced quality of life for residents.
- More Cheaper and affordable.

The Edo State mass metering program is a laudable initiative that demonstrates the state government's commitment to improving the lives of its citizens. By providing access to reliable and affordable electricity, the program is poised to have a positive impact on the state's economy and social well-being.

Millionaires don't sink their income into things that lose value.
They pump money into assets that grow their fortune.
It's not just about making money - it's about keeping it.
Invest in things that pay you back.

3. Building an Emergency Fund

Millionaires save cash for chaos.

They prepare, they don't repair.

- Not chasing fleeting luxuries.

- Always playing the long game.

Multiple streams = cash flow kingdom.

Read your way to the top.

9. Networking

Rich people have wealthy friends.
Poor people have broke friends.
Millionaires don't chitchat.
They plant seeds in rich soil & strategically ally.

10. Paying Themselves First

Millionaires treat themselves like companies.
They account for profits before expenses.
They don't save what's left.
They SAVE FIRST, then spend what is left.

*Sports Update*⚽🏀🧘🏻‍♂️🏊🏻‍♀️♟️🏆
_Sports Information from the Week_
16.08.2024


(1–12)

1. 🏀 There was a crazy semifinal basketball game last week Thursday in the Paris Olympics (USA vs Serbia) and it ended *95–91* in USA's favour. After cruising through their first 4 games of the Olympics, the star-studded USA men's basketball team got a scare from Serbia and three-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokic in that semifinal game, falling behind by as many as 17 points and heading into the final quarter down 13. *Stephen Curry* put together his best performance in a USA jersey scoring 36 points – one shy of the American Olympic record for men's basketball held by Carmelo Anthony and the most ever for a U.S. player in a knockout game, per ESPN Stats & Information. Team USA needed almost every one, along with a clutch performance from *LeBron James*, to advance and face France for the Gold medal. USA won the *Gold medal* in the men's basketball final last Saturday, defeating France *98–87*.

2. 🏀 *Stephen Curry* has now played 29 games for USA basketball team. He's never lost any of them. The best player in Basketball currently?... Team USA’s *Kevin Durant* is now the first basketball player to win *4 Gold Medals* (4 different Olympic tournaments) in men’s Olympic basketball history. Durant has also scored the most points in USA Olympic history. The two-time NBA Finals MVP cements himself as the most decorated USA Basketball player ever.

3. 🥇 *Yemisi Ogunleye* (representing Germany), grabbed the *Gold medal* in the *women’s shot put* at the Paris Olympics last Friday, throwing her winning 20.00m with her final attempt. Ogunleye’s previous best performance was a silver in the world indoor championships in 2024, while she also collected a bronze in the European Championships in Rome in June. 25-year old Yemisi Ogunleye has a Yoruba *Nigerian father* and a German mother. She was born and grew up in Germany.

4. ⚽🏆 Last Saturday, Pep Guardiola's *Manchester City* defeated Erik Ten Hag's Manchester United 7–6 on penalties (after a 1–1 FT draw) to win the 2024 Community Shield. *Pep Guardiola* has now won *39 trophies* as a Manager in his 17 years career. He has won 18 titles as Man City's manager, won 14 titles as the coach of FC Barcelona, and he won 7 titles when he managed Bayern Munich.

5. ⚽🥇 Chelsea Women's former coach, *Emma Hayes*, who became the head coach of the *United States Women's Team* just after the end of last season, guided USA to a *Gold medal* in the Paris Olympics in her first ever major tournament as their manager! USA defeated Brazil (1–0) in the women's final last Saturday. Brazil had defeated Spain (4–2) in the semifinals to get to the final.

6. 🇳🇬 The Paris Olympics came to an end last Sunday. Despite D'Tigress getting knocked out by USA in the quarter finals, coach *Rene Wakama* was named the Best Female Basketball Coach of the Paris Olympics. The US Female Basketball Team that eliminated D'Tigress, went on to clinch the Gold medal, their 8th consecutive Olympic Gold medal! The *United States* are the best nation in the Olympics, finishing with a total of *126 medals* (40G, 44S, 42B) accumulated from various sports in the tournament. *China* finished with *91 medals* (40G, 27S, 24B). A total of *91 countries* were on the medal list (won at least 1 medal).

7. 🥇🥈 Some Nigerian-born Olympians won medals representing other countries. 5 of them are: *Yemisi Ogunleye* first German to win gold medal in 28 years in shot put event. *Annette Echikunwoke* won silver medal for US in hammer throwing event. *Samu Omorodion* won gold medal for Spain in football. *Salwa Eid Naser* (formerly Ebelechukwu Agbapuonwu) won silver medal for Bahrain in 400m women's event. *Michael Olise* won silver medal for France in football.

8. 🇳🇬 In the just concluded Olympics, the *continent of Africa* won a total of *39* medals – 13 gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze – spread across 12 nations, with Kenya the most successful with 11 podium finishes, and South Africa with 6. A total of 15 African countries took part in the Olympics. In Tokyo 2020, Africa finished with 37 medals, while at Rio 2016, Africa finished with 45 medals. Will Africa perform better in the next Olympic tournament, *Los Angeles (LA) 2028*?.. One major area where Africa faces a disadvantage is in funding for facilities and support for athletes. The numbers are stark compared to most developed nations. The United States, for example, boasts world-class facilities, a college system providing a pipeline of top-level talent in individual and team sports and huge sponsorship deals.. Over the past 60 years, *Nigeria* has come home from five editions of the Olympics empty handed: Mexico City 1968, Moscow 1980, Seoul 1988, London 2012 and Paris 2024.. Read more on: www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/articles/c4gdwy72ee5o

9. ⚽💰 This week, Real Madrid's *Vinicius Jnr* REJECTED a €1B (5 years) offer from Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabian Investment Fund made the proposal to sign him to *Al Ahli* and promised the biggest contract in football history! The contract would make Vini Jnr earn 13x his current salary, with other incentives such as an ambassador role for the 2034 World Cup. The move would make him the highest paid Athlete EVER!

10. 🏅 The 2024 *PFA Awards* is here. This is the 51st edition, and about 6 players have been nominated in each of the various categories (Young Player of the Year, Players' Player of the Year, etcetera). The winners will be announced next week Tuesday (August 20).

11. ⚽🏆 The 2024 *UEFA Super Cup* game, Real Madrid vs Atalanta (Champion of UCL v UEL), ended 2–0 FT in favour of Madrid, with Federico Valverde and Kylian Mbappé on the scoresheet. Real Madrid keeps winning Europe! Congratulations to the team.. *Luka Modric* left Tottenham at 27 years old with 0 trophies. Now at 38, he's Real Madrid's most decorated player with *27 trophies*! No other Real Madrid player has won more trophies. Legend!

12. ⚽ League Football is fully back. The big one on MatchWeek 1 is *Chelsea vs Man City* on Sunday. Anthony Taylor will officiate the game.


_Share your thoughts and opinions on the Sports Update. Hope you had a good week?_

Remember to relax and recoup from the week's stress. Sports is beautiful. Do enjoy your weekend🙌🏻

GENERAL ADVICE TO CONTESTING CANDIDATES AND EDO YOUNG PHARMACISTS


*Advice to Contesting Candidates*:


❇️ Your leadership will be a service to Edo Young Pharmacists. It's a commitment to impact YPs through whatever position you're vying for, for the 2024/25 administrative period and beyond. It's one you have to value from the depth of your heart. You will also be a role model to YPs. We hope you be the best role model you can be and keep evolving in leadership.

❇️ In your election campaigns, always show respect for your opponent(s). Though you may be opponents through this election, you are all YPs who desire the best for Edo Young Pharmacists. Conduct a healthy campaign (keeping to the rules), one that would inspire Young Pharmacists, and reflect positive leadership.

❇️ Always remember that this is about serving YPs and contributing to the growth of Edo YPG, and this should be greater than any personal ambition. At the end of the elections, do celebrate with the winner(s) and celebrate yourselves as well. It's important you all collaborate and work together to ensure Edo YPG keep growing and impacting.


*Advice to all Young Pharmacists*:


❇️ It's that time again to vote for your leaders. As you get to find out the candidates vying for various positions, make your choices from a perspective of clarity, being unbiased, and putting the organization ahead of personal preferences. Let true leadership guide your decisions. May YPG Edo State keep succeeding. Amen.

❇️ During the campaigns, on the election day and after the election, appreciate and value all contesting candidates and celebrate with everyone of them (both the winners and other contestants who didn't win). As YPs, we value the growth and progress of Edo YPG and we should work together, in harmony, to achieve this.

❇️ On the day of the election (please, keep to time and come early), come along with a valid means of identification (that easily idenfies you), your PSN Dues Payment Receipt for 2024 (confirming payment of YPG Dues for the year), or a receipt of YPG Dues payment for 2024.


Let's have an inspiring and successful 2024 elections🤝

*MPOX VIRUS Outbreak?*


In the past few days, there have been news about the global outbreak of a highly contagious and severe strain of *mpox*. Sweden confirmed an outbreak on Thursday. Yesterday, Pakistan reported a case from a traveler who returned from a gulf country. The current strain of the mpox virus circulating in Congo (*mpox clade I*) and a dozen other African countries, is a different strain than the one that had circulated in the U.S. about 2 years ago (In the U.S., the *mpox clade II* strain has primarily circulated among men who have sex with men). *Mpox clade I* is considered more transmissible and the symptoms are more severe. It has infected tens of thousands of people, including children, sex workers and workers in health care settings who lack proper protective equipment.

*What is Mpox?*

Mpox, previously known as monkeypox, is a virus that spreads to people from animals and was named monkeypox because that's the animal it was first discovered in, not because monkeys are the source of infections. It comes from the same virus family as smallpox and can pass from person to person through physical contact, according to the CDC. It was first discovered in 1958 and the first human case occurred in 1970 in Congo. Infection is usually mild, but it can result in death. It causes symptoms similar to flu, as well as pus-filled skin lesions. There are two types of mpox – clade I and clade II. Clade I is endemic in central Africa, while clade II is endemic in West Africa. A new variant of clade I, called Ib, appears to spread more easily. Congo and surrounding countries have had worsening outbreaks since 2023. Just in 2024, central and eastern Africa have had over 17,000 infections and more than 500 people died from mpox, primarily in Congo, according to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, which recently issued its own emergency declaration for the outbreaks.

*How do one contract Mpox?*

Mpox spreads when one come into contact with an animal or a person infected with the virus. *Person-to-person* spread (transmission) occurs when one come in contact with the sores, scabs, respiratory droplets or oral fluids of a person who’s infected, usually through close, intimate situations like cuddling, kissing or sex. Research is ongoing, but experts aren’t sure if the virus is transmitted through semen or vaginal fluids. *Animal-to-person transmission* occurs through broken skin, like from bites or scratches, or through direct contact with an infected animal’s blood, bodily fluids or pox lesions (sores). One can also get mpox by coming into contact with recently contaminated materials like clothing, bedding and other linens used by a person or animal who’s infected.

*Management and Prevention?*

Mpox is usually a self-limited disease (gets better without treatment) with symptoms lasting from  2–4 weeks. Following diagnosis, a healthcare provider will monitor one's condition and try to relieve the symptoms, prevent dehydration and give antibiotics to treat secondary bacterial infections if they develop.

If one is at risk for mpox, getting vaccinated helps stop the spread. Other forms of prevention include decreasing human contact with infected animals and limiting person-to-person spread.

In addition to vaccines, other ways to help prevent the spread of mpox include:

– avoiding contact with infected animals (especially sick or dead animals)
– avoiding contact with bedding and other materials contaminated with the virus,
– thoroughly cooking all foods that contain animal meat or parts
– washing your hands frequently with soap and water 
– avoiding contact with people who may be infected with the virus
– p3racticing safe sex, including the use of condoms and dental dams
– wearing a mask that covers your mouth and nose when around others
– cleaning and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces
– using personal protective equipment (PPE) when caring for people infected with the virus.

_Sports Information from the Week_
23.08.2024


(1–14)

1. *Para-athletics* is the sport of athletics practiced by people with a disability as a parasport. The sport is known by various names, including disability athletics, disabled track and field and Paralympic athletics. Top-level competitors may be called elite athletes with disability. Competitors are typically organised into three broad categories: deaf sports, athletes with a physical disability, and athletes with an intellectual disability. Deaf athletes typically compete among themselves, while athletes with physical and intellectual disabilities are usually assessed and given a para-athletics classification, which groups together athletes with similar ability levels. These classifications are governed by the *International Paralympic Committee (IPC)* and comprise a single letter and a number: T for Track or F for Field, then a number defining the level of ability. In competition, events may take place between athletes of identical class if numbers are sufficient, otherwise a range of similar classes may compete in the same event. Read more on: en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para-athletics

2. The *2024 Summer Paralympics* (the 17th edition) starts in 5 days time (August 28) and ends on September 8. It will be held in Paris (France) like the just concluded Olympics. It is an International multi-sport parasports event governed by the International Paralympic Committee. It's the first time Paris will host the Paralympics in its history and the second time that France will host the Paralympic Games, as Tignes and Albertville jointly hosted the 1992 Winter Paralympics. The Paralympics will feature 549 events in 22 sports. Some of the sports are: badminton, boccia, football 5-aside, judo, paracanoe, goalball, powerlifting, sitting volleyball, swimming, wheelchair basketball, wheelchair fencing, wheelchair rugby, wheelchair tennis, etcetera

3. 🏊🏻‍♀️ American Paralympic Swimmer, *Trischa Zorn-Hudson* (currently 60 years old), is the most successful athlete in the history of the Paralympic Games, having won *55* medals (41 Gold, 9 Silver, 5 Bronze) over 7 Paralympics. Blind from birth, she competed in Paralympic swimming (S12, SB12, and SM12 disability categories). She was inducted into the Paralympic Hall of Fame in 2012.

Mpox, also known as Monkeypox, is a rare but potentially serious viral illness caused by the Mpox virus. It's usually spread through close contact with an infected person's skin lesions, respiratory droplets, or contaminated objects. Mpox can cause fever, headache, muscle aches, and a characteristic rash or blisters. While anyone can get Mpox, certain groups like healthcare workers, laboratory workers, and people with weakened immune systems are at higher risk.

There are two types or clades of mpox. Clade II, which originates in west Africa, is less severe. It has a fatality rate of up to 1% (in other words, roughly one in 100 are expected to die from it). But clade I, from central Africa, has a fatality rate of up to 10% (up to one in ten die). 

In 2022, an epidemic of mpox swept through non-endemic countries, including beyond Africa. This was a variant of clade II originating from Nigeria, called clade IIb.  That epidemic ‎image omitted

‎[24/08/2024, 08:58:18] Sir Prof  Pharm Abu Dantani John: *What is Mpox?*
Mpox formerly known as Monkeypox is an illness caused by the monkeypox virus. It is a viral infection which can spread between people, mainly through close contact, and occasionally from the environment to people via things and surfaces that have been touched by a person with mpox. 

*What are the signs and symptoms of Mpox?*
Mpox can cause a range of signs and symptoms. While some people have less severe symptoms, others may develop more serious illness and need care in a health facility. Common symptoms of mpox include 
✓a rash which may last for 2–4 weeks. 
✓fever,
✓ headache, 
✓muscle aches, 
✓back pain, 
✓low energy and 
✓swollen glands (lymph nodes). 

*How is Mpox contracted?*
Mpox spreads from person to person mainly through close contact with someone who has mpox. 
Close contact includes ✓skin-to-skin (such as touching or sex)  ✓mouth-to-mouth, or mouth-to-skin contact (such as kissing),  ✓face-to-face with someone who has mpox (such as talking or breathing close to one another, which ‎image omitted

*THE YOU PROJECT* : _Protecting the Welfare and Interests of Young Pharmacists_

_Priorities:_
1. *Career Development and Advancement Opportunities*: Empowering young Pharmacists to grow professionally and reach their full potential.

2. *Encouraging Innovation, Research, and Entrepreneurship*: Fostering creativity, innovation, and entrepreneurial spirit to drive progress in Pharmacy practice.

3. *Fostering a Positive and Inclusive Work Environment*: Creating a supportive, diverse, and inclusive workplace culture that promotes collaboration and well-being.

4. *Improving Job Satisfaction and Retention*: Addressing factors that lead to burnout and turnover, ensuring young pharmacists stay engaged and committed to their careers.

5. *Enhancing Skills and Knowledge*: Providing access to training, education, and resources that keep young Pharmacists up-to-date with best practices.

6. *Work-Life Balance and Flexible Scheduling*: Supporting young Pharmacists in achieving a healthy balance between their professional and personal lives.

7. *Urgent Support and Solutions*: Providing prompt attention and addressing challenges and concerns of young Pharmacists.

*Call to Action:*
We invite you to share your thoughts, challenges, and suggestions on how to further improve our practice through ‘’The You Project’’

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSe4Wr7FQPI14qhQbFZyEMzsuqvmw5t7g51HGO7S49JFWlhjyw/viewform?usp=sf_link

 Your input will help shape the future of Pharmacy practice and support the well-being and success of young Pharmacists.

One of our Young Pharmacist, *THEOPHILUS VENN*, founder of *Edveen Cup*, won the Battle of Ideas Cohort 1 about a week ago. He contested with other young entrepreneurs before reaching the final stage where he won the contest. The “Battle of Ideas” is a TIO initiative to provide young entrepreneurs with necessary resources needed to thrive and become self sustainable in a competitive society like Nigeria.

Connect with Pharm Theophilus Venn on Instagram: www.instagram.com/vennbiscuits

Pharm Theophilus Venn shared the story behind *Edveen Cup*'s mission. It address the critical social issue of plastic pollution and its associated environmental and health impacts. Single-use plastics contribute significantly to environmental degradation, accounting for nearly 50% of the plastic generated globally. Nigeria generates 2.5 million tonnes of plastic waste annually, ranking ninth globally in plastic pollution. Unfortunately, over 88% of this waste in Nigeria is not recycled, ending up in landfills..

*Edveen Cup*'s mission is to reduce plastic waste and promote healthy living through innovative, environmentally friendly products. By offering edible, biodegradable alternatives, Edveen Cups reduce reliance on single-use plastics, promoting a healthier planet and enhancing community well-being by minimizing pollution. Edveen Cups is not solving environmental issues but serves as a healthy alternative for all ages. These fiber-rich, preservative-free cups offer a delicious and sustainable option for serving creams and yogurt.

[29/08/2024, 11:15:50] Rx Esohe: This will take only two minutes of your time. 🙏

Technology-driven Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) reporting systems are crucial for improving patient safety and enhancing the accuracy of ADR detection. Community pharmacists play a vital role in this process. To ensure effective utilization, it is essential to understand pharmacists' knowledge and perceptions of these systems.

*This study aims to assess community pharmacists' knowledge, and perception of technology-driven ADR reporting systems*. It will also assess the current practices and training needs of community pharmacists on ADR reporting. We kindly request your participation in this study by completing the questionnaire, which will take less than 2 minutes of your time. Your insights are invaluable in improving ADR reporting practices. We also encourage you to share this study with colleagues to further enhance our understanding.

Thank you for your commitment to advancing patient safety.
