‎[26/11/2024, 08:43:59] Surge: ELIMINATION AGAINST GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE.
*___________________________________________*

🔖The Sixteen Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence is a key international moment to call for an end to violence against women and girls (VAWG).

🔖It runs from 25th November (the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women) until 10th December, Human Rights Day.  

🔖Violence against women happens in every country and culture, causing harm to millions of women and girls.

🔖Risks and challenges to access care increase even more for women and girls living in humanitarian emergencies. 

🔖Around the world today, prolonged and intense conflicts have resulted in a continuous rise in of all forms of gender-based violence.  

🔖The world health organization plays an active role in strengthening health systems and local health partner capacity to prevent and respond to VAWG in humanitarian emergencies.

🔖Additionally, WHO is calling for all parties to respect their obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law to protect women and girls from gender-based violence and ensure access to essential health services.

_Ending violence against women is possible, but only if we act together, now._‼️‼️‼️‼️

[26/11/2024, 20:05:43] Okosodo Joshua Ypgd: If you’re waiting for the perfect moment to launch your plans, you may need to reconsider. Life doesn’t give us the luxury of endless time. The opportunities you have today might not be there tomorrow, and the resources you hold now lose value with every passing second.

I’ve seen people with big dreams—pharmacists in Nigeria, for example—who wanted to pursue graduate studies but insisted on only attending schools in the US. Even when they were admitted to schools in the UK, they refused to enrol because it didn’t align with their original plan. They had good jobs and saved money for their ambitions, but they waited too long. Now, that money has vanished, and even if it were still available, it wouldn’t cover the costs they once hoped it would.

The lesson here is simple: don’t wait too long to act. If you want something, take the steps to get it now. Think of it this way—if you crave suya today and you have the money, don’t wait until tomorrow to buy it. By then, the 500 naira suya you want might shrink in size to what 100 naira could buy today. Inflation, time, and missed chances work against us all.

So make your move. It doesn’t have to be perfect. If it turns out to be a mistake, that’s fine—reassess, adjust, and try again. The most important thing is to act. This is your life, and no one else will live it for you. Take charge, make decisions, and move forward.

Copied.

‎[01/12/2024, 08:52:52] Sir Prof  Pharm Abu Dantani John: 🩸 *World AIDS Day 2024*🩸

📍"The world can end AIDS – if everyone’s rights are protected. With human rights at the centre, with communities in the lead, the world can end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030." _WHO

📍On 1st December ACPN joins partners and communities to commemorate World AIDS Day 2024. Under the theme *“Take the rights path: My health, my right!”,* ACPN is calling on global leaders and citizens to champion the right to health by addressing the inequalities that hinder progress in ending AIDS.

📍Not only on every 1st December, but always, members of ACPN are called to speak up for health equity. Help us ensure that everyone, everywhere, has the right to quality healthcare services in the fight against HIV and AIDS.

📍Everyone should have access to the health services they need, including HIV prevention, treatment and care services when and where they need them. Protecting rights means ensuring that healthcare is available to everyone, without any discrimination, regardless of their HIV status, background, gender, or where they live. 

📍So let the campaign continue!

[03/12/2024, 11:27:38] Surge: *#NowYouKnow Series: Did You Know? ✨*

💡 A Pharmacist Once Served as Nigeria's Minister of Health! 💡

Did you know that Prince Julius Adewale Adelusi-Adeluyi made history as the only pharmacist to ever serve as Nigeria’s Minister of Health? This remarkable milestone is just one of the many groundbreaking achievements in the life of a man who has significantly impacted the fields of pharmacy, healthcare, and public service.

📅 Born on August 2, 1940, Prince Adelusi-Adeluyi graduated in 1965 from the University of Ife (now Obafemi Awolowo University) with a degree in Pharmacy. A Pharmacist and Lawyer, he is the founder and Chairman of Juli Pharmacy Plc, the first indigenously promoted company to be quoted on the Nigerian Stock Exchange in 1986. 💼📈

Prince Adelusi-Adeluyi's leadership journey spans far beyond the pharmacy field. He joined the Rotary Club of Ikeja in 1969 and later became the District Governor-elect for District 210, covering West Africa. 🌍 In 1982, he was elected the first District Governor of Rotary District 911, after carving out Nigeria from District 210. His contributions to the Rotary movement were pivotal, earning him a letter of commendation from President Shehu Shagari for promoting service organizations in Nigeria. 🏅 His efforts were recognized at the Toronto Rotary International Convention in 1983. 🇨🇦

A former Minister of Health and Social Services, Prince Adelusi-Adeluyi’s roles also include being a past Group Chairman of Oodua Investment Conglomerate, a founding Fellow of the Institute of Directors (FIoD), and the pioneer President of the Nigeria Academy of Pharmacy. 🏛️ He has also served as a Fellow of the Nigerian Institute of Management and the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Nigerian-American Chamber of Commerce, among many other notable positions. 🌟

His legacy continues to inspire the next generation of pharmacists and healthcare leaders. 👩‍⚕️👨‍⚕️

‎[04/12/2024, 08:41:14] ~ Dr. Favvy☺️: It is essential to have a well-stocked first-aid kit within easy reach, as a parent. Having the right supplies within reach ahead of time will help you handle any unforeseen emergency. 

Always have a first-aid kit in your home, in your car and when travelling with your family!

You can buy one at any pharmacy or a local Red Cross office nearest to you, or you can just make one of your own. When doing this, use containers that are sturdy, roomy, easy to carry and open. Lunch boxes, plastic tackle boxes, or containers used for storing art supplies can be used because they are lightweight, have handles, and provide a lot of space and separate sections.

•	Build and sustain relationships with stakeholders and regulatory bodies.
•	Address patient and stakeholder concerns while maintaining transparent communication.

•	Medication Management & Dispensing: Ensuring accurate and efficient drug administration.
•	Inventory Management & Drug Forecasting: Maintaining optimal stock levels and forecasting needs.
•	Regulatory Compliance & Quality Assurance: Adhering to legal standards and ensuring high-quality services.
•	Vendor Relationship Management: Building and maintaining strong supplier partnerships.

[21/12/2024, 08:48:01] Surge: This statement beautifully captures the duality of solitude. Here's a deeper exploration:

The Power in Being Alone:

Self-Reflection: Time alone allows for introspection, self-discovery, and personal growth. It’s an opportunity to reconnect with oneself without external distractions.
Creativity and Productivity: Solitude often fosters creativity and concentration, enabling deep work and innovative thinking.
Independence: Embracing solitude builds resilience and a sense of independence, empowering individuals to rely on their inner strength.
The Danger in Loneliness:

Emotional Toll: Prolonged loneliness can lead to feelings of sadness, isolation, and even depression.
Health Implications: Studies have linked chronic loneliness to increased risks of heart disease, weakened immune systems, and mental health challenges.
Social Disconnection: Humans are inherently social beings. Extended loneliness can erode social skills and hinder one’s ability to build or maintain relationships.
This delicate balance reminds us to embrace solitude as a tool for growth while recognizing the importance of meaningful connections to mitigate the risks of loneliness.

The speed wasn’t magic..it was science evolving. The mRNA technology used in COVID vaccines wasn’t invented overnight. It had been under development for decades, and the pandemic provided the urgency (and funding) to scale it up. Plus, regulatory bodies didn’t skip trials....they conducted them in overlapping phases to save time, not cut corners. Saying it was rushed is like calling a plane fast because you didn’t see the years of engineering behind it.

 for the hydroxychloroquine saga. Early reports were anecdotal, not robust clinical evidence. Proper studies, like the RECOVERY trial, showed it didn’t work and even posed risks. Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, is actively funding malaria vaccine programs, and Nigeria is among the pilot countries. As for antimalarials, they’ll still be needed even with a vaccine because vaccines don’t replace treatment ...they prevent future cases. Pharma companies would actually make money selling both.

It’s like updating antivirus software on your computer; new threats require new defenses. If boosters were about cashing out, why not make a “one-and-done” mega-dose? That would’ve been a bigger moneymaker!

Countries signing waivers against litigation isn’t a sinister plot; it’s standard practice during emergencies. Developing and distributing vaccines at pandemic speed is risky, and manufacturers wouldn’t take on that liability without protections. This isn’t unique to COVID—similar frameworks existed for Ebola vaccines and other global health emergencies. It’s about ensuring action in crises, not hiding shady intentions.

Any medical intervention, even paracetamol, carries risks. Serious vaccine side effects are exceedingly rare—less than 1 in a million for most. If companies had sinister intentions, they wouldn’t report adverse effects publicly, yet you can easily find them in safety databases. Transparency is a key part of the process.

The vaccines saved millions of lives and prevented healthcare systems from collapsing. It’s not perfect, but it’s a net positive. Calling it a conspiracy because of rare side effects is like saying cars are a conspiracy because of accidents—ignore the 99.9% who get to their destination safely.

As the year 2024 draws to an end, I take much  pleasure on behalf of PSN Edo State, to send heartiest good wishes and warm season greetings to all our esteemed members. 

At Christmas, we reflect on the humble, symbolic and divine birth of Jesus Christ. We reflect on his message of hope, compassion, salvation, reconciliation, forgiveness and peace.

The sound of hymns, exchange of gifts and best wishes that characterized the celebration of the festive holiday, also provide us the much needed courage, aspiration and commitment to create a better society in which all humans are treated equally, virtuously and with dignity.

[31/12/2024, 15:33:41] Pharm. Austin YPGd: December 31, 2024

*Dear YPG EDO,*

As we close the year 2024, we (Job Advocacy and Employment Committee) want to take a moment to express our heartfelt gratitude for the opportunity to serve the Edo State Young Pharmacist Group (YPG-Edo) in the capacity of Job Advocacy and Employment Mediation. 
It has been an incredible journey, marked by collaboration, innovation, and our shared commitment to addressing employment challenges within our profession as it relates to Young Pharmacists (YPs), particularly in the private sector.

Your support, dedication, and ideas have been instrumental in driving our initiatives forward. Together, we have made strides toward creating opportunities and advocating for better prospects for YPs. 

While there is still much to be done, with your continued engagement, we can achieve even greater success in the coming year.

As I said during the salary review meeting, we should begin to think of prophylaxis rather than treatment in our approach to addressing our challenges. For instance, I will suggest that the keyword for YPs in 2025 should be:  
> "Be intentional about where you work." 
The employer needs the employee and vice versa. Therefore, no one should take advantage of the other. The employers MUST be willing and ready to adequately remunerate the YPs, just as the YPs MUST commit to providing value-added services. Beyond remuneration, the workspace must be toxicity-free from both parties.

Therefore, YPs must be intentional about their terms of engagement. The YPG-Edo Employer-Employee agreement is a draft and a skeleton that is adjustable to meet the terms of your employment. Before we start going to the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria office for 2025 registration, ensure that the agreement is modified to reflect your desired and agreed terms of engagement for 2025. Every agreement should and must be documented and signed by both parties. Avoid shalaye in 2025. 

Additionally, do not take a job in 2025 without speaking with the previous Superintendent Pharmacist. 

It is critical that you know who you are committing to working with for the next 365 days. Resigning in the middle of the year is a journey no one wants to embark on. Jumping in is easy, but coming out is an uphill task. 

JAEC and YPG-Edo EXCO will ensure that they provide you with the contacts of those you need to talk to. If we can address the issue of YPs jumping on anything that appears in the nomenclature of “job,” some of these issues will be resolved seamlessly. 
> "Be intentional about where you work." 

Finally, we urge YPs to do more in the area of networking and collaboration in the coming year. Attend YPG, ALPs, ACPN, and PSN meetings. Be known, and know your colleagues, especially those saddled with the responsibility of leading you. 

Have the contact of the Chairmen and Secretaries of the above-mentioned societies. Pay your dues. Know the laws that apply to your practice space. Be informed. Rest assured that the JAEC will always be here for you.

Thank you for trusting us to serve you. We look forward to another year of impactful teamwork and progress.
Wishing you all a prosperous and fulfilling new year.
Warm regards,


*Aigbagenode Aiyebor Augustine, _Pharm.D_* 
Committee Head
Young Pharmacist Group Job Advocacy and Employment Committee
Edo State.

*ALPS  NATIONAL DUES IS N4000.00*

Dear colleagues,
Greetings from the National Secretariat of ALPs..
Compliments of the season.
Our parent body, the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria PSN, has approved two platforms for the payment of dues....
*Pharmapay* and *Pharmagetaway*


These are online payment platforms and all dues for the various technical and interest groups are paid through it.  


ALPs state chapters should submit their branch accounts to the PSN of their state for upload on the platform.

Once dues are paid the alert receiver gets it..

It's quite convenient to use though a little processing charge applies.  But the convenience is much better.( No need for multiple bank visits in these days of high fuel cost)

National dues is *N4000.00*

Ensure you see this and the amount when you log in on either site.
These two sites takes you to the approved platforms 

www.pharmagateway.com.ng

https.pharmpay.brainstorm.ng


Please kindly pay your dues using this mode..


However should you have need for the national account details 

0693128098
ACCESS BANK
ASSOCIATION OF LADY PHARMACISTS.


Thanks for your cooperation and service to ALPs .
We wish a rewarding and fulfilling 2025.


Best Regards,

Pharm. Regina M. Chichi- Agir FPCPharm

[10/01/2025, 18:17:15] King Penet: A locum pharmacist is a temporary or contract pharmacist who works on a short-term basis, often filling in for a permanent pharmacist who is absent or on leave. Locum pharmacists may work in various settings, including community pharmacies, hospitals, or clinics. The key characteristics of a superintendent pharmacist include strong leadership and management skills, excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and the ability to make strategic decisions.

[12/01/2025, 15:16:45] Daniel Adulphus Ypgd: this one no good at all o...

I don't know how the SP tracks stock.. I know many people use electronic tracking, but I'm a big fan of manual tracking..

I use a notebook system, and twice every year I personally check every drug stock in the premise for their expiry dates (also helps me monitor the arrangement of stock on the shelf with regards FEFO). For the next 1 year, I have the list of every item expiry expiring in my premise. Nothing expires without me being aware from time.. Something that will expire like say in 6 months time with excess quantities, I already set it up to be moved from time. I always tell my MD (who covers the evenings when I'm off duty) the brands of a class of drug (antimalarial, antibiotic, etcetera) that is next to expire, and we collectively move it. We know the brands to focus on right now, after which we know the next brand to face.. This also helps in procurement.

I develop my system many years ago, and this usually makes me invaluable anywhere I work.

[14/01/2025, 11:14:18] Idara Pcxx: Redman syndrome, also known as "Red Neck Syndrome," is a rare but potentially serious side effect associated with vancomycin, a commonly used antibiotic.

Symptoms
Redman syndrome typically presents with:

1. _Erythema_: Redness of the upper body, including the face, neck, and chest.
2. _Pruritus_: Itching or burning sensation in the affected areas.
3. _Wheezing or dyspnea_: Difficulty breathing or wheezing.

Causes
Redman syndrome is thought to be caused by:

1. _Rapid infusion_: Vancomycin administered too quickly, leading to high peak levels.
2. _High doses_: Exceeding recommended vancomycin doses.

Treatment
If you suspect Redman syndrome,:

1. _Stop the infusion_: Immediately discontinue vancomycin administration.
2. _Administer antihistamines_: Diphenhydramine or other antihistamines to alleviate symptoms.
3. _Use corticosteroids_: In severe cases, corticosteroids may be necessary.

Prevention
To minimize the risk of Redman syndrome:

1. _Follow recommended dosing_: Adhere to established vancomycin dosing guidelines.
2. _Infuse slowly_: Administer vancomycin over at least 60 minutes.
3. _Monitor patients closely_: Watch for signs of Redman syndrome during and after vancomycin infusion.

Vancomycin is an essential antibiotic, and with proper administration and monitoring, the risk of Redman syndrome can be minimized.

[15/01/2025, 12:30:48] Pharm Mike Graceville Pharmacy (dreamlife): Here are some examples of male contraception:

Hormonal Methods
1. *Male Birth Control Pill*: Similar to the female birth control pill, this method uses hormones to prevent sperm production. (Still in clinical trials)
2. *Male Birth Control Injection*: An injectable form of hormones that prevent sperm production. (Still in clinical trials)

Barrier Methods
1. *Condoms*: Worn over the penis to prevent sperm from reaching the egg.
2. *Male Diaphragm*: A silicone dome inserted into the penis to prevent sperm from reaching the egg.

Surgical Methods
1. *Vasectomy*: A surgical procedure that cuts and seals the vas deferens, preventing sperm from reaching the semen.
2. *Vasalgel*: A non-surgical, reversible procedure that blocks the vas deferens with a gel-like substance.

Other Methods

[17/01/2025, 11:48:21] King Penet: *Observations on the Correlation Between Chronic Dental Issues, Cardiovascular Health, and Erectile Dysfunction* 

*By Prof. Kayode Oseni*

As a clinician with over 30 years of experience in patient care, I have had the opportunity to observe recurring patterns that warrant further discussion and exploration within the field of natural medicine. Specifically, I have noted significant correlations between chronic dental issues, cardiovascular health, and erectile dysfunction in men, which may offer valuable insights into integrated treatment approaches.

1. *Chronic Dental Issues and Cardiovascular Problems:*
   Through my clinical practice, it has become evident that men suffering from chronic dental issues, particularly periodontal disease, frequently develop cardiovascular problems later in life. The underlying connection seems to stem from shared risk factors—such as inflammation, bacterial proliferation, and systemic health—often exacerbated by poor oral hygiene. These chronic dental issues appear to serve as both a marker and a potential precursor for cardiovascular disease.

2. *Chronic Cardiovascular Issues and Erectile Dysfunction:*
   Similarly, I have observed that men with chronic cardiovascular conditions consistently develop erectile dysfunction as a secondary complication. The impairments in vascular health caused by cardiovascular diseases directly impact penile perfusion, leading to difficulties with erectile function. This relationship underscores the importance of recognizing erectile dysfunction not only as a sexual health issue but also as a potential indicator of broader cardiovascular health status.

 Implications for Natural Medicine

Given these observations, it is crucial for practitioners of natural medicine to consider the interconnections between these health conditions. Addressing oral health may play a vital role in preventing cardiovascular disease, while simultaneously, treating cardiovascular health can help mitigate the incidence of erectile dysfunction. 

 Recommendations
- *Holistic Assessment:*
  Clinicians should conduct comprehensive assessments that include evaluating oral health, cardiovascular risk factors, and sexual health, allowing for a more integrated treatment plan.

- *Intervention Strategies:*
  Promoting proper oral hygiene, dietary changes, and lifestyle modifications can be beneficial. Additionally, early intervention in cardiovascular health can prevent or alleviate the progression of erectile dysfunction.

- *Patient Education:*
  Educating patients about the connections among dental health, cardiovascular health, and erectile dysfunction can empower them to take proactive steps in managing their health.

In conclusion, the relationships between chronic dental issues, cardiovascular diseases, and erectile dysfunction present an opportunity for the natural medicine community to adopt a more holistic and integrative approach to patient care.

I encourage further discussion and research into these patterns to enhance our understanding and improve treatment outcomes for our patients.

𝑾𝒆 𝒂𝒓𝒆 𝒕𝒊𝒓𝒆𝒅 𝒐𝒇 𝒔𝒆𝒆𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂 𝒔𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒕 𝒘𝒊𝒕𝒉 𝒅𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏𝒔 𝒊𝒏 𝑷𝒉𝒚𝒔𝒊𝒄𝒔 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝑪𝒉𝒆𝒎𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒓𝒚, 𝒃𝒖𝒕 𝒌𝒏𝒐𝒘𝒔 𝒏𝒐𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂𝒃𝒐𝒖𝒕 𝒄𝒉𝒆𝒎𝒊𝒄𝒂𝒍 𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏𝒔 𝒐𝒓 𝒆𝒏𝒆𝒓𝒈𝒚 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒔𝒊𝒐𝒏.

𝑺𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒘𝒊𝒕𝒉 𝒅𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏𝒔 𝒊𝒏 𝑳𝒊𝒕𝒆𝒓𝒂𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆, 𝑮𝒐𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒏𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒕 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝑪𝑹𝑺/ *IRS* , 𝒚𝒆𝒕 𝒃𝒍𝒂𝒏𝒌 𝒐𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒅𝒊𝒇𝒇𝒆𝒓𝒆𝒏𝒄𝒆𝒔 𝒃𝒆𝒕𝒘𝒆𝒆𝒏 𝑫𝒓𝒂𝒎𝒂 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝑷𝒓𝒐𝒔𝒆 𝑭𝒊𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏, 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒇𝒐𝒓𝒎𝒔 𝒐𝒇 𝑮𝒐𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒏𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒕 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒊𝒈𝒏𝒊𝒇𝒊𝒄𝒂𝒏𝒄𝒆 𝒐𝒇 𝑹𝒆𝒍𝒊𝒈𝒊𝒐𝒖𝒔 𝒔𝒕𝒐𝒓𝒊𝒆𝒔.

𝑾𝒆 𝒉𝒂𝒅 𝒕𝒐 𝒂𝒔𝒌 𝒔𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒔𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒔𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒚𝒆𝒂𝒓𝒔 𝒃𝒂𝒄𝒌 𝒕𝒐 𝒍𝒐𝒐𝒌 𝒇𝒐𝒓 𝒂 𝒕𝒖𝒕𝒐𝒓𝒊𝒂𝒍 𝒕𝒆𝒂𝒄𝒉𝒆𝒓 𝒕𝒐 𝒉𝒆𝒍𝒑 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒎 𝒘𝒊𝒕𝒉 𝑱𝑺3 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝑺𝑺1 𝑴𝒂𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒎𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒔, 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒘𝒉𝒐𝒍𝒆 16 𝒐𝒇 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒎 𝒊𝒏 𝑬𝒏𝒈𝒊𝒏𝒆𝒆𝒓𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒄𝒍𝒂𝒔𝒔 𝒘𝒊𝒕𝒉 𝒆𝒙𝒄𝒆𝒍𝒍𝒆𝒏𝒕 𝑺𝑺𝑪𝑬 𝒓𝒆𝒔𝒖𝒍𝒕𝒔 𝒂𝒓𝒆 𝒗𝒊𝒔𝒊𝒃𝒍𝒚 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒇𝒖𝒔𝒆𝒅 𝒂𝒕 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒊𝒈𝒉𝒕 𝒐𝒇 𝒂𝒏𝒚 𝑨𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒉𝒎𝒆𝒕𝒊𝒄 𝒘𝒐𝒓𝒌.
𝑻𝒉𝒆𝒊𝒓 𝒍𝒂𝒔𝒕 𝒔𝒆𝒎𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒓'𝒔 𝒑𝒆𝒓𝒇𝒐𝒓𝒎𝒂𝒏𝒄𝒆 𝒃𝒆𝒕𝒓𝒂𝒚𝒆𝒅 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒂𝒍 𝑨1'𝒔 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝑩3'𝒔 𝒐𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒊𝒓 𝑾𝑨𝑬𝑪 𝑹𝒆𝒔𝒖𝒍𝒕𝒔 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒄𝒂𝒓𝒓𝒚 𝒂𝒃𝒐𝒖𝒕 𝒇𝒐𝒓 𝒂𝒅𝒎𝒊𝒔𝒔𝒊𝒐𝒏.
𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒂𝒎𝒆 𝒂𝒑𝒑𝒍𝒊𝒆𝒔 𝒕𝒐 𝒂𝒍𝒍 𝒅𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒕𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒊𝒏 𝑼𝒏𝒊𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒔𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒆𝒔.

𝑻𝒉𝒆𝒔𝒆 𝒔𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒚𝒐𝒖 𝒉𝒆𝒍𝒑 𝒂𝒄𝒒𝒖𝒊𝒓𝒆 𝒈𝒓𝒂𝒅𝒆𝒔 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒄𝒂𝒏𝒏𝒐𝒕 𝒅𝒆𝒇𝒆𝒏𝒅, 𝒂𝒓𝒆 𝒖𝒔𝒖𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒚 𝒇𝒓𝒖𝒔𝒕𝒓𝒂𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒊𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑰𝒗𝒐𝒓𝒚 𝑻𝒐𝒘𝒆𝒓. 

𝑺𝒂𝒗𝒆 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒎 𝒂 𝒗𝒐𝒚𝒂𝒈𝒆 𝒐𝒇 𝒑𝒂𝒊𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒓𝒆𝒈𝒓𝒆𝒕𝒔 𝒊𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒇𝒖𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆 𝒃𝒚 𝒆𝒏𝒔𝒖𝒓𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒂𝒓𝒆 𝒘𝒆𝒍𝒍 𝒕𝒖𝒕𝒐𝒓𝒆𝒅 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒐𝒘𝒆𝒅 𝒕𝒐 𝒑𝒓𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒆 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒘𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒆 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒊𝒓 𝒆𝒙𝒂𝒎𝒊𝒏𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏𝒔 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒎𝒔𝒆𝒍𝒗𝒆𝒔 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒖𝒏𝒂𝒊𝒅𝒆𝒅.

𝑯𝒆𝒍𝒑 𝒖𝒔 𝒕𝒐 𝒉𝒆𝒍𝒑 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒔𝒆 𝒔𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔. 𝑻𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒂𝒓𝒆 𝒐𝒏𝒍𝒚 𝒖𝒔𝒆𝒅 𝒕𝒐 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒎𝒐𝒕𝒆 𝒕𝒉𝒐𝒔𝒆 𝑺𝒄𝒉𝒐𝒐𝒍𝒔. 𝑰𝒕'𝒔 𝒄𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒐𝒖𝒔, 𝒘𝒊𝒄𝒌𝒆𝒅𝒏𝒆𝒔𝒔, 𝒔𝒆𝒍𝒇𝒊𝒔𝒉𝒏𝒆𝒔𝒔 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒖𝒏𝒇𝒂𝒊𝒓 𝒕𝒐 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒇𝒖𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆 𝒐𝒇 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒔𝒆 𝒔𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔.

𝑻𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒊𝒔 𝒘𝒉𝒚 𝒔𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒅𝒆𝒔𝒑𝒆𝒓𝒂𝒕𝒆 𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒄𝒉𝒂𝒏𝒈𝒆 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒊𝒓 𝒄𝒉𝒊𝒍𝒅𝒓𝒆𝒏'𝒔 𝒔𝒄𝒉𝒐𝒐𝒍 𝒕𝒐 "𝑷𝒖𝒔𝒉-𝑼𝒑" 𝑺𝒄𝒉𝒐𝒐𝒍𝒔 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒈𝒆𝒕 𝒕𝒐 𝑺𝑺 𝑪𝒍𝒂𝒔𝒔𝒆𝒔 𝒕𝒐𝒘𝒂𝒓𝒅𝒔 𝑾𝑨𝑬𝑪/𝑵𝑬𝑪𝑶/𝑱𝑨𝑴𝑩, 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒔𝒆 𝒑𝒂re𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒌𝒏𝒐𝒘𝒔 𝒂𝒍𝒍 𝒕𝒉𝒆 "𝑷𝒖𝒔𝒉-𝑼𝒑 𝑺𝒄𝒉𝒐𝒐𝒍𝒔 𝒘𝒊𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒊𝒓 𝒂𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒔, 𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒇𝒂𝒓 𝒂𝒘𝒂𝒚 𝑺𝒄𝒉𝒐𝒐𝒍𝒔.
𝑻𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒖𝒔𝒖𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒚 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒑𝒍𝒂𝒊𝒏, 𝒈𝒓𝒖𝒎𝒃𝒍𝒆, 𝒓𝒂𝒏𝒕 𝒐𝒓 𝒘𝒂𝒊𝒍 𝒂𝒃𝒐𝒖𝒕 𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂𝒕 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒊𝒓 𝑪𝒉𝒊𝒍𝒅𝒓𝒆𝒏'𝒔 𝒑𝒓𝒆𝒔𝒆𝒏𝒕 𝑺𝒄𝒉𝒐𝒐𝒍 𝒊𝒏 𝒑𝒓𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒆𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒕𝒐 𝒄𝒉𝒂𝒏𝒈𝒆 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒎 𝒕𝒐 𝒕𝒉𝒆 "𝑷𝒖𝒔𝒉-𝑼𝒑" 𝑺𝒄𝒉𝒐𝒐𝒍𝒔. 

𝑾𝒉𝒆𝒏 𝒚𝒐𝒖 𝒅𝒐 𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒇𝒐𝒓 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒎 𝒂𝒕 𝑺𝒆𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒅𝒂𝒓𝒚 𝑺𝒄𝒉𝒐𝒐𝒍 𝒍𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒍, 𝒘𝒊𝒍𝒍 𝒚𝒐𝒖 𝒂𝒍𝒔𝒐 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒄𝒆𝒆𝒅 𝒕𝒐 𝒅𝒐 𝒔𝒂𝒎𝒆 𝒂𝒕 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒊𝒓 𝑼𝒏𝒊𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒔𝒊𝒕𝒚 𝒍𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒍?

𝑻𝒉𝒆𝒏, 𝒊𝒇 𝒊𝒕 𝒅𝒐𝒆𝒔 𝒏𝒐𝒕 𝒘𝒐𝒓𝒌 𝒂𝒄𝒄𝒐𝒓𝒅𝒊𝒏𝒈𝒍𝒚, 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒆𝒂𝒔𝒊𝒍𝒚 𝒋𝒐𝒊𝒏 𝒄𝒂𝒎𝒑𝒖𝒔 𝒀𝒂𝒉𝒐𝒐, *_𝑪𝒖𝒍𝒕ism group_* 𝑺𝒍𝒂𝒚 𝑸𝒖𝒆𝒆𝒏𝒔, 𝑳𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆𝒓𝒔 𝑺𝒑𝒆𝒄𝒔, 𝒆𝒕𝒄.

[23/01/2025, 09:46:15] Pharm Osakponmwen Oviasogie: *PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENT*

*NATIONAL HEALTH FELLOWS PROGRAM*

The Edo State Ministry of Health is pleased to announce the call for applications for the National Health Fellows Program of the Federal Government through the SWAP Coordination Office of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare. 

*Program Overview:*
The National Health Fellows Program aims to enhance the capacity of young professionals in the health sector, promoting innovative solutions to address the country's health challenges.

*Eligibility Criteria:*
*For Edo State Applicants:* 
To be eligible for the program, applicants must meet the following criteria : 
* must be between ages 25 and 35 years 
* Bachelors degree(health related, IT, or social Science). 
* Demonstrable interest /or experience in Public health or health related NGO and partner organization OR community projects that demonstrate leadership and initiative 
* Candidates must not be currently engaged as the position is for full time support 
* Candidates must be an indigene of Edo State. 
* Candidates must reside in their local Government Area of Origin. 
* Candidates must possess smartphones with data capabilities i.e for WhatsApp, Zoom etc. 
* Recommendation from the University Dean or NYSC place of Primary assignment or a respected Organization demonstrating character and Leadership 
* Demonstrate analytical skills and entrepreneurial drive. 

*Application Instructions:*
* Visit : www.healthfellows.ng to begin your application. 
* Ensure you meet the programme's requirements. 
* Provide all necessary details and complete the online application.
* Await feedback on your application 
* Shortlisted candidates will be notified and provided with details on the next steps. 



*Deadline for Application:*
The deadline for application submission is 27th January, 2025. 

*Selection Process:*
A competitive selection process will be conducted to identify successful applicants. 

*Signed*: *SWAP D.O*
 
 *For: Honorable Commissioner for Health*

Dear Young Pharmacists,

🔖We wish to bring to your notice about the launch of the National Health Fellows program initiated by the coordinating Minister for the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare; Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate.

🔖The *National Health Fellows Program*, approved by President Tinubu, is a *1-year paid, hands-on initiative* by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare (FMoH&SW). Fellows will be placed in all 774 Local Government Areas across Nigeria.  

🔖This program aims to train emerging professionals through mentorship and leadership opportunities, contributing to the *Health Sector Renewal and Investment Initiative (RII)*.  

📍 *Benefits*:  
- Paid fellowship  
- Hands-on experience  
- Nationwide placement  
- Leadership and mentorship opportunities  

🖥️ *Apply here*: https://healthfellows.ng
🗓️ *Deadline*: 27th January, 2025

                                                                                                 Federal Civil Service Commission Is Not Recruiting Right Now
                                                                                                                         The attention of the Federal Civil Service Commission (FCSC) has been drawn to information making the rounds on various media platforms about advertised vacancies and recruitments in the Commission.

Early dental care plays a very vital role in the dental health and overall well-being of our children. As parents and caregivers, it is important to understand the significance of prioritizing pediatric dental care to ensure your child’s optimal dental development and long-term oral health.

Establishing a healthy oral routine ensures a lifetime of strong, healthy teeth and helps keep your children’s smiles beautiful. It also helps them develop a positive attitude towards oral hygiene and reduces the likelihood of dental anxiety.

However, neglecting it can have potential long-term implications, like, gum disease, tooth loss, and even systemic health issues like cardiovascular disease.

Still, life with kids can seem unpredictable. So, how do you build good oral hygiene habits? Or, what do you do when a dental emergency happens?

World Cancer  day is an international day observed 4th of February to raise awareness about cancer, encourage its prevention and mobilize actions to address the global Cancer epidermic

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide. In Nigeria, the statistics are equally grim, with approximately 127,000 new cases and 79,000 cancer-related deaths reported in 2022.  

On this year’s World Cancer Day themed United by Unique, which is a reminder of the collective commitment against cancer, WHO acknowledges every patient’s unique experiences and the value of people-centered care delivered jointly by healthcare providers, families, friends and community.

The cancer burden continues to grow globally, exerting tremendous physical, emotional and financial strain on individuals, families, communities and health systems.

Its important as pharmacist and as individual we unite to raise awareness about the need for people -centered care. [06/02/2025, 19:07:44] Surge: *🇳🇬Dora Akunyili: The Pharmacist Who Took on the Drug Cartels—and Paid the Price!💥*

_Dora Nkem Akunyili was born on July 14, 1954, in Makurdi, Benue State, Nigeria, but hailed from Anambra State. She was a brilliant student, earning a first-class degree in Pharmacy from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN). Her academic excellence paved the way for a career in pharmacology, public health, and regulatory affairs._

*The NAFDAC Revolution: A War Against Fake Drugs 💪💪*

```In 2001, President Olusegun Obasanjo appointed Akunyili as the Director-General of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC).``` 

```At the time, Nigeria was drowning in counterfeit drugs, with an estimated 60-70% of medicines in circulation being fake or substandard😳.```

*🚨 Key Challenges She Faced:*
• Drug cartels were running a multi-billion naira fake drug industry.
• Corrupt officials were complicit, making regulation difficult.
• Fake drugs had caused thousands of deaths, particularly among children and pregnant women.

*🔥Dora’s Bold Actions:*
• She led massive raids on markets selling fake drugs.
• Shut down dozens of illegal drug factories across Nigeria.
• Fought against powerful counterfeit drug syndicates that had operated unchecked for years.
• Pushed for stricter drug importation and registration policies.

*💥 The Assassination Attempts:*

Dora's fight against counterfeit drugs earned her death threats. 

In 2003, gunmen sprayed her car with bullets in an assassination attempt, but she miraculously survived but her gele (headscarf was damaged).

Despite this, she refused to back down, telling Nigerians:
“If I die fighting fake drugs, I will be happy to go to heaven knowing I saved lives.”

*International Recognition & Later Years*

*Her fearless work gained her global recognition:*

🏅 In 2005, she won the TIME Magazine "Heroes of Our Time" Award.
🏅 She received the Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR) honor.
🏅 Earned more than 900 local and international awards—the highest by any Nigerian woman.

Later, she became the Minister of Information and Communications (2008-2010), where she championed the “Re-brand Nigeria” campaign.

*The Battle with Cancer and Death ❤️*

In 2013, Dora was diagnosed with ovarian cancer. Despite undergoing surgeries and treatments in India and the US, she eventually lost the battle. She died on June 7, 2014, at the age of 59.

Her legacy lives on as a symbol of integrity, courage, and selfless service in Nigeria’s health sector.

💡 Why Dora Akunyili’s Story Still Matters Today

• Fake drugs remain a global problem—her story is a reminder of the need for vigilance.
• ⁠She showed that pharmacists are not just drug dispensers but frontline defenders of public health.
• Her fight against corruption proves that one person can make a difference, even against powerful enemies.

📢 What do you think? Should more pharmacists be actively involved in policymaking like Dora Akunyili? Let’s discuss! ⬇️

Determine the nature of the premise if it's wholesale or retail

Go on https://pay.pcn.gov.ng and pay the amount that pertains to the nature of your premise. Wholesale is 150k..  retail is 10k

Print the receipt of payment 

Go on https://pharmagateway.com.ng and pay the relevant dues which must include the Acpn dues in this case.

Download the soft copy of the receipt 

Go to https://www.psnedo.com upload the receipt and request for clearance. 

Once cleared print the clearance slip

Once cleared print the clearance slip

[14/02/2025, 20:42:30] Mamabasii: Pharmaceutical care is a patient-centered approach to pharmacy practice that focuses on the provision of medication therapy management and other health-related services to achieve optimal patient outcomes.

Key Elements of Pharmaceutical Care
1. *Patient assessment*: The pharmacist assesses the patient's medication therapy needs, including their medical history, current medications, and health goals.
2. *Medication therapy management*: The pharmacist works with the patient and their healthcare team to develop a personalized medication plan, including selecting, dosing, and monitoring medications.
3. *Medication counseling*: The pharmacist educates the patient on the safe and effective use of their medications, including potential side effects and interactions.
4. *Monitoring and follow-up*: The pharmacist regularly monitors the patient's medication therapy and adjusts the plan as needed to ensure optimal outcomes.
5. *Collaboration with healthcare team*: The pharmacist works with other healthcare professionals to ensure comprehensive care and coordination of services.

[19/02/2025, 17:31:11] ~ ospx: *How to carry out premises registration for the year*

Determine the nature of the premise if it's wholesale or retail

Go on https://pay.pcn.gov.ng and pay the amount that pertains to the nature of your premise. Wholesale is 150k..  retail is 10k

Print the receipt of payment 

Go on https://pharmagateway.com.ng and pay the relevant dues which must include the Acpn dues in this case.

Download the soft copy of the receipt 

Go to https://www.psnedo.com upload the receipt and request for clearance. 

Once cleared print the clearance slip 

Go to https://acpnedo.macrosxp.com upload the receipt and request for clearance 

Once cleared print the clearance slip

Gather all the printouts with your application for renewal and go to the council for registration.
[19/02/2025, 18:23:27] Daniel Adulphus Ypgd: *ROLES OF A SUPERINTENDENT PHARMACIST*
▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

🔖Many pharmacists take on the role of Superintendent Pharmacist without fully understanding the scope of responsibilities that come with the position. 

🔖As a result, they may find themselves overwhelmed or uncertain about how to fulfill their duties. 

🔖Having a clear understanding of the roles and responsibilities of a Superintendent Pharmacist is crucial, not only for success in the role, but also for negotiating fair compensation.

🔖By knowing the expectations and impact of the position, pharmacists can effectively advocate for their worth and negotiate a salary that reflects their value.

🔖Furthermore, this knowledge helps pharmacists understand their impact on the organization, patients, and the profession as a whole, enabling them to make informed decisions and prioritize their efforts.

🔖 In reality, the role of Superintendent Pharmacist is multifaceted and requires a broad range of skills and knowledge.

1. *Professional Leadership*
Provide professional leadership and guidance to pharmacy staff, ensuring that all staff members are aware of their roles and responsibilities.

2. *Pharmaceutical Services*
Ensure that pharmaceutical services are provided to patients in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and standards, including the provision of medication, advice, and counseling.

3. *Medicines Management*
Oversee the management of medicines, including the procurement, storage, and dispensing of medications, to ensure that patients receive safe and effective treatments.

4. *Patient Safety*
Ensure that patient safety is prioritized, by implementing procedures for reporting and learning from errors, and by providing guidance to staff on patient safety best practices.

5. *Licensing and Regulatory Compliance*
Ensure that the pharmacy operates in compliance with all relevant laws, regulations, and standards, including those related to pharmacy licensing, pharmacy practice, medicines management, and patient safety.

6. *Staff Management and Training*
Manage and supervise pharmacy staff, providing training and guidance on pharmacy procedures, patient safety, and regulatory compliance.

7. *Quality Assurance*
Implement and maintain a quality assurance system to ensure that pharmaceutical services are provided to patients in accordance with relevant standards and guidelines.

8. *Patient Counseling*
Provide patient counseling and advice on medication use, ensuring that patients understand how to use their medications safely and effectively.

9. *Medication Review*
Conduct medication reviews to ensure that patients are receiving optimal treatment, and to identify opportunities for improving patient outcomes.

10. *Interprofessional Collaboration*
Collaborate with other healthcare professionals to ensure that patients receive comprehensive and coordinated care.

11. *Business Management*
Oversee the business operations of the pharmacy, including financial management, inventory control, and marketing.

12. *Continuous Professional Development*
Participate in continuous professional development to stay up-to-date with the latest developments in pharmacy practice, and to maintain professional competence.

13. *Risk Management*
Identify and manage risks associated with pharmacy practice, including patient safety risks, regulatory compliance risks, and business risks.

14. *Audit and Inspection*
Prepare for and respond to audits and inspections by regulatory authorities, ensuring that all necessary documentation and records are available and up-to-date.

15. *Complaints Handling*
Develop and implement procedures for handling patient complaints, ensuring that complaints are investigated promptly and that patients receive a satisfactory response.

16. *Professional Association Participation*
Participate in activities of professional associations, including:

- Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN)

- Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN)

- Interest groups (e.g. YPG, ALPS, CPAN)

- Attend zonal, state, national, and international meetings and conferences.

- Contribute to the development of policies and guidelines for pharmacy practice.

- Network with other pharmacists and healthcare professionals to share best practices and stay up-to-date with the latest developments in pharmacy practice.

*Conclusion*
🔖In conclusion, the role of Superintendent Pharmacist is complex and demanding, requiring a broad range of skills, knowledge, and experience. 

🔖By understanding the roles and responsibilities of a Superintendent Pharmacist, pharmacists can better prepare themselves for the challenges and opportunities of this critical leadership position. 

🔖Effective performance in this role is essential for ensuring the safe and effective delivery of pharmaceutical services, maintaining regulatory compliance, and advancing the profession of pharmacy in Nigeria.

*Dr. Ehitare Patrick Omoarebu*
*Assistant National Secretary*
*PHARMACEUTICAL SOCIETY OF NIGERIA*

‎[09/03/2025, 12:47:58] Idara Pcxx: Theme for World glaucoma day 2025

 *Uniting for a* *Glaucoma-Free World".* ‎image omitted
[09/03/2025, 12:50:13] Idara Pcxx: Glaucoma is an eye condition that damages the optic nerve. This damage can lead to vision loss or blindness. The optic nerve sends visual information from your eye to the brain and is vital for good vision. Damage to the optic nerve is often related to high pressure in the eye. But glaucoma can happen even with typical eye pressure.

Glaucoma can happen at any age but is more common in older adults. It is one of the leading causes of blindness for people over the age of 60.

Many forms of glaucoma have no warning signs. The effect is so gradual that you may not notice a change in vision until the condition is in its later stages.

It's important to have regular eye exams that include measurements of your eye pressure. If glaucoma is found early, vision loss can be slowed or prevented. If you have glaucoma, you'll need treatment or monitoring for the rest of your life.


The symptoms of glaucoma depend on the type and stage of the condition.

 *Open-angle glaucoma* 
No symptoms in early stages.
Gradually, patchy blind spots in your side vision. Side vision also is called peripheral vision.
In later stages, difficulty seeing things in your central vision.


 *Acute angle-closure* *glaucoma* 
Bad headache.
Severe eye pain.
Nausea or vomiting.
Blurred vision.
Halos or colored rings around lights.
Eye redness.


 *Normal-tension glaucoma* 
No symptoms in early stages.
Gradually, blurred vision.
In later stages, loss of side vision.


 *Glaucoma in children* 
A dull or cloudy eye (infants).
Increased blinking (infants).
Tears without crying (infants).
Blurred vision.
Nearsightedness that gets worse.
Headache.



 *Pigmentary glaucoma* 
Halos around lights.
Blurred vision with exercise.
Gradual loss of side vision.

[17/03/2025, 22:18:47] dreze016 Ypgd: A Dangerous Precedent: The Flawed Judgment Against Sunday Jackson

The Supreme Court’s decision to uphold the death sentence of Sunday Jackson is not only a miscarriage of justice but also a dangerous precedent that criminalizes self-defense and emboldens lawlessness in Nigeria.

Jackson, a farmer and student from Dong Community in Demsa LGA, Adamawa State, was attacked on his own farm by Buba Ardo Bawuro, a herdsman who trespassed and deliberately allowed his cattle to destroy Jackson’s crops. When challenged, Bawuro pulled out a knife and stabbed Jackson, prompting a struggle in which Jackson, despite being injured, managed to overpower and fatally wound his attacker in self-defense.

The courts, instead of recognizing his right to protect himself, sentenced him to death under Section 211 of the Penal Code, a punishment meant for intentional and premeditated murder, not for someone acting in self-defense.

A Flawed Judgment & Its Dangerous Implications

1. Criminalizing Self-Defense

The trial judge, Fatima Ahmed Tafida, shockingly ruled that Jackson should have run away instead of defending himself—even though he had already been stabbed! How does an injured person outrun an aggressive attacker armed with a knife? This reasoning is not just flawed; it is absurd and dangerous.

If this ruling is allowed to stand, it sends a clear message to Nigerians: If you are attacked, you must accept your fate, no matter how unjust or violent. The implication is that victims must either submit to being killed or risk execution by the very system that is supposed to protect them.

2. Bias & Selective Justice

For eight years, the Buhari administration turned a blind eye to the atrocities committed by armed Fulani herdsmen, who murdered thousands of innocent Nigerians and destroyed entire communities. Not one of these killers was brought to justice. Not one was sentenced to death. Yet, a farmer who defended himself against an attacker on his own land is being hanged? This exposes the hypocrisy and ethnic bias in Nigeria’s justice system.

This is not about religion or ethnicity; it is about justice and fairness. When the law is applied selectively, it becomes a tool of oppression rather than protection.

3. The Impact on Farmers & National Security

This judgment will only embolden criminal herders who invade farms with impunity, knowing that farmers cannot fight back without facing execution. Farmers are already vulnerable due to insecurity and lack of government support. If they are now legally barred from defending their lives and lands, Nigeria risks a further decline in food production and an increase in land grabs by violent groups.

This case sets a deadly precedent: If you are attacked, do not fight back—otherwise, the government will kill you instead of your attacker.

A Call for Justice

The only way to correct this injustice is for Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri to exercise his constitutional right of mercy and grant a pardon to Jackson. Allowing this execution to proceed would not only be an injustice to one man but a death sentence on the right to self-defense in Nigeria.

If the government truly values the rule of law, it must stop protecting aggressors and punishing their victims. Justice must not only be done but must be seen to be done.

Jackson’s life must not be taken to satisfy a flawed judicial system. This execution must not happen.

Alert on the circulation of falsified Cikatem (Artemether 180mg/Lumefantrine 1080mg) with falsified NAFDAC Registration Number NRN A11-100025
#NafdacALERTS

Read more 🔗 https://bit.ly/4hJ3ykU

NAFDAC is notifying the public about the circulation of a confirmed falsified Cikatem (Artemether 180mg/Lumefantrine 1080mg) suspension. This product was discovered in the Coordinated Wholesale Centre (CWC) in Kano following a consumer complaint received and investigated by the Agency.

All the falsified Cikatem (Artemether 180mg/Lumefantrine 1080mg) suspension discovered during the investigation has been mopped up and surveillance is ongoing.

The product was observed to have a discrepancy on the packaging with NAFDAC Registration Number (A11-100025) printed on the label, which belonged to Cikatem Tablet 20/120mg, and not the suspension formulation.

The manufacturing facility was visited for further investigation, during which 17,280 bottles of Cikatem (Artemether 180mg/Lumefantrine 1080mg) suspension were placed on hold and are scheduled for destruction.

ARTEMETHER+LUMEFANTRINE FOR ORAL SUSPENSION is indicated for the treatment of malaria in children caused by all forms of plasmodium including severe malaria.

Mfg. Date: 10/2024

Exp. Date: 09/2027

NRN: NRN A11-100025

Manufactured by: Michelle Laboratories

Manufacturer Address: Plot 23, Block 2, Thinkers Corner Industrial Layout P.O. Box 2709, Enugu, Nigeria.

[25/03/2025, 12:31:18] Wellington: *🔊ANNOUNCEMENT*

*📍PSN CLEARANCE*

1. Kindly make all your dues payment via Pharmagateway website (www. Pharmagateway.com.ng) or Pharmpay (download via Google play store).

2. After making your payment download the receipt for subsequent usage.

3. Log on to PSN EDO website *(www.psnedo.com)* Fill in all necessary information and upload your dues  payment slip from Pharmagateway or Pharmpay. 

4. As a first timer on the website you are expected to Sign up first

5. Your subsequent log in details will be;
 *Username: Phone Number*
 *Number Password: PCN Reg number*

6. After registration, you may have to wait for sometime to get your clearance slip on your dashboard. 

*NB. Members are to please follow this process for a seamless registration*

*ACPN members are to please ensure that they already have thier clearance  ACPN SLIP  before PSN Edo will give the final clearance*

 
Thanks 


Announcer;

Dr. Wellington Omokaro 
Publicity Secretary 
PSN Edo State.

[25/03/2025, 16:39:31] St. Pharm  Yp Justine: *How to carry out premises registration for the year*

Determine the nature of the premise if it's wholesale or retail

Go on https://pay.pcn.gov.ng and pay the amount that pertains to the nature of your premise. Wholesale is 150k..  retail is 10k

Print the receipt of payment 

Go on https://pharmagateway.com.ng and pay the relevant dues which must include the Acpn dues in this case.

Download the soft copy of the receipt 

Go to https://www.psnedo.com upload the receipt and request for clearance. 

Once cleared print the clearance slip 

Go to https://acpnedo.macrosxp.com upload the receipt and request for clearance 

Once cleared print the clearance slip

Gather all the printouts with your application for renewal and go to the council for registration.

A bill to create the Office of the Prime Minister as head of government and the Office of President as head of state, and to provide for a framework for the mode of election to the said offices, has passed second reading in the House of Representatives.

The bill was among 32 Constitution amendment bills that scaled second reading in the House of Representatives on Thursday.

Also among the bills is a bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, to provide for specific seats for women in the National Assembly and state houses of assembly.

Another is a bill for an Act to alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, to reduce the period for determination of pre-election petition matters and provide for the establishment of pre-election tribunals for pre-election matters and regulate the process of suspending a member of the National Assembly from legislative duties.

A bill for an Act to alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, to review the requirements that qualifies persons to be elected as President and Vice-President, governors and deputy governors, passed second reading as well.

Also, a bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, to review the status of the Federal Capital Territory as regards the election of the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and bills for the creation of Wan State and Gobir State, equally passed second reading.

About 113 Constitution amendment bills have so far passed second reading.

[30/03/2025, 19:42:39] King Penet: *Urine: An Ancient Remedy and Its Use in Homeopathy*

Urine, often overlooked in modern medicine, has a long and fascinating history as a natural remedy. Across various cultures and civilizations, urine has been recognized as a powerful healing agent for thousands of years. In ancient times, urine therapy was practiced in Egypt, India, China, and other regions as a way to treat a wide variety of conditions. Today, in homeopathy, urine-derived remedies continue to play an important role, offering an alternative approach to health and healing. This article explores the ancient use of urine as a remedy and its applications in homeopathic medicine.

The History of Urine as a Healing Substance

The therapeutic use of urine spans millennia, with evidence found in ancient texts and practices. In India, the Shivambu Kalpa Vidhi, an ancient Ayurvedic practice, highlights the consumption and application of urine for its medicinal properties. This practice was based on the belief that urine, particularly one’s own, contains vital life force and healing energy.

In ancient Egypt, urine was used topically to treat wounds, infections, and skin diseases. The Egyptians even documented its use in their medical papyri. Similarly, in traditional Chinese medicine, urine was considered a vital substance, used for detoxifying the body and treating conditions such as urinary tract infections, skin issues, and digestive disorders.

European folk medicine also valued urine as a remedy for various ailments, especially for its antiseptic properties. It was believed to treat infections, promote healing, and restore bodily balance.

Urine in Homeopathy: Nosodes and Sarcodes

In the world of homeopathy, remedies are made from a variety of natural sources, including plants, minerals, and biological substances. Urine-derived remedies in homeopathy fall into two broad categories: nosodes and sarcodes.

Nosodes are homeopathic remedies made from substances that are linked to disease processes, such as the urine of individuals suffering from specific infections or diseases.

Sarcodes, on the other hand, are remedies made from healthy tissues or bodily fluids, such as urine from a healthy individual. These remedies are believed to support and restore balance to the body's systems.

Some of the key urine-based remedies in homeopathy include:

*Urina* (Urine) – A remedy prepared from human urine, used to support kidney function, aid detoxification, and treat urinary issues such as frequent urination, bladder infections, and kidney stones.

*Urea* – Derived from the waste product in urine, urea is used in homeopathy to address fluid retention, edema, metabolic disorders, and conditions where there is an imbalance in the body's ability to eliminate toxins.

*Parotidinum* – A nosode made from the urine of individuals infected with the mumps virus, this remedy is often used for conditions affecting the parotid glands and can be helpful in cases of glandular swelling and inflammation.

*Therapeutic Benefits of Urine-Based Homeopathic Remedies*

Urine-derived homeopathic remedies are versatile and can be used to treat a range of conditions. The key benefits include:

1. Support for Urinary Health

Urine remedies are particularly effective for addressing urinary tract infections (UTIs), bladder conditions, kidney issues, and problems such as frequent urination or incontinence. The remedies are believed to enhance the body’s natural detoxification process and promote kidney and bladder health.

2. Skin Conditions

Chronic skin issues, such as eczema, psoriasis, acne, and rashes, can be treated with urine-derived remedies. These remedies are believed to help balance the skin’s internal energy, promoting healing from the inside out.

3. Metabolic and Fluid Balance

Urine remedies, especially those derived from urea, are commonly used for conditions that involve fluid retention, edema, and metabolic imbalances. They can support the body’s ability to eliminate toxins and excess fluid, thus improving overall health and preventing further complications.

4. Immune System Regulation

Some urine-based homeopathic remedies are known to strengthen the immune system and increase the body’s ability to fight infections. These remedies are particularly useful in chronic conditions where the body’s immune defenses may be weakened or overburdened.

5. Detoxification

One of the primary roles of the kidneys is to filter toxins from the body, and urine-based remedies are thought to enhance this natural detoxification process. These remedies support the body in flushing out harmful substances and restoring a balanced internal environment.

The Homeopathic Process: Potentization and Healing

A key principle in homeopathy is the process of potentization, where substances are diluted and vigorously shaken (succussed) to release their healing energies while removing any harmful effects. When urine is used in homeopathic remedies, it undergoes this process, transforming from a waste product into a potent therapeutic agent. The remedy is believed to work on an energetic level, stimulating the body’s innate healing abilities without introducing any toxicity or harmful side effects.

The concept behind urine-based homeopathic remedies is that they work by rebalancing the body’s vital force (or life energy). In homeopathy, it is believed that every individual has a unique energetic signature, and remedies act to restore harmony between mind, body, and spirit.

*The Ancient Power of Urine in Homeopathy*

Urine, once dismissed as a simple waste product, has proven to be a valuable remedy in both traditional medicine and modern homeopathy. With a rich history of use across various cultures, urine therapy has stood the test of time. Homeopathic remedies derived from urine offer a holistic, non-toxic approach to healing and can support a variety of conditions, from urinary and metabolic disorders to immune system dysfunction and skin diseases.

By embracing the ancient wisdom of urine therapy in a modern, homeopathic form, individuals can access a safe and effective means of restoring balance and well-being to the body. Whether used for detoxification, healing, or supporting overall health, urine-based homeopathic remedies are a testament to the power of nature in its purest, most therapeutic form.

[01/04/2025, 13:49:33] Gildsluv Ypgd: *ATTENTION PLEASE!*

There is a new scamming technique in town called
'JUMPED'.

A scammer will send you a real deposit of money into your phone using his number.

This is not a fake deposit. They will really send you money, a relatively small amount  like N20K or N30K and you won't even doubt it.

After sending this money they will then launch a withdrawal attack on your alert SIM number.

When you receive the message on your phone that you have received some money, the natural thing is to be excited and then to want to check your balance.

To check the balance you'll need to enter your PIN.

The moment you put in your PIN, you will validate their withdrawal request on your account.

Your account will automatically allow this withdrawal request and your account will be debited.

The trick is to lure you with a relatively small amount initially and to steal something much larger from you. 

To protect yourself from this scam, whenever you receive such an unexpected deposit to your account, resist the temptation to immediately check your balance, then deliberately enter a wrong PIN.

This will cancel any withdrawal requests then thereafter check your balance with your real PIN.

With this new electronic money transfers and Artificial Intelligence coming in let's do this all the time to avoid being fooled by these scammers who are always coming up with new methods to try and steal from us.

Always share such information with family, friends and colleagues to keep them updated,  and always be at alert.
 
PLS. BE INFORMED.

[02/04/2025, 08:54:57] Omono Vincimus: *The Pot of Love*

As she took her seat at the family table, beads of sweat were still visible on her forehead. She heaved a sigh as the day's tasks neared their end. The kids were joyfully eating the meal of soup and eba. Junior chimed in, "Mum, you're the best!" Simi, his sister, followed, "Mum, you're the best cook in the whole world! I love you."

A heartfelt smile appeared on her face as her eyes checked his face for a reaction. He ate quietly, no emotion, as he swallowed. The day's events replayed in her head.

Her day had started at 7:30 a.m. at the abattoir, where she spent hours, her eyes smoked out from the roasting meat. She had chosen a juicy cowtail at a fair bargain, her eyes monitoring the slaughter boys to ensure they didn't compromise her meat. From there, she navigated the bustling New Benin Market, a hub of activity with varied items. She skillfully avoided barrow pushers and goods spread out on the floor, amidst traders' chants: "Customer, check here! Yellow, follow me buy na!"

At her favorite spice shop, she made her purchases and gathered other ingredients for the pot of soup. Her bag was full and heavy, straining her face as she pulled it, containing her conquest. Reaching home on time was a priority, to wash and pack the meat before it developed an odor. Finally home, the real work began.

She boiled the banga seeds, pounded, and washed the hot mash, her fair hands slipping in to extract the puree. It was hot, she thought to herself. In a matter of minutes, the base was ready. As she proceeded to add each ingredient to the pot of soup, she whispered to herself, "He's sure to enjoy this soup today." With care and love, she added condiments, tasting for flavor, reminding herself the soup must be perfect to please his taste buds.

She had specifically added some native spices for his health and originality. Locust bean seeds were good for men his age, she recalled. The aroma wafted, a rumble in her neighbors' stomachs, a combination of iru, stock fish, dried fish, and other swimming and walking things that was sure to make them salivate.

Lost in thought, wondering what could have gone wrong to make his expression so bland, Junior's voice cut through, "Thanks, Mum, I really enjoyed dinner! I love you." A weak smile appeared on her face as she asked, "Was anything wrong with the food?" Without raising his eyelids, he replied, "The food is okay, nothing's wrong." He washed his hands as he got off the table.

She smiled pitifully, continuing her meal. Definitely, the meal was okay. It was just another Pot of Love unappreciated. Maybe tomorrow, a compliment or appreciation, she murmured to herself. Tomorrow is another day. The lump in her throat became a stone, her appetite vanished, and she quietly cleared the plates. It should have been a Pot of Love.

[07/04/2025, 18:54:35] Idara Pcxx: *WORLD HEALTH DAY 2025*

This year's World Health Day theme, "Healthy beginnings, hopeful futures," highlights the crucial importance of improving maternal and newborn health and survival. The ultimate goal is to reduce global maternal mortality rates to less than 70 per 100,000 live births by 2030.

The World Health Organization (WHO) is urging governments and health communities to intensify efforts to end preventable maternal and newborn deaths. This can be achieved by ensuring equity in access to high-quality healthcare for women and babies, investing in healthcare, and improving the rights of women and girls to better protect their health. 

Here are some key statistics that underscore the urgency of this issue:

- *300,000 women die annually*: Due to pregnancy or childbirth complications.
- *2 million babies die within their first month*: With around 2 million more stillborn.
- *1 preventable death every 7 seconds*: Translating to millions of families affected worldwide.

To address this, WHO is calling for a worldwide reinvigoration of efforts to ensure access to high-quality care for women and babies. This includes:

- *Providing useful information*: To support healthy pregnancies, births, and postnatal health.
- *Advocating for effective investments*: To improve maternal and newborn health.
- *Encouraging collective action*: To support parents and health professionals.

The health of mothers and babies is the foundation of healthy families and communities, helping ensure hopeful futures for us all.

[08/04/2025, 19:28:00] MaduabuGod YPGd: @⁨Meta AI⁩ explain corned beef to this reputable Pharmacist
[08/04/2025, 19:28:04] Meta AI: Corned beef - a staple in many cuisines, particularly in the West. As a pharmacist, you're likely familiar with the intricacies of food preservation, so let's dive into the details.

Corned beef is a type of salt-cured beef, typically made from tougher cuts of meat like brisket or round. The "corning" process involves soaking the meat in a brine solution, which is a mixture of water, salt, and various spices. This helps to:

1. *Preserve the meat*: The high salt concentration inhibits bacterial growth, allowing the meat to be stored for longer periods.
2. *Tenderize the meat*: The brine solution breaks down the connective tissues, making the meat more palatable.
3. *Enhance flavor*: The spices and seasonings in the brine infuse the meat with a distinctive taste.

The corning process typically involves several steps:

1. *Curing*: The meat is submerged in the brine solution, which can take several days or even weeks.
2. *Rinsing*: The meat is removed from the brine and rinsed to remove excess salt.
3. *Cooking*: The corned beef is then cooked, often by boiling or steaming, to make it more palatable.

As a pharmacist, you might be interested to know that the curing process involves some chemistry. The salt in the brine solution helps to:

1. *Denature proteins*: The high salt concentration disrupts the protein structures, making the meat more tender.
2. *Inhibit bacterial growth*: The salt creates an environment that's unfavorable for bacterial growth, thereby preserving the meat.

Some popular types of corned beef include:

1. *Pastrami*: A type of corned beef that's been cured in a mixture of spices and herbs, then smoked or steamed.
2. *Corned beef hash*: A mixture of corned beef, potatoes, and onions, often served as a breakfast dish.
3. *Canned corned beef*: A convenient, shelf-stable version of corned beef that's been cooked and packaged in cans.

[10/04/2025, 22:30:26] Wellington: New Telegraph

Pharmacists Urge FG To Reflect Balanced Appointments In Health Sector


The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has urged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to ensure a more balanced and circumspect approach to political appointments in the health sector.

In a letter addressed to the President, and jointly signed by the President of the PSN, Pharm Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba and the National Secretary, Pharm.

Gafar Madehin, the PSN expressed concerns about the overwhelming dominance of physicians in key health-related appointments, noting the negative implications the trend has on the multidisciplinary nature of healthcare in Nigeria.


“We wish to convey our compliments of the season and our sincere prayers for Your Excellency’s health and wisdom as you continue to steer the ship of the Nigerian State.”

The letter tagged: “An Appeal For More Circumspection in Appointments in The Health Sector” addressed the mounting concern regarding appointments within the Ministry of Health and other related agencies since June 2023. Noting that the health sector is multidisciplinary, the PSN highlighted what they see as an alarming trend as nearly all key positions within the Ministry of Health and its agencies are being occupied by physicians.

“Almost all the appointments in the Health Sector… have gone to only one profession (Medicine), to the extreme detriment of all other healthcare professions,” the letter reads.

The PSN noted that this has created a significant imbalance, particularly given the mandate of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Ali Mohammed Pate, to build and harmonise and sustainable healthcare workforce.

The PSN pointed to numerous examples to underline their concerns. These included the appointment of two physicians as ministers in charge of the Federal Ministry of Health & Social Welfare (FMoH&SW), four other physician ministers in other federal ministries, and the appointment of a physician as the National Coordinator of the Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain (PVAC).

The PSN was especially critical of appointments in agencies that directly affect the practice of other health professionals. “The Chairman of NAFDAC, the National Health Insurance Agency (NHIA), and more than 90 per cent of MDAs that have been constituted are all physicians,” they noted.


The letter further pointed out that all Vice-Chancellors of Nigeria’s universities of health sciences are physicians, further illustrating the profession’s overwhelming presence in key decision-making positions within the healthcare sector.

Calling for balance and fair representation, the PSN in the letter acknowledged the President’s constitutional prerogative to make political appointments, stressing the need for greater circumspection in these decisions.

“We solicit that a lot more circumspection is brought to bear in making these appointments. It is worrisome that even areas that should not be considered as preserves of physicians are ceded to them,” they stated.


We must respect the diversity and contributions of all professionals in the sector

The PSN specifically criticised the appointment of physicians to leadership roles in agencies such as the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), which is primarily concerned with pharmacy practice and drug management.

“NAFDAC, an agency that specialises in pharmacy practice and drug and food management, should not be headed by a physician,” PSN argued. Further raising alarms, the PSN pointed to the appointment of Dr. Ibrahim Oloriegbe as the Chairman of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), a position that the PSN believes is unsuitable for someone with such a controversial history.

They argued that Oloriegbe, a former senator, was involved in a failed bill that sought to restrict the use of the title ‘doctor’ within Nigerian hospitals to only physicians. The PSN argued that such appointments, combined with others under the leadership of physicians, have led to a failure in managing Nigeria’s social health insurance system.

“As of now, Nigeria’s health insurance coverage rate has plummeted from about 20 per cent in 2010 to a dismal 1.72 per cent in 2017. This underperformance cannot be divorced from the leadership styles of previous physician-led administrations.

“How will Nigeria ever attain Universal Health Coverage (UHC), if social health insurance, which is a major condition precedent globally acclaimed, is managed by people who have never appreciated consensus building in health management,” the letter asserted.

On the threat of the National Health Facility Regulatory Agency (NHFRA) Bill, the PSN said it has raised issues over the proposed NHFRA bill.”


The PSN said the bill, which was orchestrated by the former Minister of State for Health Dr. Tunji Alausa and current Minister of State for Health Dr. Iziaq Salako, has raised concerns about professional dominance in the health sector.

The PSN claimed that the bill was designed by a team of 15 physicians and only three non-physicians, and that its goal was to restore privileges that physicians had been unable to secure through the National Health Act of 2014. The PSN warned that the NHFRA bill would undermine the leadership and regulatory power of other healthcare professionals and could lead to further professional marginalisation.

“That draconian and vengeful bill which was conceived by the representative templates of physicians was oiled by the unholy professional domination of the leadership of the FMoH&SW by physician-ministers, special advisers and a director of hospital services who is more of an employee of umbrella-template of physicians in output.

“Your Excellency, the NHFRA draft bill which was concocted by a team of 15 physicians and three non physicians is designed to restore all the undeserved privileges physicians could not get through the National Health Act -2014 and it actively seeks in spirit to get the enabling Acts of the other 12 professional regulatory Councils apart from the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria to be repealed when the content is appraised albeit critically.

This bill was finalised for submission to Dr Iziaq Salako on Friday, March 28, 2025,” they claimed. The PSN appealed to the President for a more equitable approach to appointments, akin to the structure seen in other sectors like Building and Works, where professionals such as architects, engineers, and surveyors work in tandem, with each discipline’s privileges respected.

“The health sector, like any other sector, is multidisciplinary. We must respect the diversity and contributions of all professionals in the sector, from pharmacy to nursing, to ensure a more inclusive and efficient healthcare system.”

Affirming PSN’s commitment to help to stabilise Nigeria’s health system, which they argued has been underperforming due to unbalanced leadership, they said: “We assure Your Excellency that the PSN will continue to provide building blocks for the stability of the health system.”

[15/04/2025, 22:25:55] Okosodo Joshua Ypgd: We Are Not Doctors’ Maids—We Are the Heartbeat of Healthcare

Stop calling us “just nurses.”
We are not doctors’ maids.
We don’t exist to carry clipboards, make beds, or follow orders without thought.
We are professionals.
We are the heartbeat of healthcare.

We are trained.
Not just in theory, but in practice.
We assess. We diagnose. We act.
Not later. Not eventually. But timely, safely, and based on solid evidence.

When a patient is crashing, it’s often the nurse who notices first.
When pain goes unspoken, the nurse hears it in a whisper, in a grimace, in silence.
When hope fades, it’s the nurse who still believes—who still fights.

We don’t just give drugs—we monitor effects, catch adverse reactions, and advocate for alternatives.
We don’t just follow orders—we collaborate, we question, we inform decisions.

Respectful care isn’t optional—it’s our standard.
We care for everyone, regardless of status, background, or belief.
From the newborn in NICU to the aged in palliative care,
From the mother in labor to the patient in ICU—we show up. We stay. We serve.

So, next time you think nurses are just helping hands—look again.
We’re calculating doses. Managing emergencies. Educating families. Leading teams.
And still holding hands when no one else will.

We are not assistants. We are essential.
We are not backup—we are frontline.
We are not beneath—we are beside.

Nurses are not doctors’ maids.
We are the voice of advocacy, the soul of compassion, and the pulse of healing.

We are nurses.
Trained. Trusted. Tireless.
The heartbeat of healthcare.

[16/04/2025, 21:31:34] Mr Michael Ypg State Cordinator: *YOU ARE AN AMBASSADOR OF THE PROFESSION*

Colleagues, hear this truth today: You are not merely pharmacists. You are ambassadors.  
You carry in your hands, your words, and your daily choices the sacred responsibility of an entire profession. The world does not see ‘pharmacy’ as a building, a counter, or a shelf of bottles. They see *you*. Every interaction, every prescription filled, every word of counsel you offer....it all writes the story of what pharmacy means to humanity. *You* are the living embodiment of this calling.  

*You were chosen for such a time as this.* 
Just as an ambassador represents the authority, values, and heart of their nation, *you* represent the soul of pharmacy. When a patient walks into your space, they are not seeking a transaction.....they are seeking hope, healing, and trust. Your white coat is not just fabric; it is a mantle of authority. Your title is not just a degree; it is a covenant. You hold the power to redefine perceptions. If they leave inspired, it is because *you* inspired them. If they leave doubting, it is because *we* have failed to show them the fullness of our purpose.  

*Never forget: Perception is shaped by proximity.*  

To the single mother clutching her child’s antibiotic, *you* are pharmacy. To the elderly man navigating five medications, *you* are pharmacy. To the teenager buying their first pain  relief, *you* are pharmacy. They will not remember the textbooks you studied or the exams you passed. They will remember the respect you gave, the patience you showed, and the light of competence in your eyes. *Your character is their curriculum.*

*"The enemy of our profession is not ignorance.....it is indifference.*  
In the words of my mentor and friend, Prof Azuka Oparah, the renowned clinical pharmacist:  *“If a patient does not experience Pharmaceutical Care when they encounter you in your community pharmacy, they should have the right to sue you.”*  
When you reduce your role to counting pills or reciting side effects, you shrink the legacy of those who walked before you.  

Let me speak plainly: Theft, fraud, and ethical shortcuts are not just crimes....they are betrayals of your sacred mandate.  
*Pilferage* robs your community of life-saving resources. *Fronting*;aiding non-pharmacists to illegally own pharmacies.....mocks the very laws that protect our practice and patients. Selling illicit or banned drugs poisons the well of trust our forebears dug with their integrity. These acts are not mere “mistakes”; they are arrows aimed at the heart of pharmacy’s soul. Every time you falsify ownership, bypass PCN standards, or prioritize profit over people, you teach the world that pharmacy is a business of loopholes, not a calling of light.  

Pharmacy is not a title to exploit but a covenant to uphold. You cannot claim to champion health while peddling harm. You cannot demand respect for the profession while undermining its laws. *Indifference is deadly, but complicity is catastrophic.* When you tolerate these acts by silence or participation, you endorse a lie: that pharmacy is a playground for the unprincipled. But I want to believe: *This is not who we are.*  

We are custodians of a sacred trust.  
Every pill you dispense, every license you honor, every policy you uphold....these are threads in the tapestry of our profession’s integrity. Do not cut them with greed or apathy. Rise above the shameful compromise of “everyone does it.” *You were called to set the standard, not chase it.*  

Pharmacy was born from the ancient pursuit of healing; of alchemists, herbalists, and healers who saw their work as a divine partnership. You are heirs to that legacy. You do not ‘work’ in pharmacy; pharmacy works through *you*. Every time you educate instead of rush, listen instead of assume, or advocate instead of comply, you declare to the world: *This is what pharmacy is.*  

*So rise, ambassadors!*  
Walk with the confidence of those who know their purpose. Speak with the clarity of those who understand their power. Serve with the compassion of those who recognize their privilege. The next generation of pharmacists will inherit the reputation *you* create today. Will they inherit a profession diluted by apathy, or one elevated by excellence? The answer lies in your hands. 

Ehitare Patrick OMOAREBU
Pharm.D, MPH, MBA 
Assistant National secretary, PSN

‎[19/04/2025, 13:29:24] Sunday Stanley Pcx: 🧠💚 World Liver Day: The Mind-Body Connection 💚🧠
Theme: “Food is Medicine”

Today is World Liver Day, a reminder of how vital liver health is to our overall well-being — and yes, that includes mental well-being too.

Most people think of the liver only in terms of digestion and detoxification. But did you know that your liver plays a significant role in your brain chemistry and mood regulation?

Here’s how they’re connected:

🔸 A healthy liver helps regulate hormones, including cortisol and serotonin — both crucial in managing stress, mood, and anxiety.
🔸 Liver dysfunction can lead to the buildup of toxins in the bloodstream, which may contribute to mental fog, irritability, and even depressive symptoms.
🔸 What you eat directly impacts both your liver and your mind. Processed foods, alcohol, and high sugar can strain the liver and negatively affect your mental state.
🔸 Nutrients like omega-3s, B-vitamins, and antioxidants support both liver function and cognitive health.

At InYou Mental Health, we understand that mental health is not just in your head — it’s deeply rooted in how you nourish and care for your body, too.

🌿 This World Liver Day, let’s commit to holistic health:
🫀 Support your liver.
🧠 Support your mind.
🥗 Choose healing foods.
💬 Talk about how you feel.

Because healing isn't one-dimensional — it's all connected.
