[26/04/2025, 01:22:19] ~ Lancelot: *How TRACK SYSTEM in LANC PHARMA works*

1. Sales Order 
2. Invoice creation 
3. Payment 
4. Shipment 

1. *Sales order* is created with an autogenerated number set to track each order filled or unfilled .
 Sales order becomes filled when the client has paid for the item or unfilled when no payment is made.

Filled order are labelled Green (client pay in full)
Partially Filled order are labelled yellow (client made partial payment)
No filled order are label red(no payment was made at all by client)

2.*Invoice creation*
 Every sales order creates an invoice of which is tracked with an autogenerated serial number set assign to each invoices
3. *Shipment fulfillment* is tracked by 2 means 
A. Package serial number 
B. Shipment serial number 

For large number of item sent to 1 client in 1 invoice ,a default autogenerated serial number can be used as the package serial number but the shipment serial number is the plate number of the driver.

Or if it is just 1 item to 1 client,the serial number crested on the product can be captured as the Package serial number but the Shipment serial number remains the Driver plate number.

Once the package has arrived it destination,we then tick that shipment order has already been filled or completed

Other details collected prior to shipment include Driver name and contact as well as client details(Name, location package is to be delivered, phone number) to keep  client's abreast with the incoming package to be delivered to them. ‎<This message was edited>

[28/04/2025, 09:44:57] Sir Hope Onyemaechi: ￼
*THE COMMUNIQUE OF THE NMA LAGOS STATE EMERGENCY STATE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL (SEC) MEETING CONVENED ON THURSDAY, THE 24TH OF APRIL, 2025 AT MRC AUDITORIUM, LASUTH, IKEJA LAGOS*.


*The emergency SEC meeting, which was convened due to the implementation of the Consultant Pharmacy Cadre by the Medical Director of the Federal Medical Centre ( FMC), Ebute Metta, Dr Adedamola Dada and the Medical Director of the Federal Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Dr Olugbenga Owoeye*. 

The SEC rendered the following observations and resolutions subsequent to a thorough discourse on the agenda.

*OBSERVATIONS*
1.      The SEC expressed profound disappointment concerning the enactment of the consultant cadre by the Medical Directors of the Federal Medical Center, Ebute Metta, and the Federal Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Lagos, notwithstanding the stance of the NMA that no medical institution should initiate such a directive, which is prone to crises and fails to contribute positively to the management of the institution in the pursuit of efficient and effective service delivery.

2 . This cadre provides *no clinical value* in direct patient care, undermines established medical protocols, and sets a dangerous precedent that is *capable of triggering industrial disharmony and eroding the structure of patient-oriented healthcare systems* across health institutions in Lagos State and beyond.


*RESOLUTIONS*
1.      The SEC categorically rejects the decision to appoint Consultant Pharmacists by the Medical Directors of the Federal Medical Center, Ebute Metta, Dr. Ademola Dada, and the Federal Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Dr. Olugbenga Owoeye, as this cadre offers no clinical advantage to patient management and poses a risk of inducing industrial discord within healthcare facilities across Lagos State.

2.      The SEC mandates the issuance of a seven-day ultimatum to the Medical Directors of the Federal Medical Center, Ebute Metta, Dr. Adedamola Dada, and the Federal Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Dr. Olugbenga Owoeye, to reverse the implementation and appointment of this cadre.

3.       The SEC asserts that should this decision remain unaltered upon the expiration of the ultimatum, it encourages the physicians within the affected institutions to initiate a warning strike to emphasize this demand.

4.      The SEC mandates that a subsequent SEC meeting be convened to reassess all actions delineated in point (3) after the stipulated time frame has elapsed.

5.      The SEC mandates the State Officers Committee (SOC) to convene a press conference within 48 hours following this meeting to address the public regarding the perilous implications of instituting the consultant pharmacy cadre within clinical environments, which jeopardizes patient welfare in Lagos State.

6.       The SEC asserts that the SOC should formally communicate this decision to the National NMA and notify them that should any of the individuals, Dr. Adedamola Dada or Dr. Olugbenga Owoeye, be considered for any form of award or recognition, such considerations should be suspended until this action has been reversed and resolved.

7.      The SEC mandates the SOC to draft a correspondence to the Federal Ministry of Health and pertinent stakeholders regarding the inherent dangers of this decision to patient care in Lagos State.

8.      The SEC urges the National NMA to engage in a discourse concerning the ramifications of the implementation of the Consultant Pharmacist role at the national level and to undertake the requisite measures to reverse and halt the establishment of this dangerous precedence .

A clear and strong warning is hereby issued to all other Medical Directors and Chief Medical Directors who may be contemplating implementing the Consultant Pharmacist Cadre: NMA Lagos State will not hesitate to deploy every legitimate means necessary to resist such moves.

 We urge all members across Lagos State to remain vigilant, united, and fully prepared in the coming days as we collectively defend the integrity of our profession and the sanctity of patient care.

*These decisions reaffirm our unwavering commitment to promoting a functional, ethically sound, and patient-centered healthcare system in Lagos State and Nigeria*.


*Together, we stand strong.*


*Dr. B.K.S SAHEED*                                                                              
*Chairman, NMA Lagos State.*


*Dr Jimoh Hassan* 
*Secretary, NMA Lagos State.*

[28/04/2025, 09:48:09] Sir Hope Onyemaechi: Consultant Pharmacist Cadre: A Non-Negotiable Pillar of Modern Healthcare—A Scathing Rebuttal to NMA’s Obstruction


I write as a pharmacist who refuses to stand by while the Nigeria Medical Association indulges in petty, self-serving antics that threaten patient lives. The NMA’s intransigent threat of strike action over the creation of a Consultant Pharmacist cadre is not only intellectually bankrupt—it is morally reprehensible.

Medical Negligence: The Grim Toll You Refuse to Acknowledge!

The World Health Organization reports that 2.6 million patients die yearly from medical errors, with prescription blunders and improper drug use among the culprits. Yet, the NMA would rather wage a tantrum than accept the only proven measure—empowering Consultant Pharmacists—to slash these deadly mistakes.

Global Leaders Embrace Consultant Pharmacists—Why Does NMA Cling to Obsolescence?

In the UK’s NHS, Consultant Pharmacists have been saving lives for over a decade, slashing medication errors and streamlining complex therapies. Australia, Canada, the U.S., and Europe have long integrated Clinical Pharmacist Specialists into patient-care teams, reaping measurable gains in safety and efficiency. Meanwhile, the NMA stubbornly clings to a medieval hierarchy, as if modern medicine can survive on outdated egos.

Your Authoritarian Posture Betrays a Fragile Ego, Not Patient Welfare
Brandishing threats of Industrial action against professionals whose specialized pharmacotherapy expertise is indispensable exposes the NMA’s brittle sense of supremacy.

 Consultant Pharmacists mentor junior staff, refine treatment plans, and intercept adverse drug events—duties you refuse to share. This isn’t about safety; it’s about preserving an illusory rank.

Burnout as a Strategy: Exploiting Young Doctors Under the Guise of Advocacy.

Your hollow proclamations to “protect young doctors” ring as hollow as your actions are exploitative. By hoarding prescribing authority, you subject interns and residents to relentless overwork, turning them into de facto prescription clerks while pharmacists stand ready to prevent errors. This cynical exploitation must end.

Stop Holding Patients Hostage with Your Cynical Power Plays!

Threatening to cripple healthcare delivery to satisfy doctors’ bruised egos is nothing short of hostage-taking. True advocacy invests in staffing, infrastructure, and protocol-driven collaboration—not in blocking reforms that save lives.

Respect the Rule of Law: Regulatory Decisions Are Not Your Plaything
The Pharmacy Council of Nigeria and the Federal Ministry of Health have lawfully ratified the Consultant Pharmacist cadre. The NMA’s attempts to subvert these determinations are an affront to governance, professional ethics, and the basic principles of institutional integrity.

A Defining Moment: Choose Progress Over Petty Politics
Embracing Consultant Pharmacists is not a concession—it is an exigency. It is the difference between preventable tragedy and therapeutic triumph. Nigeria’s health system stands at a crossroads: evolve with international standards or languish under the weight of ego-driven stagnation.

— Arogundade Taoheed, B.Pharm., MSc. (University of Ibadan), MPSN
Published from Ibadan

🔰Through this program, volunteers will actively participate in various NAFDAC activities, including enforcement operations, public sensitization campaigns, Pharmacovigilance activities, surveys, community outreaches, NYSC orientation programs, and other ad-hoc assignments.

*🔰Volunteer recruitment opens today, Monday, 28th April, and will close on Thursday, 30th May, 2025.*

🔰All Young Pharmacists interested in volunteering are encouraged to fill the registration form via this link: 

https://forms.office.com/r/qXzZfLkaKA?origin=lprLink

🔰The official unveiling and launch of the NAFDAC Young Pharmacists Reserve Volunteers Program will take place on *Tuesday, 17th June, 2025, in Lagos State.*

🔰The event will be officiated by the Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, and will hold via a hybrid (Physical and virtual) format for all volunteers.

[01/05/2025, 15:04:06] Dr. Joshua Idemudia (PharmD) Ypgd: *PRESS RELEASE NO.106/EDSGH/2025* 

*OFFICE OF THE GOVERNOR* 
*EDO STATE GOVERNMENT* 

*MAY DAY: GOV OKPEBHOLO RAISES MINIMUM WAGE FOR EDO WORKERS TO N75,000* 

Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo has increased the minimum wage for Edo State workers from N70, 000 to N75,000 to further improve their standard of living.

Governor Okpebholo made the announcement while delivering his May Day speech at the Samuel Ogbemudia Stadium in Benin City Edo State.

The Governor, while appreciating the contributions of Edo State workers to the growth and development of Edo State, said his administration will always seek ways to improve the welfare of Edo workers.

Okpebholo noted that the workers’ day celebration is a special day set aside to honour the hardworking men and women who keep the State moving forward as they support their families with dignity and strength.

“Today, I am proud to announce that our administration has approved a new minimum wage of N75,000 per month for Edo workers.

“It’s our way of saying thank you, Edo workers. We believe this will make a real difference, and in return, we count on your renewed dedication as we build a better Edo together.

“Since assuming office, my administration has remained fully committed to the welfare of our workers. One of our first actions in office was to convert many casual workers, including over 1,000 cleaners who, for years, had no job security into the core civil service, giving them stability and peace of mind.

“We hired 500 new teachers to ease classroom pressure and help students learn better. We are also reviewing the casual position of over 3,000 Edo State teachers for possible full employment because their effort will shape our children’s future,” he said.

Continuing, Okpebholo said, “We approved the recruitment of 450 clinical and non-clinical staff for our State hospitals and regularized 126 contract staff at Edo State Specialist hospital. These steps not only strengthen our health system but also improve job stability for health professionals.”

The Governor also used the medium to inform the public that his administration has cleared outstanding salary arrears owed to Edo State polytechnic staff. “In the judiciary, we made sure that judges who had been delayed in their appointments were properly sworn in and now fully carrying out their duties.

“To show our commitment doesn’t end at retirement, we have also approved health insurance coverage for our retirees because we believed that our responsibility to workers doesn’t end when they leave active service.”

Governor Okpebholo said his administration is committed to timely payment of salaries and pension; steady recruitment where needed to improve service delivery; staff welfare and development and ensuring that Edo workers are treated with dignity and fairness.

“As we mark this day, I joined His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and my fellow governor’s in wishing all Nigerian workers a peaceful and fulfilling celebration. Your efforts shaped our nation and laid the foundation for a better tomorrow.”

The acting chairman of Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Edo State chapter, Comrade Bernard Egwekhide commended the governor of Edo State senator Monday Okpebholo for the formations and implementation of laudable policies and programmes towards alleviating the suffering and hardships faced by Edo workers and pensioners.

He noted that the theme: “reclaiming the Civil space in the midst of economic hardship” is apt and thought provoking as it borders on the very serious challenges faced by the Nigerian workers and the people as a result of the present day economic hardship faced by them in the country.

Egwekhide thanked Governor Monday Okpebholo led administration for taking the welfare of Edo workers very seriously and embarked on interventions that to a great extent enabled workers in the State to enjoy their civil rights.

“Just within six months in office, you have done excellently well for Edo State for Edo State workers as your performance is beyond our expectations as workers.

“We thank the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria Ahmed Bola Tinubu for the support given to Edo State Government as the first flyover is under construction while a second one has been approved. Federal roads across the State are also getting the needed attention they deserve.”


Guest at the event include Deputy Governor of Edo State Hon. Dannis Idahosa; Speaker, Edo State House of Assembly, Rt Hon Blessing Agbebaku; secretary to Edo State Government, Musa Ikhilor; Chief of Staff, Gani Audu, Head of Service (HOS), Anthony Okungbowa; former deputy governor of Edo State, Comrade Phillip Shaibu; chairman of APC, Edo State Jaret Tenebe; party leaders, labour leaders, Edo State workers, amongst others.


*Signed*:
*Fred Itua*,
*The Chief Press Secretary to the Edo State Governor.*
*Thursday, 01 May, 2025*.

▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

〽️The Emir's Palace in Kano City, known as Gidan Rumfa, is a monumental testament to Nigeria's rich cultural heritage and architectural grandeur.

〽️Located in the heart of Kano, this historical site offers visitors a fascinating glimpse into the life and customs of the region. 

〽️Originally constructed in the late 15th century by Sarkin Muhammadu Rumfa (King Muhammad Rumfa), the palace was later expanded and renovated over the centuries, with significant transformations taking place after the Fulani Jihad of 1805.

〽️The palace, which covers an expansive 33 acres, is the oldest and largest traditional palace in Northern Nigeria.

〽️The Emir's Palace is a must-visit destination that promises to leave a lasting impression.

WHAT is LANCE CONSULT?

LANCE CONSULT is a unique package  that offers you one of the most educative and illustrative  studies on clinical intervention when looking for scarce medication through  Lance Pharma.

*Why is LANCE CONSULT so important?*

While we as a team sort for your scarce medication we open you to some learning based on the intervention made as follows 

1. Category A scarce medicine : drugs banned in some countries as a result of the side effects 
2. Category B scarce medicine : Drugs not in use yet due to the fact it hasn't fully passed it's clinical trials
3. Category C scarce medicine :Drugs scarce as a result of their carcinogenic or teratogenic properties in very the short term


Lately

Here below was an intervention made on a Client A

The Client complained of numbness of hand and feets alongside with occasion pains once a while.

Plan initially given

Dimethylglycine which was one of the prescribed scarce medication ‎image omitted
[12/05/2025, 17:17:54] ~ Lancelot: *LANCE CONSULT*

*What to know about Dimethylglycine* 


*Dimethylglycine (DMG)* is an amino acids which as shown unsafe addictive effect after prolong use more than 28days which was banned in Chicago USA due to that.

Dimethylglycine aids the remethylation of homocysteine to methionine which in long term converted to glycine.

*Drug Therapetic problem :*  unsafe Addictive effect after 28days

*How the client case was solved*

Client for safety reason was switched from Dimethylglycine (Vitamin B16) to Renerve plus (containing Selenomethione)

Selenomethione follows the remethylation chain but we have bypass the dimethylglycine involvement in methylation of homocysteine to methionine.

Selenomethione serves as a methionine substrate able to be converted to adenosylmethionine and at the end glycine.

This pathway helps to reduce oxidative stress and also helps in nerve rejuvenation .


*Conclusion*
Patient was counselled and changed to Renerve plus which not only have Selenomethione an another methionine sunstrate (Zinc mono methionine) ,folic acid , methylcobalamine and other unique API which will not only reduces side effects but only reduce patient pill burdens

‎[13/05/2025, 15:25:53] Sir Prof  Pharm Abu Dantani John: *ACPN EDO MARKS WORLD HYPERTENSION DAY 2025* 

Dear colleagues,
Please be informed that World Hypertension Day 2025 comes up on Saturday  17th May.

As community pharmacists, we play a pivotal role in the detection, prevention, management, counselling and referral services of HYPERTENSION as a public health burden. Preventive healthcare information, disease identification and effective management of hypertension are core components of our practice.

Therefore, the EDO ACPN invites you to join her as we mark this year's world hypertension day with  a public healthcare awareness and intervention outreach in IYARO community Benin City.
The choice of this location is due to the aggregation of motor parks and drivers who do long distance travels and hardly check their blood pressure despite being a high risk group.
The details of the outreach are as follows:
*Date:* Saturday 17th May, 2025
*Time:* 10.00 am
*Venue:* NNPC Filling Station, IYARO bus stop, after Iyare motor park.

Community Pharmacists are encouraged to turn up enmass for this outreach and also come along with the following;
* A Lab coat
* A BP monitoring device (manual or digital)
* Short dated antihypertensives if available 
* Other short dated medications (supplements, antidiabetics, analgesics, etc) if available 
* Glucometer devices and strips.

I look forward to seeing you.

[13/05/2025, 17:38:06] Daniel Adulphus Ypgd: *DEFENDING PROGRESS IN HEALTHCARE: A REBUTTAL TO NMA’S STANCE ON PHARMACIST CONSULTANTS AND DOCTORAL TRAINING*

The Clinical Pharmacists Association of Nigeria (CPAN) has observed, with profound disappointment, the recent spate of unprofessional and divisive statements by some medical associations in Nigeria, including the Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors (NARD), the Medical and Dental Consultants Association of Nigeria (MDCAN) and even the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), regarding the well-considered advancements in Nigeria’s healthcare system; specifically, the recognition of Pharmacist Consultants and the move by the National Universities Commission (NUC) to upgrade key health professional degrees to doctoral levels (PharmD, DPT, OD, etc.).

As a major stakeholder in the Nigerian health sector and an interest group of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria *(Nigeria’s foremost and oldest healthcare professionals’ body* established in 1927 and approaching its centenary) CPAN is compelled to correct the NMA’s misleading narrative.

For nearly a century, Nigerian Pharmacists have served as pioneers of public health, from malaria control to vaccine policy, long before many of the NMA’s affiliates (NARD, MDCAN, etc.) existed. It is regrettable that in *2025*, we must *debunk elementary falsehoods* about interprofessional roles from bodies that should know better.

Rather than embracing global best practices that prioritize *patient-centred care through interprofessional collaboration*, the NMA and some of its affiliates have chosen the path of territorialism, misinformation, and needless rivalry: a stance that is not only *archaic* but detrimental to the evolution of Nigeria’s healthcare system.

*1. THE CONSULTANT PHARMACIST CADRE: A GLOBAL STANDARD, NOT A THREAT*

The NMA’s opposition to the Consultant Pharmacist cadre betrays a shocking ignorance of global healthcare structures.

- *United Kingdom*: The Royal Pharmaceutical Society (RPS) *accredits Consultant Pharmacists* who engage clinical services, prescribe independently, and manage complex patient cases—*with full recognition by the National Health Service (NHS)*.
- *United States*: Board-Certified Pharmacotherapy Specialists (BCPS) and other PharmD-trained clinical Pharmacists *hold consultant roles in hospitals, ICUs, as well as private and public health institutions*.
- *Saudi Arabia, Canada, Australia and many other countries*: Consultant Pharmacists are integral to multidisciplinary teams, with *prescribing rights and direct patient care responsibilities*.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has repeatedly emphasized *task-shifting and collaborative practice* as key strategies to strengthen health systems, particularly in resource-limited settings like Nigeria. The NMA’s resistance to this is not just anti-progress, but anti-patient.

*2. DOCTORAL TRAINING IN HEALTH PROFESSIONS: A NECESSITY, NOT A LUXURY*

The NUC’s decision to upgrade Pharmacy, Physiotherapy, and other health professional degrees to *Doctorate levels (PharmD, DPT, OD, etc.)* aligns with *global educational standards*.
- *PharmD (Doctor of Pharmacy)* has been the *minimum entry-level degree for clinical pharmacy* practice in the U.S. and many countries for a long time.
- NMA may wish to note that *Algeria, Egypt, Ghana, Uganda*, and some other African countries have since transformed their Pharmacy degrees to *Doctor of Pharmacy*. 
- *Doctor of Physiotherapy (DPT)* is the *standard in Europe and North America*, ensuring practitioners are equipped with *advanced diagnostic and therapeutic skills*.

The NMA’s claim that this upgrade “dilutes the medical profession” is *laughably illogical*. Medicine does not hold a monopoly on the title “Doctor”. The term is rooted in academia (from the Latin docere, “to teach” or “to instruct”). Physicians are *doctors of medicine*, just as pharmacists are *doctors of pharmacy (PharmD)*, and physiotherapists are *doctors of physiotherapy (DPT)*.

*3. THE FOLLY OF THE NMA’S ARGUMENTS: A CRITIQUE OF THE RESISTANCE*

The NMA’s statements exhibit *four critical flaws:*
1. *Misunderstanding of Roles*: Clinical Pharmacists *do not seek to “replace” physicians* but to *complement them*; optimizing drug therapy and improving outcomes. 
2. *Fear of Progress*: The global shift toward *interprofessional education (IPE)* and *collaborative practice* is irreversible. The NMA’s stance is akin to opposing stethoscopes because they were not used in 1800.
3. 	*Patient-disregarding Territorialism*: The NMA’s fixation on *hierarchy over teamwork* harms Nigerian patients. In nations with *strong pharmacist-physician collaboration (e.g., Canada, UK)*, patient outcomes are *superior*.
4. Wilful Disregard to Local Evidence
The NMA’s rhetoric ignores Nigeria’s own documented successes with pharmacist interventions. *Peer-reviewed studies from Nigeria itself demonstrate* this:

*a*. For any practitioner genuinely invested in evidence, a 5-minute PubMed search using simple strings like *‘(((pharmacist) AND (impact OR effect)) AND (intervention)) AND (Nigeria)’* reveals dozens of publications where pharmacist-led interventions directly improved survival rates in sepsis, antimicrobial stewardship, and chronic disease management. Specific outcomes that have been reported include reduced mortality and sustained viral load suppression in HIV care, improved blood pressure and blood glucose controls, epilepsy management, and slashed medication errors in hospitals at all levels as well as community pharmacies.

*b*.These are not theoretical claims but Nigerian data, published globally (see publications in _BMC Health Services Research, PLOS ONE, Patient Education and Counselling, British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, Epilepsy Research, BMC Medical Education, American Journal of Health-System Pharmacy, International Journal of Clinical Pharmacy, Journal of Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics, Pharmacy Practice, Value in Health (Regional Issue_), among others), validating that Pharmacists are indispensable collaborators, not competitors.

One wonders: *If the NMA truly values ‘evidence-based medicine,’ why does it so readily ignore evidence from its own backyard?* To dismiss this is to dismiss Nigerian science itself!

*4. A CALL FOR MATURITY, COLLABORATION, AND PATIENT-CENTERED REFORMS*
CPAN urges the NMA to *abandon its regressive rhetoric* and instead:
- *Engage in constructive dialogue* with other healthcare professionals.
- *Recognize global best practices, where team-based care improves survival rates*.
- *Focus on Nigeria’s healthcare crises* - drug shortages, poor infrastructure, brain drain - rather than *fighting phantom threats*.

The *21st-century healthcare system thrives on collaboration, not territorialism*. Nigeria cannot afford to remain shackled by *outdated professional rivalries* while the world moves forward.

*CONCLUSION: A FINAL APPEAL TO REASON*

To the NMA: *Our patients need enhanced services from every healthcare provider, not nomenclatures*.
To policymakers: *Stay the course; Nigeria’s healthcare system must evolve*.
To the public: *Demand teamwork from your healthcare providers; your life depends on it.*

CPAN remains committed to *scientific rigour, interprofessional collaboration, and patient welfare*. We will *not be dragged into petty squabbles* but will continue to advocate for *evidence-based, globally competitive healthcare reforms*.

Dr. AbdulMuminu Isah, _BPharm, M Pharm, PharmD, PhD, FPCPharm, CSCA_
*National Secretary*

Dr. Maureen Nwafor, _BPharm, M Pharm, PharmD, MBA, FPCPharm_	
*National Chairman*

#CollaborationOverCompetition #PatientFirst #21stCenturyHealthcare

‎[14/05/2025, 15:32:23] ~ Chronicles & scrubs: *ACPN EDO MARKS WORLD HYPERTENSION DAY 2025* 

Dear colleagues,
Please be informed that World Hypertension Day 2025 comes up on Saturday  17th May.

As community pharmacists, we play a pivotal role in the detection, prevention, management, counselling and referral services of HYPERTENSION as a public health burden. Preventive healthcare information, disease identification and effective management of hypertension are core components of our practice.

Therefore, the EDO ACPN invites you to join her as we mark this year's world hypertension day with  a public healthcare awareness and intervention outreach in IYARO community Benin City.
The choice of this location is due to the aggregation of motor parks and drivers who do long distance travels and hardly check their blood pressure despite being a high risk group.
The details of the outreach are as follows:
*Date:* Saturday 17th May, 2025
*Time:* 10.00 am
*Venue:* NNPC Filling Station, IYARO bus stop, after Iyare motor park.

Community Pharmacists are encouraged to turn up enmass for this outreach and also come along with the following;
* A Lab coat
* A BP monitoring device (manual or digital)
* Short dated antihypertensives if available 
* Other short dated medications (supplements, antidiabetics, analgesics, etc) if available 
* Glucometer devices and strips.

I look forward to seeing you.

 *Signed:* 
 *Dr. Allen Iboi*

‎[15/05/2025, 16:33:02] ~ Chronicles & scrubs: *ACPN EDO MARKS WORLD HYPERTENSION DAY 2025* 

Dear colleagues,
Please be informed that World Hypertension Day 2025 comes up on Saturday  17th May.

As community pharmacists, we play a pivotal role in the detection, prevention, management, counselling and referral services of HYPERTENSION as a public health burden. Preventive healthcare information, disease identification and effective management of hypertension are core components of our practice.

Therefore, the EDO ACPN invites you to join her as we mark this year's world hypertension day with  a public healthcare awareness and intervention outreach in IYARO community Benin City.
The choice of this location is due to the aggregation of motor parks and drivers who do long distance travels and hardly check their blood pressure despite being a high risk group.
The details of the outreach are as follows:
*Date:* Saturday 17th May, 2025
*Time:* 10.00 am
*Venue:* NNPC Filling Station, IYARO bus stop, after Iyare motor park.

Community Pharmacists are encouraged to turn up enmass for this outreach and also come along with the following;
* A Lab coat
* A BP monitoring device (manual or digital)
* Short dated antihypertensives if available 
* Other short dated medications (supplements, antidiabetics, analgesics, etc) if available 
* Glucometer devices and strips.

I look forward to seeing you.

 *Signed:* 
 *Dr. Allen Iboi*

‎[16/05/2025, 04:28:39] ~ Lancelot: *WHY YOU MUST NEVER USE TETRACYCLINE AND ISOTRETINOIN CAPSULE* 

Minocycline was one of the scarce medication in Nigeria recently obtained for a client known to belong to the class of tetracycline. Even though minocycline can be used for several condition ,you much watch out for some dangers as well as other tetracycline when combining with other medications 

*DANGERS OF USING MINOCYCLINE OR TETRACYCLINES WITH ISOTRETINOIN  INDICATED BOTH FOR TREATMENT OF ACNE*
Most common life threatening effect is increase in cranial pressure which result into permanent vision loss(permanent blindness)  known as pseudotumor cerebri.

*MEDICAL INTERVENTION* 
If you see a prescription that comes to you combining tetracycline with Isotretinoin capsule, please return back to the doctor as it could  save the patient life as well as millions of life.

Or

Another approach to using Minocycline with Isotretinoin capsule is as follows 
There is usually a *WASH-OUT PERIOD*  or *DRUG FREE PERIOD* which is a period between discontinuation of tetracycline and the start of isotretinoin capsule usually a 5-7days gap

*CONCLUSION*
Kick against the use of self-medication by clients and educate them to always seek a medical practitioner

‎[17/05/2025, 10:02:02] ~ Lancelot: *LORUNDROSTAT ,THE MIRACLE DRUG THAT IS WHAT IS PROMISED TO BE  SUPERIOR TO  POTASSIUM SPARING DIURETIC E.G SPIRONOLACTONE AND EPLERERONE AND POTASSIUM SPARING DIURETICS PITFALLS* - _from the American College of Cardiology's 2025 scientific  Session last held in March 2025_


If a standard drug combination for treating hypertension (a thiazide diuretic, a calcium channel blocker, and an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker) does not adequately control BP, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), typically spironolactone, is added


But Hey!!!
Potassium sparing diuretics has some downsides that affect significantly a large proportion of Males than females. 

*MECHANISM OF POTASSIUM SPARING DIURETICS*

Spironolactone binds to intracellular aldosterone receptors as an antagonist,a receptor to which aldosterone is suppose to bind to.So been able to prevent binding of aldosterone, aldosterone level in the body begins to rises.

*PITFALLS OF POTASSIUM SPARING DIURETICS*

Due to the Nongenomic effect of aldosterone level , client have high tendency to have erectile dysfunction (due to reduce in nitric oxide synthesis by altering the activity of nitric oxide synthase).

Secondly, Aldosterone increase oxidative stress by increasing reactive oxygen species which could result into more cardiovascular and health issues.


*HERE BELOW YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT THE BREAKTHROUGH DRUG "LORUNDROSTAT" WHICH JUST PASSED LATELY PHASE 2 CLINICAL TRIAL*

Lorundrostat 50mg  who has just passed it's phase 2 clinical trial conducted by the Cleveland Clinical Cardiologist ascertain that a 50mg is more  beneficial in lower uncontrolled hypertension than escalated doses like 100mg with negligible impact . Lorundrostat was shown to be an aldosterone synthase inhibitor,reducing the level of aldosterone production unlike Spironolactone that only act as a aldosterone receptors blocker or antagonist while aldosterone level keeps on rising.

*Alleviate ST segment depression of ECG*

*Nicardipine* (also effective as migraine prophylaxis) unlike other CCBs.Though Nicardipine causes reflex tachycardia but about 98% of them showed improvement in ST depression of ECG despite a temporal reflex tachycardia 

*Esmolol*
A. (also effective as migraine prophylaxis due to it selective beta blocking activity of Beta 1 receptor) as a Beta Blocker agent.
B. *Esmolol* as a beta blockers have no reflex tachycardia effect when lowering blood pressure.

*Worsens ST segment depression of ECG*

*Hydralazine* (causes reflex tachycardia that leads to myocardial ischemia)

*Nitroprusside* (by potentially reducing blood flow to ischemic areas of the heart thereby causing ischemia ,worsen ST segment depression)

*No impact on ST segment depression* (neutral)
*Amlodipine*

[20/05/2025, 09:38:10] ~ Pharm. Theo: Dear Parent, Let’s Talk.

Not every child will be a doctor.
Not every child will love maths.
Not every child will shine in class.
But every child carries something God put inside them.

Some children are quiet, but they observe deeply.
Some are always singing, drawing, or fixing things.
Some are natural leaders—even if they can’t sit still in class.
Every child has a spark. Your job is to notice it early.

Stop comparing your child to others.
Your neighbour’s child is not your standard.
Your child is not a mistake—they are a message.
They came with an assignment only they can fulfil.

Have you prayed for your children this morning?
Did you mention them by name?
Each one has a different calling, a different struggle, and a different need.
One may need boldness.
Another may need peace.
Another may need direction.

Your prayers are not small—they are spiritual investments.

So look again.
Watch closely.
Listen without judging.
Guide them gently.

One day that small gift you noticed will become a global solution.

If this speaks to you, share it.
Another parent needs this reminder.

#RaisingWiseChildren #ParentingWithPurpose #CallThemByName

Pharm. Stephen Theophilus

[31/05/2025, 08:48:59] Consultant Pharmacist YPGd: 📣Update from NAFDAC!

NATIONAL AGENCY FOR FOOD & DRUG ADMINISTRATION AND CONTROL (NAFDAC)

Regulatory Directive on Discontinuation of Registration of some Fixed-Dose Combination (FDC) Drugs
Purpose:
This regulatory directive aims to discontinue the registration of some Fixed-Dose Combination (FDC) drugs due to the risks associated with product safety.  The therapeutic justifications for these FDCs have not been established and irrational therapy with accompanying Adverse Drug Reactions (ADR) have been well documented. These FDCs are banned in several countries including India (which is a major source of these medicines) because they were found to pose risks to human health.
Scope:
This Regulatory Directive applies to locally and imported pharmaceutical Fixed-Dose Combinations (FDCs) in which new, renewal and variation applications are not received anymore.

Directive Details:
The control or discontinuation is imperative because of the increased risk of liver and kidney damage 
 caused by these Fixed-Dose Combinations. In view of the foregoing, the Agency will no longer 
accept applications for new, renewal and variations for the attached list of the locally and 
imported versions of these medicines.

TIRZEPATIDE (TIZARO)


*REFERENCE IS SITED BELOW (on the last session)*

SOME THINGS ABOUT TIRZEPATIDE YOU MAY NOT KNOW

TIRZEPATIDE A NOVEL ANTIDIABETIC MEDICATION
It was approved recently by USA and EU for the treatment of Type 2 diabetes and obesity after passing Phasing 3 clinical trial.

This drug was very effective even as a once of week dosing therapy helps promotes compliance .

CLIENTS DEMOGRAPHICS 

✓Greater than 30 kg/M² in BMI
✓Have  Obstructive sleep apnea e.g Snoring Issues
✓ Above 18years of age
✓Type 2 diabetes and or hypertension.

Phase 3 Clinical trial results 



CONCLUSIVE STUDIES OF TIRZEPATIDE AGAINST OTHER ANTI-DIABETIC MEDICATION 

 1. 23–62% of participants achieved normoglycemia (HbA1c < 5.7%), vs. participants treated with semaglutide 1 mg (20%), insulin degludec (5%), and insulin glargine (3%) [9]. 
Normoglycemia was achieved without clinically significant hypoglycemia in 93.6–100% patients when tirzepatide was not combined with insulin and in 85.9% patients when tirzepatide was added to insulin.
 2. TIRZEPATIDE had a significant improvement from baseline of  glycated haemoglobin percentage by 1.87-2.59%,weight loss by 6.2kg to 12.9kg over 4 weeks treatment as compared to insulin glargine and insulin degludec.

3. In the phase 3  clinical trial program, weight loss in adults with T2DM treated with tirzepatide 5, 10, and 15 mg was associated with an improvement in weight-related.

[03/06/2025, 07:49:09] Sir Hope Onyemaechi: *HEALTH NOTICE IN MEDICINE DEPARTMENT*
Good afternoon Professors, Senior Colleagues and Colleagues.

I wish to bring to our attention that some of us may have noticed a recent trend in patients presenting to UBTH either via the Emergency or GPC.

Initial findings show that these patients present with;

-Fever (usually high grade)
-GI symptoms (Diarrhea, Vomiting, Epigastric pain/discomfort which is usually severe) -Occasionally, joint pains
-Respiratory symptoms e.g cough with reduced oxygen saturation 
-Skin findings of purpura, ecchymosis
-Leucocytosis
-Anaemia
-Thrombocytopenia 
-Renal impairment that may require HD
-Other non specific symptoms

Patients usually are quite ill and unfortunately we have lost some of them.

We have also observed that females are more affected in this recent trend.

It is believed there must be a yet to be identified infectious agent responsible for these symptoms.

We have had to do a lot of lassa PCR in recent times however, we haven't had any positive results so far.

RDT for yellow fever isn't confirmatory and definitive diagnosis for this takes days...same thing for Dengue fever.

Only Lassa fever has a specific therapy aside managing complications like renal failure with HD.

Yellow fever and Dengue fever have no specific treatment...treatment is largely symptoms based.

The reason for this health notice is for us to watch out for these symptoms as a department because most of the patients end up with Medicine Department.

Secondly, there is the need for us to be more proactive in the care of the patients with respect to fever control, pain control, appropriate fluid and electrolyte replacement, transfusion (preferably fresh blood) and haemodialysis as quickly as possible while surveillance efforts are increased to identify the possible infectious agent.

It will be appreciated if our residents can provide a summary of patients we have managed recently including mortalities in order for us to have a look and possibly identify a pattern.

information needed include;
-Biodata (Names, Age, Gender, Address,  Occupation, Marital status etc)
-Presenting symptoms 
-Positive clinical findings 
-Lab results available (Urinalysis, FBC/ESR, E/U/Cr, HIV, LFT, MP, CXR etc.)

Kindly send these info to my WhatsApp no: 08078674356 or my email: bensonokwara81@gmail.com 

*Lastly and very importantly too, let us all strictly observe standard precaution while providing care for our ailing patients.*

Thank you.

Dr. Benson Okwara

[04/06/2025, 16:55:33] Sir Hope Onyemaechi: *EDO HEALTH COMMISSIONER CONVENES EMERGENCY MEETING OVER DIPHTHERIA OUTBREAK*

The Edo State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Cyril Adams Oshiomhole, has convened an emergency meeting with key health stakeholders following the confirmation of a diphtheria outbreak in the state.

This swift action follows an official report from the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) confirming five cases of diphtheria, including two deaths. The meeting, which took place in Benin City, brought together representatives from the World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, local health institutions, and other critical partners to address the urgent public health situation.

Dr. Oshiomhole described the outbreak as a “serious cause for concern,” warning that diphtheria, a highly contagious bacterial infection affecting the nose and throat, could lead to severe complications or death if not treated promptly.

“The rise in cases, coupled with other growing health threats such as drug resistance and viral infections, underscores the need for immediate and coordinated action across the sector,” he stated.

The Commissioner outlined key focus areas from the emergency meeting, including:
	•	Deployment of a Rapid Response Team
	•	Strengthening coordination between state and local health facilities
	•	Enhancing surveillance and contact tracing
	•	Improving public awareness and community engagement
	•	Ensuring availability and access to vaccines

Dr. Oshiomhole commended UBTH for their prompt action and lauded the continued support of international and local health partners. He assured the public that the Edo State Government, under the leadership of His Excellency Governor Monday Okpebholo, is fully committed to halting the spread of the disease.

Citizens have been advised to report symptoms such as sore throat, fever, and difficulty breathing early, and to avoid close contact with infected individuals. The Commissioner also urged the public to remain calm but vigilant.

“This is not the time to panic, but to prepare, educate, and act responsibly,” he added.
[04/06/2025, 16:55:52] Sir Hope Onyemaechi: *Diphtheria outbreak — All you need to know* 

Diphtheria is a serious bacterial infection caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae. It primarily affects the mucous membranes of the throat and nose but can also affect the skin and other body parts.

🔬 *Key Facts*
	•	Cause: Corynebacterium diphtheriae
	•	Transmission: Spread through respiratory droplets (coughing, sneezing) or direct contact with infected wounds or surfaces.
	•	Incubation Period: 2–5 days

⚠️ *Symptoms*
	•	Sore throat
	•	Fever
	•	Swollen glands in the neck
	•	Weakness
	•	A thick gray or white coating on the throat, tonsils, or nose
	•	Difficulty breathing or swallowing (in severe cases)

If untreated, the toxins released by the bacteria can cause:
	•	Myocarditis (inflammation of the heart)
	•	Paralysis
	•	Respiratory failure
	•	Death

🧪 *Diagnosis*
	•	Clinical signs (especially the throat membrane)
	•	Throat swab culture or PCR test

💊 *Treatment*
	•	Antitoxin to neutralize the diphtheria toxin
	•	Antibiotics (e.g., penicillin or erythromycin)
	•	Isolation to prevent spreading to others
	•	Monitoring for complications (especially heart and nerves)

🛡️ *Prevention*
	•	Vaccination: DTP or DTaP (Diphtheria, Tetanus, and Pertussis)
	•	Part of routine childhood immunizations
	•	Booster doses recommended for teens and adults

*PRACTICE IMPROVEMENT TRAINING COURSE FOR PHARMACISTS - WHY YOU CANNOT AFFORD TO MISS OUT*

Dear Colleagues,
Permit me to reemphasize the importance or imperativeness of the proposed practice improvement training course for pharmacists as follows:
* The course title - *understanding, interpretation and application of routine laboratory investigations and execution of point of care tests*  speaks largely to the foundation of modern day community pharmacy practice. You must be well equipped in order to provide valuable services in your practice 
* This is an international training brought to you cheaply at your convenience. The facilitators are drawn from multiple disciplines in the healthcare sector within and outside Nigeria. The quality of this training is too much for you to miss.
* You must appreciate the effort of your leaders - a lot had gone into the conception, planning and execution of this programme up to this point. People are working round the clock to ensure this training succeed and all you have to do is to subscribe for the training for your own good.
* This is easily the most valuable event of our administration.

THE NUMBERS ARE NOT ENCOURAGING FOR NOW. I know you will register and participate in this training but the time is short. Online classes begin on the 16th of June 2025.
PLEASE REGISTER FOR THIS TRAINING. No fall my hand 😊

Thank You
Dr. Allen IBOI
Chairman, ACPN
Edo State.

‎[12/06/2025, 07:04:13] Wellington: *🩸DEMOCRACY DAY*

As Nigerians commemorate this 12th day of June as 'Democracy Day', it is indeed a memorable and an eventful period in the history of our existence as a people, nation and a democratic independent entity.

This indeed calls for celebration that we could still stand as a people, a nation and a voice, despite all odds and challenges over the years. 

We urge the Government at all tiers to learn from the obstacles we overcame as a Country, and the progress we made thus far, to help strengthen the plans that we have in place to put Nigeria back on the path of progress.

I wish to state unequivocally that the Focal Point and Central Theme of Democracy is the people. Government of the PEOPLE, by the PEOPLE, and for the PEOPLE. Therefore, Government must show unconditional concern for the people it governs. 

Workable techniques and solutions should be swiftly deployed to stop the incessant killings across the country. Adequate security measures should also be taken with drastic approaches towards stopping the ill-acts.
Government should as a matter of fact make  healthcare and pharmaceutical services  a priority because a healthy nation is  a wealthy nation. 

I sincerely want to congratulate all pharmacists in Edo State on today's commemoration of this important day in our democratic calendar. 

God bless Nigeria!



Signed;
Pharm. Chris Oisakede MAW

*📍PSN CLEARANCE*

1. Kindly make all your dues payment via Pharmagateway website (www. Pharmagateway.com.ng) or Pharmpay (download via Google play store).

2. After making your payment download the receipt for subsequent usage.

3. Log on to PSN EDO website *(www.psnedo.com)* Fill in all necessary information and upload your dues  payment slip from Pharmagateway or Pharmpay. 

4. As a first timer on the website you are expected to Sign up first

5. Your subsequent log in details will be;
 *Username: Phone Number*
 *Number Password: PCN Reg number*

6. After registration, you may have to wait for sometime to get your clearance slip on your dashboard.

‎[17/06/2025, 19:16:35] PHARM(DR)OTAKHOR JENNIFER: *YOUNG PHARMACISTS CONDEMN BENUE MASSACRE, MOURN LOSS OF COLLEAGUE, AND CALL FOR URGENT GOVERNMENT ACTION.*

The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria – Young Pharmacists Group (PSN-YPG) is heartbroken and outraged by the recent massacre in Benue State on Friday, June 13, which claimed the lives of over 200 innocent Nigerians, including one of our own, *Pharm. Matthew Lormba*, a dedicated Community Pharmacist and graduate of the University of Jos.

We condemn, in the strongest possible terms, this senseless and barbaric act of violence against unarmed and innocent civilians, many of whom were Christians, targeted simply for their faith and existence in their own homeland. The brutal murder of *Pharm. Matthew Lormba*, a young Pharmacist committed to serving his community through healthcare, is a painful reminder of the deepening insecurity that continues to plague our nation.

It is particularly disheartening that at a time when Nigeria is facing a dangerous brain drain in the health sector, driven by unfavorable working conditions and lack of institutional support, those who have chosen to stay back and serve are not even guaranteed the safety of their own lives.

We call on the Federal Government to act decisively and proactively in safeguarding the lives and properties of all Nigerians. 

The situation in Benue and other parts of the country demands urgent and sustained intervention. The Nigerian people can no longer afford to live under constant threat, nor can we continue to bury the brightest minds of our future due to preventable violence.

We stand in grief and solidarity with the family of Pharm. Matthew Lormba, with the people of Benue State, and with all communities across Nigeria devastated by such acts of terror. We therefore demand justice, not only for Matthew but for every innocent life lost. 

*These killings must end.*

May the souls of all the departed rest in peace. May the conscience of our leaders be stirred toward true accountability and security for all.

Signed,

Tekena George 
National Chairman, PSN-YPG ‎image omitted

‎[25/06/2025, 15:46:16] ~ Dr.  Lisa Mote: 🌏 *June 25 – World Vitiligo Day: 7 facts about Vitiligo*

🔸 Vitiligo is a skin condition where patches of skin lose their pigment.
🔸 It happens when the body’s immune system attacks pigment-producing cells (melanocytes).
🔸 Vitiligo is not contagious, not an infection, and not caused by poor hygiene.
🔸 It can affect anyone—regardless of race, gender, or age.

‎[26/06/2025, 07:37:45] Sir Prof  Pharm Abu Dantani John: Today, the ACPN Edo, join the world to mark *"International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking"*

This year's theme is, *"The Evidence is Clear, Invest in Prevention"*

The initiative aims to strengthen coordination and collaboration and prevent the initiation of substance use through evidence-based interventions such as promoting life skills education in both schools and workplaces.

Rather than relying on punitive measures, it promotes policies and regulations that prioritize evidence-based treatments and harm reduction programmes across health and social care systems, and advocates for evidence-based interventions for drug use disorders to be embedded in UHC benefit packages.

To expedite implementation of the substance use flagship initiative, the Regional Office has established a Regional Strategic and Technical Advisory Group on Mental Health and Substance Use and a Regional Coalition of Civil Society Organizations for Mental Health and Substance Use Prevention to engage and empower civil society organizations, and people with lived experience of drug use disorders, to advance public health actions across the Region.

The flagship initiative calls for decisive, collective action to address one of the most urgent public health challenges of our time. Through investments in sustainable, evidence-based solutions, we can significantly improve public health outcomes and foster social stability for future generations. 

Given current resource constraints, the need for effective collaboration is greater than ever. We must join forces, align our strategies, and pursue joint actions to achieve more with less.

On the International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, WHO urges governments, health organizations, and communities across the Eastern Mediterranean Region and globally to unite in combating drug use disorders. Together, we can create a healthier future for all by ensuring that everyone, everywhere, has access to the care and support they need.

The Regional flagship initiative on accelerating public health action on substance use is a call for decisive, collective action to confront one of the most pressing public health challenges of our time. With the right investments in sustainable, evidence-based solutions, we can significantly reduce morbidity, mortality, and the social costs associated with drug use disorders and build a more stable society.

[26/06/2025, 21:28:13] King Penet: *Highlights of the New Tax Reform Bills signed into law today:*

Here is what the new development means for Nigeria and Nigerians:

- Federal Inland Reveneu Service (FIRS) will now become Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS)

- The  Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) will now collect revenues previously handled by agencies such as the  Nigeria Customs Service, NUPRC, NPA, and NIMASA. 

- Tax exemption for workers earning  ₦800,000 and below annually. 

- 25% personal income tax applies only to individuals earning  above ₦50 million annually. 

- Small businesses owners are exempted from paying  income tax.

- Company income tax for medium and large companies will be reduced from  30% to 25% starting in 2026. 

- Value Added Tax (VAT) exemptions on essential goods and services consumed by the poor, including food items, medical services, pharmaceuticals, educational fees, and electricity.

- VAT remains at 7.5%, and  corporate income tax stays at 30%. NO INCREMENT!

- Introduction of a Development Levy ranging from 4% to 2%, allocated to support the NELFUND, TETFund, NITDA, and NASENI.

[27/06/2025, 18:39:34] King Penet: Nigeria’s 2025 Tax Overhaul: What Small Retailers (e.g. a Benin City Pharmacy) Need to Know

In late June 2025, President Bola Tinubu signed four new tax laws aiming to simplify Nigeria’s taxes and modernize collection.  These laws (effective Jan 1, 2026) merge many old tax rules into unified bills for income taxes, VAT, and tax administration.  For a small pharmacy in Benin City, the key changes affect VAT, corporate tax, personal income tax, and new compliance rules.  Below we explain each in plain language and show how a typical pharmacy might be affected (pricing, filings, payroll, etc.).

Value-Added Tax (VAT) Changes

Under the new law, the VAT rate **stays at 7.5%**.  This means most products (including non-essential pharmacy items) are still taxed 7.5%.  However, many everyday goods have been moved to 0% VAT: essential foods, health and education items (which would include most medicines or drugs for patients) are VAT-exempt.  For example, if a cough syrup now costs ₦10,000, a 7.5% VAT would have added ₦750 before.  With the reform, if that syrup is classified as a healthcare item, the pharmacy can charge only ₦10,000 (no extra VAT).  This cut in VAT on medicines makes them cheaper for customers.

Another big VAT change is how revenue is shared between federal, state and local governments.  Now “each state will keep 30% of the VAT it generates” locally.  In practice, this means Edo State will directly benefit from VAT collected on sales in Benin City.  Of the remaining VAT, 50% is split equally among all states and 20% by population.  (Local government areas also get a share.)  For the pharmacy, this doesn’t change what it charges, but it means Edo State has more incentive to grow business and improve services (since it keeps more of the VAT you collect).

Finally, businesses can now recover input VAT on all purchases.  If the pharmacy buys inventory, equipment or even pays for electricity, it can claim back that VAT in its filings.  In effect, the pharmacy only pays VAT on the markup it charges, not on its costs.  This lowers the net VAT the business owes each tax period.

Corporate Income Tax Changes

If the pharmacy is set up as a company, company tax remains 30% on profits.  However, one welcome change is that very small companies pay nothing.  The new law exempts companies with annual revenue under ₦50 million from corporate tax.  In practical terms, a tiny pharmacy making ₦40m a year (with modest profit) would owe zero company tax, saving potentially millions.  If turnover exceeds ₦50m, profits are taxed at 30% as before.  (This threshold was raised from what it used to be, so slightly larger “small” businesses now qualify.)

For example, say the pharmacy’s sales are ₦100m but its profit is ₦10m.  Under the old rules it would pay about ₦3m tax (30% of profit).  Under the new rule, it still pays 30% (≈₦3m) because profit exists, unless the whole company earned under ₦50m.  Many micro-retailers will fall under the threshold and pay no company tax.

Also, with the new laws, any VAT the pharmacy paid on its purchases (stock, equipment, etc.) is fully creditable against VAT owed.  So if the pharmacy bought ₦10,000 of goods with ₦750 VAT, it can deduct that ₦750 from its VAT bill.  This only raises the pharmacy’s corporate tax (since taxable profit = revenue minus costs) if it no longer expensed that VAT.  In simple terms: the pharmacy must file VAT return and can offset input VAT, lowering its net VAT payable.

Personal Income Tax (PIT) and Payroll

Employees and owners who draw salaries are also better off under the new tax rules.  The tax-free salary threshold rises from ₦300,000 to ₦800,000 per year.  In other words, anyone earning ₦800,000 or less annually (about ₦66,667 per month) pays no income tax, up from the old ₦300k limit.  Above that, income is taxed in new bands (for example, 15% on the next portion of income).  For a pharmacy worker earning ₦100,000 a month (₦1.2m yearly), only the amount above ₦800k is taxed.  The result is that lower-paid staff keep more of their pay.

Importantly, the reform also changes payroll procedure.  Going forward, every employee must file an annual tax return covering all their income (not just relying on PAYE withholding).  For a small pharmacy, this means continuing to deduct PAYE from wages, but also ensuring workers get their full Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and file any personal tax forms.  (For example, if an assistant works extra hours or does a side job, they must report that income too.)

New Compliance Rules & Penalties

The tax overhaul brings stricter compliance and digital filing requirements.  For instance, all taxpayers now need a TIN and must provide it for everyday transactions.  To open a bank account, apply for government services, or even contract with public bodies, the pharmacy (and its employees) must show a tax ID.  Banks will report large transactions to the tax authorities: any individual moving over ₦50m in a month or a business moving ₦250m will trigger a report.

There is also a move toward electronic processes.  The new Tax Administration law introduces VAT fiscalization and e-invoicing.  In practice, this means the pharmacy may need to issue digital receipts or use a government portal when filing VAT returns.  A “National Single Window” system will streamline filings, so eventually the pharmacy might file one online tax return instead of many paper forms.

Penalties for non-compliance have been updated.  For example, failing to register or file on time can incur fines – roughly ₦50,000 for the first month and ₦25,000 for each month overdue.  (Importantly, the law removed imprisonment for unspecified offences.)  This means it’s crucial for the Benin City pharmacy to stay registered, file returns, and meet deadlines.  Getting a TIN early (before opening bank accounts) and keeping proper records will avoid these new fines.

Everyday Impact: Pricing, Filing, Payroll (Examples)

To see how this plays out, consider a typical Benin City pharmacy:

Product pricing (VAT effects): A bottle of pain relievers costing ₦8,000 would formerly have ₦600 VAT included (total ₦8,600).  If the reform deems it an essential medicine (0% VAT), the pharmacy can charge ₦8,000 only, making it cheaper and more competitive.  Even for non-exempt items (like cosmetic products), the rate is still 7.5%, so the price to consumers is unchanged. The pharmacy’s paperwork will simply record any VAT collected on sales and subtract any VAT paid on supplies.

Company tax (profits): Suppose the pharmacy’s annual revenue is ₦40m and its profit is ₦4m.  Under old rules it paid about 30% of ₦4m = ₦1.2m in company tax.  Under the new law, because ₦40m < ₦50m, the pharmacy pays no company tax at all.  That saves ₦1.2m, which could be reinvested in the business.  If one year the pharmacy’s sales grow to ₦60m (profit say ₦6m), it would then pay 30% of ₦6m = ₦1.8m as usual.  Either way, being aware of the ₦50m cutoff is important for financial planning.

Payroll (personal tax): Imagine a staff member earns ₦80,000 per month (₦960,000 yearly).  This was slightly above the old tax-free level, so they would have paid a small tax.  Now it is just under the new ₦800k threshold, so they pay no income tax.  The pharmacy can therefore increase take-home pay at the same gross salary.  For higher earners, the pharmacy must update payroll software to apply the new rate table.  Each employee will also need to submit an annual tax return, but for junior staff the return will simply show “no tax due.”

Tax filing: Going forward, the pharmacy will file taxes under the new unified laws.  Instead of separate outdated forms, it can eventually use the government’s e-portal (when available) to file VAT and income tax returns together.  The bookkeeping will require digital invoices or receipts that link to the tax system.  In practice, the pharmacy’s accountant will register on the new Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) portal and file returns online.  Because the VAT base and rates haven’t suddenly changed (except exemptions), and company tax is the same rate (just a threshold change), the learning curve is mainly in new forms and IT procedures.


In summary, these tax reforms give small retailers some relief (no company tax under ₦50m, higher personal tax-free wage, lower VAT on essentials) while introducing stricter administration (mandatory tax IDs, digital filing, and tougher enforcement).  A Benin City pharmacy that adapts early—getting its TIN, training staff to file new returns, and adjusting prices if needed—will benefit from the changes and avoid penalties.  Keeping clear sales records and using proper invoicing software will make compliance easier under the new system.

Sources: Information above is drawn from official reports on the 2025 Nigerian tax reforms and related news analysis. Each citation points to the relevant detail in the reform laws and expert summaries.

[28/06/2025, 12:52:11] Sir Hope Onyemaechi: A Guarantor is not a Surety and definitely not a Referee

Let’s get this straight.

A lot of people confuse these terms.
Some even think they all mean the same thing.

They don’t.

When you stand as a Guarantor, you are giving the lender a promise that you will pay if the borrower fails to pay after all steps have been taken to recover the debt from the borrower first.

The borrower must first default.

The lender must first exhaust all means to get the borrower to pay.

Only then can they come for you as the guarantor.

But when you stand as a Surety, it’s more serious.

A surety is like saying, “If this person doesn’t pay on the due date, come straight to me. No need to chase them first.”

In other words, as a surety, you’re equally and immediately liable once there’s default.

Now, let’s talk about Referees.

Some people think being a guarantor is the same thing as being a referee.
It’s not.

A referee is simply someone who confirms that the person applying for a job, loan, or apartment is known to them and has good character.
That’s all.

A referee is not taking on any financial responsibility. A referee is not liable to pay any debt.They are just vouching for the person’s behaviour, not their ability to repay loans.

So next time you’re asked to be a guarantor, surety, or referee understand exactly what you’re signing up for.

One carries serious financial risk.

One comes with immediate liability.

The other? Just character reference.

Be wise. Read before you sign. Don’t let friendship or emotions drag you into debt.

‎[06/07/2025, 13:59:12] Stanley Sunday Ypgd: *PRESS RELEASE NO.152/EDSGH/2025* 

*OFFICE OF THE GOVERNOR*
*EDO STATE GOVERNMENT*

*GOV OKPEBHOLO APPROVES ₦1 BILLION ANNUAL BURSARY FOR EDO STUDENTS IN TERTIARY INSTITUTIONS* 

The Executive Governor of Edo State, His Excellency, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has approved the sum of ₦1 billion as bursary support for students of Edo State origin in tertiary institutions across the country.

Governor Okpebholo, during a town hall meeting with young people in Edo State recently, pledged to look into a passionate request made by various youth leaders. 

The youths, had requested for the introduction of bursaries to assist Edo indigenes pursuing higher education in various institutions nationwide. 

The approval of the bursary initiative by Governor Okpebholo, barely eight months in office, is expected to become an annual program designed to ease the financial burden on students and their families. 

According to Governor Okpebholo, eligibility for the bursary will be based on proper verification through the applicant’s Local Government of Origin to ensure that only genuine indigenes of the State benefit from the scheme.

Governor Okpebholo emphasized that the initiative aligns with his administration’s broader vision to enhance access to quality education, encourage academic excellence, and support the aspirations of Edo youths to contribute meaningfully to the development of the State and the nation.

Further details on application procedures and timelines will be made available by the various relevant government agencies.

*Signed*:
*Fred Itua*,
*The Chief Press Secretary to Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State.*
*Sunday, 6 July, 2025*. ‎image omitted

‎[10/07/2025, 10:13:41] Dr. Joshua Idemudia (PharmD) Ypgd: *PSN-YPG BYE-LAW AMENDMENT*

🔰Following the PSN-YPG Congress held at the Annual General Meeting during the 6th PSN-YPG National Conference in Kano State on 9th July 2025, and in line with Article 16:8 of the National Bye-Law, the Congress hereby resolves and adopts the following amendments:

1. *Tenure of Office*

🔰The tenure of office for both Chapter Officers and the National Central Executive Council shall be for a period of two (2) years, within which elections must be conducted. This shall take effect from November 2026.

2. *Frequency of the National Conference*

🔰The PSN-YPG National Conference shall henceforth be held biennially (once every two years) by a State Chapter. This shall also take effect from November 2026.

- The National Conference shall be held within the second quarter of the second year in each two-year tenure cycle.

- The host state Chapter shall be announced at the preceding conference, following a successful bidding process.

- The PSN-YPG National Conference shall not be held in the same state as the
PSN National Conference, that year. 

- To qualify as a host, State Chapters must meet the following criteria (among others):

A. Demonstrated capacity to host Young Pharmacists from across the country.

B. Active participation in PSN-YPG activities for at least the past two (2) years.

C. Assurance of safety and security to provide a conducive environment for all delegates.

3. *Review of the National Bye-Law*

🔰The Congress adopts the immediate review of the PSN-YPG National Bye-Law and mandates the Central Executive Council to set up a Bye-Law Review Committee in line with Article 13.7(ii) of the Bye-Law.

🔰It’s been four days since we drew the curtain on the 6th Annual National Conference of Young Pharmacists held in Kano State.

🔰 As part of our administration’s agenda, we committed to delivering a National Conference that prioritizes value for Young Pharmacists, strengthens our association, and advances advocacy for medicine security in Nigeria, highlighting the vital role of Young Pharmacists in building resilient supply chain systems while enhancing their professional capacity.

🔰 With over 280 registered delegates, we are immensely grateful to God Almighty for His grace, mercy, and the incredible people who made it possible to bring Young Pharmacists from across the country together to connect, grow, and build a stronger community.

*Highlights from the Conference include:*

✨ Excursion Activities: Delegates visited the first Coordinated Pharmaceutical Wholesale Centre established in Kano State, and explored the rich cultural heritage of Gidan Makama and the Ancient Dye Pit Centre.

The NAFDAC–Youth Against Drug Abuse project will be implemented in Rivers, Lagos, Abuja, Plateau, Borno, Kano, and Anambra States. It will commence in September 2025 and will open up volunteer opportunities for Young Pharmacists nationwide.

✨ Supply Chain Symposium & Business Roundtable: Featuring distinguished experts who shared actionable strategies to strengthen local Pharmaceutical supply chains and build sustainable business models.

*Strengthening the PSN-YPG Structure.*

During the Congress held at the Annual General Meeting, key amendments were made to our National Bye-Law in line with Articles 16.8 and 16.9. These changes are geared toward strengthening institutional structures, enhancing partner confidence, and aligning PSN-YPG with long-term development goals. The amendments are:

🔖 The tenure of office for State Chapter and Central Executive Council members shall now be two (2) years, effective from November 2026.

🔖 National Conferences shall henceforth be held biennially (once every two years), effective from November 2026. Future conference dates shall fall within the second quarter of the second year of a two-year tenure cycle.

🔖 The Congress unanimously mandated the Central Executive Council to immediately set up a Bye-Law Review Committee in line with Article 13.7(ii), to align the National Bye-Law with our evolving realities.

[15/07/2025, 22:24:46] Okosodo Joshua Ypgd: 📘 Topic: PharmD vs MBBS – A Comparative Insight into Two Health Degrees

PharmD (Doctor of Pharmacy) and MBBS (Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery) are two distinct professional programs in the health sciences. While both aim to improve patient care and outcomes, they differ in training, scope, and career paths.

🔍 Key Differences Between PharmD and MBBS

Here’s a breakdown of how the two degrees compare in terms of:

💡 1. Curriculum

Though both are health-related programs, their academic content and structure differ greatly.

PharmD:
Trained under the Faculty/College of Pharmacy, the curriculum emphasizes pharmaceutical sciences, pharmacology, clinical pharmacy, pharmaceutics, and public health.
Students learn drug discovery, development, formulation, dispensing, and therapeutic optimization.

MBBS:
Trained under the Faculty/College of Medicine, the curriculum focuses on anatomy, physiology, pathology, internal medicine, surgery, and clinical rotations in hospitals.

🎯 2. Program Focus

PharmD Graduates (Pharmacist Doctors) focus on:

Ensuring safe and effective medication use

Patient counseling & consultation

Optimizing drug therapy outcomes

Clinical research & pharmacovigilance

Pharmaceutical care planning

MBBS Graduates (Medical Doctors) focus on:

Diagnosing and managing diseases

Prescribing appropriate medications or therapies

Performing surgical and non-surgical interventions

Ordering and interpreting diagnostic tests

Overseeing holistic patient care

🌐 3. Career Opportunities

PharmD holders can work in:

Hospital & Community Pharmacies

Pharmaceutical Industry & Regulatory Agencies

Research Institutions & Academia

Clinical Trials & Drug Development

Public Health & Policy Organizations

MBBS holders can work in:

Hospitals and Clinics

Private Practice

Surgical Centers

Medical Teaching & Research

Government & Public Health Agencies

📋 4. Scope of Practice

PharmD Professionals are licensed to:

Dispense and formulate medications

Manage drug therapy and medication reviews

Provide drug information and patient education

Participate in clinical rounds and collaborate with physicians

Engage in drug research and pharmacoeconomics

MBBS Professionals are licensed to:

Diagnose diseases and conditions

Prescribe treatments and medications

Perform surgeries and minor procedures

Interpret lab and imaging results

Provide direct clinical management

🩺 What About the Title “Doctor”?

Though PhDs are traditionally referred to as academic doctors, it's important to note that "Doctor" is also a professional title granted to licensed professionals in clinical fields like Medicine (MBBS) and Pharmacy (PharmD).

🔔 Therefore, PharmD graduates are fully entitled to the title "Doctor", just like their MBBS colleagues — not because they hold a PhD, but because they’ve earned a professional doctoral degree in pharmacy.

> ✅ In fact, addressing PharmD holders as "Dr." helps highlight their critical role in patient care, therapeutic management, and drug safety.

🧠 Final Thoughts

PharmD and MBBS are not superior or inferior to one another—they are complementary. The modern healthcare system thrives when pharmacists and physicians collaborate. While one diagnoses and prescribes, the other ensures the prescription is appropriate, safe, and effective.

Let’s respect every health professional’s path, and empower our PharmD graduates to carry their “Dr.” title with pride and responsibility.

Key Differences

[17/07/2025, 08:10:40] Okosodo Joshua Ypgd: ABOUT THE  DOCTOR OF PHARMACY ( PharmD) TRAINING IN AFRICA 

Globally speaking, a  Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD; Neo-Latin: Pharmaciae Doctor) is a professional doctorate in pharmacy.

In some countries, it is a proficient graduate degree to practice the profession of pharmacy or to become a CLINICAL PHARMACIST. In many countries, persons with their Doctor of Pharmacy degree are allowed to practice independently and can PRESCRIBE drugs directly to patients. 
A PharmD program has significant experiential and/or clinical education components in introductory and advanced levels for the safe and effective use of drugs. 
Experiential education prepares graduates to be practice-ready, as they already have spent a significant amount of time training in areas of direct patient care and research.

WITHIN THE BLACK CONTINENT.

SOUTH AFRICA 
Since 2006, Pharm.D is a post-graduate course being offered by Rhodes University.

TUNISIA.
The PharmD program has been available in Tunisia since 1975.
There is only one faculty in Tunisia that provides education for PharmD; Faculty of pharmacy of Monastir.

MOROCCO  
PharmD is a program offered at the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy of Rabat.[2] and the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy of Casablanca.

GHANA
PharmD is a 6-year course offered in Ghana from the academic year 2012/2013, initially by the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). It leads to the award of the Doctor of Pharmacy certificate making one eligible to qualify, register and operate as a licensed pharmacist

EGYPT.
PharmD is a professional degree in pharmaceutical sciences and according to newly adopted educational advancements, it is the minimum requirement to be licensed as a Pharmacist in Egypt, the curriculum consists of 6 years ( 5 years of Pharmaceutical & clinical studies followed by 1 year of Clinical internships ), this program is intended for students who have graduated from High school. As for the Pharmacists with a bachelor of Pharmaceutical Sciences who graduated before the decree of the new law, there is a Postgraduate PharmD offered by many faculties of Pharmacy for Pharmacists.

ALGERIA
In Algeria, Doctor of Pharmacy degree replaced the state's diploma of pharmacist in 2011, thus concepts on CLINICAL PHARMACY and PHARMACEUTICAL CARE were taught for the first time. Algeria has 01 Faculty of Pharmacy (University of Algiers 1) and 08 Pharmacy Department (University of Batna 2, University of Blida 1, University of Tlemcen, University of Tizi Ouzzou, University of Sétif 1, University of Sidi Bel Abbes, University of Annaba, University of Constantine 3).

NIGERIA 
These are the Universities that have commenced the PharmD program in Nigeria: University of Benin, Benin City, Bayero University, Kano, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, University of Jos, Gombe State University, Delta State University, Abraka, University of Ilorin, and University of Ibadan, and the State University of Medical And Applied Sciences, Igbo Eno. 
The University of Benin (Uniben) commenced the program in 2001 following the approval given for the commencement of the program by the regulatory government agency for pharmacy education and practice in the country, Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN). However, it was not until 2016 that the overall regulatory government agency for all university degree programs in the country, National Universities Commission (NUC), formally approved the PharmD degree program.

LIBERIA 
The University of Liberia (UL) offers a Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree through its School of Pharmacy, which is part of the UL College of Health Sciences (ULCHS). The PharmD program was approved in 2019 and implemented with the first cohort admitted in the 2021/2022 academic year. The School of Pharmacy was established in 1986 to develop human resources in the pharmaceutical sector in Liberia, Sierra Leone, and The Gambia. 

KENYA
In Kenya, the Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree is offered by the University of Nairob

ETHIOPIA 
Mekelle University in Ethiopia has launched  a PharmD program, which will be the first of its kind in the country.. 
The university's College of Pharmacy has already added a Post-Baccalaureate ( Postgraduate ) PharmD program, and it is working towards offering a traditional PharmD program. This development is part of a broader effort to modernize pharmacy education in Ethiopia, moving from a product-centered approach to a patient-centered one. The curriculum is being revised to include more clinical pharmacy and patient-focused training.

LECTURER I & II
Ph.D or Master degree plus three (3) years teaching experience with a minimum of 3 peer-reviewed Publications.

ASSISTANT LECTURER

INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL ADVERTISEMENT 
FOR ACADEMIC AND NON-ACADEMIC STAFF POSITIONS
		PART I
Applications are invited from suitably qualified candidates to fill the following academic and non-teaching positions in the University of Benin, Benin City.
This advertisement is open to both internal and external candidates and will run for six (6) weeks from the date of this publication.
UNIBEN Job Application Website:  unibenportal.uniben.edu    
Candidates should submit –via the online application portal, soft copies of their application with detailed Curriculum Vitae, photocopies of credentials and supporting documents. 
Any applicant for academic staff position with qualification less than Ph.D must possess a minimum of second class upper division in first degree qualification plus NYSC Discharge/Exemption Certificate.
The CV for Academic applications should be presented in the following order:

Research in Progress

Extracurricular Activities
Names and Addresses of Three Referees
