[14/11/2025, 08:54:39] Wellington: Vanguard News

PSN unveils bold vision to transform pharmacy education, practice in Nigeria
Health
November 12, 2025

PSN unveils bold vision to transform pharmacy education, practice in Nigeria
PSN unveils bold vision to transform pharmacy education, practice in Nigeria
By Chioma Obinna

The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria, PSN, has reaffirmed its commitment to building a competent, future-ready pharmaceutical workforce, setting a bold agenda for reform and excellence in education and practice.

Speaking at the opening ceremony of the 98th Annual National Conference of the PSN, themed DABO 2025, held in Kano recently, the President of the Society, Pharm. Tanko Ibrahim Ayuba, unveiled strategic reforms aimed at redefining pharmacy education, enhancing professional recognition, and consolidating recent victories in regulation and welfare.

“The pharmacy profession must build a new workforce that is holistic, broad-based, and versatile,” Ayuba declared. “Our vision is to make the Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D) the minimum entry level to practice pharmacy in Nigeria.”

According to the PSN President, the Society is intensifying efforts to strengthen academic and professional alignment in the training of pharmacists. The new roadmap focuses on enforcing the Pharm.D as the minimum qualification for practice, expanding postgraduate opportunities, and harmonising Ph.D and Fellowship programmes in pharmacy education.

Ayuba said this integration will produce a formidable pool of experts who can be both academics and consultant pharmacists, ensuring Nigeria’s pharmacy education meets global standards while addressing local health challenges.

“Our profession missed a golden opportunity to actualise this pathway over five years ago,” he noted. “This is the time to move forward—to elevate academic pharmacists to a platform of total practice of the profession.”

The PSN, he said, has fought long-standing battles to preserve the integrity of the profession. One major victory came when the Federal Ministry of Education directed the cessation of “Pharmacy Technologist” training in Nigerian polytechnics—an unlicensed and globally unrecognised cadre.

Following interventions by the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria, PCN, and the National Board for Technical Education, NBTE, a Memorandum of Understanding was signed on April 17, 2025, formally ending the programme and recognising pharmacy technicians as the only acceptable technical cadre, aligning with international best practices.

“This reform restores order to our professional structure. It ends years of confusion and protects the future of licensed pharmacy practice.”

In another milestone, the PSN secured a landmark judgment affirming the powers of the PCN to regulate and control the sale, dispensing, and custody of veterinary drugs across the country.

“This victory is not just for pharmacists but for all Nigerians,” Ayuba said. “It reinforces the legal and professional boundaries that safeguard the health sector from unregulated practices.”

The PSN has also made significant strides in improving the welfare of public sector pharmacists, working closely with the Joint Health Sector Unions, JOHESU, and the Assembly of Healthcare Professionals Association, AHPA.

Achievements include recognition of pharmacists as hospital-based consultants, payment of 25–35 percent CONHESS salary arrears, creation of IPPIS payment elements for Pharm.D holders, and an increase in call-duty allowance for Pharm.D pharmacists to 4 percent of basic salary.

Perhaps the most symbolic breakthrough was the extension of the retirement age for pharmacists to 65 years, and 70 years for consultant pharmacists, aligning them with their medical counterparts.

“This was a tough battle that raged for over 12 hours across four meetings,” Ayuba recalled. “But we prevailed—and that recognition now stands as a testament to the unity and perseverance of our profession.”

As the PSN ushers in a new era, Ayuba called for continuous learning, innovation, and collaboration among pharmacists, policymakers, and educators.

He reiterated the Society’s plan to push for legislative action to establish a National Postgraduate College of Pharmacy, designed as a Nigerian-oriented institution to complement the West African Postgraduate College of Pharmacists.

“We must seize this opportunity to define our future,” he urged. “The new pharmacy workforce must be equipped not just for practice, but for leadership, research, and policy influence in the health sector.”

Ayuba also encouraged delegates to take full advantage of the five-day conference, which features scientific sessions, lectures, and special meetings.

“Beyond the scientific sessions, please attend meetings that will add value. Let this conference pass through you as you enjoy DABO 2025.”

 *During the recent PSN National Conference held in Kano State* , a disturbing trend was observed where non-pharmacists gained unauthorized access to the exhibition halls, purchasing various drugs even before official directives were issued by the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN).

📌Potential misuse or resale of drugs without proper oversight.

📌Price distortion and unethical competition within the market.

‎[17/11/2025, 10:24:13] ~ Lancelot: *🔥 The Dynamic Duo for Hair Regrowth:*

*Minoxidil + Finasteride Topical Spray (FDA-Recommended for Male Baldness)*

*1. What Is This Spray? (Simple Explanation)*

It’s a *two-in-one hair regrowth treatment* combining:

*Minoxidil*
— First FDA-approved for hair loss.
— Approved 1988 for men, 1992 for women.
— Safe for both men and women.

 *Finasteride*
— FDA-approved 1997 for hair loss.
— Approved ONLY for men (not approved for women due to hormonal effects).

*Minoxidil* – boosts blood flow to the hair roots.

*Finasteride (Topical)* – blocks the hormone that shrinks hair follicles.

Together, they *regrow hair faster and stronger* than Minoxidil alone.

*2. How Each Ingredient Works (Easy to Understand)*

*🔹 MINOXIDIL — “The Hair Booster”*

Expands blood vessels around the scalp.

Improves oxygen and nutrient delivery to hair follicles.

Helps weak, dying hairs grow thicker and longer.

Time to see results:
👉 3–4 months (steady improvement after)

*🔹 FINASTERIDE (Topical) — “The Hair Protector”*

Blocks *DHT*, the hormone responsible for male pattern baldness.

Stops further hair loss and protects new hair from thinning.

*Time to see results:*
👉 3–6 months (strong protection after consistent use)

*3. Why This Combination Is Better Than Minoxidil Alone*

*✔ 2 Modes of Action Instead of 1*

Minoxidil grows hair.
Finasteride prevents hair loss.
Together = *maximum regrowth + protection*.

*✔ Stronger Results, Faster*

Studies show the combo works significantly better at:

Regrowing thinning hair

Thickening existing hair

Slowing down or stopping baldness


*✔ Less Systemic Side Effects*

Topical finasteride reduces hair loss without the systemic risks sometimes associated with oral finasteride.

*4. How to Use (Dosing Guide)*

Apply 1–2 sprays on the bald or thinning areas.

Use once daily (or as directed by your doctor).

Apply to a dry scalp for best absorption.

Wash hands after applying.

*5. How Long to Use It*

Hair regrowth requires consistency.

Use for at least 6 months for full benefits.

Continue long-term to maintain results.
Stopping will slowly reverse progress.

*6. What to Avoid During Treatment*

*❌ Do NOT apply on wet scalp*

It reduces absorption and effectiveness.

*❌ Do NOT wash your hair for 3–4 hours after application*

Water removes the medicine before it works.

*❌ Avoid applying on irritated or cut skin*

It may cause increased absorption.

*❌ Avoid combining with unknown hair creams*

Some products interfere with absorption.

*❌ Avoid skipping days*

Hair loss restarts when treatment becomes irregular

📌 *IMPORTANT* *HEALTH NOTE* *(FACT-BASED)*

🔹 *Vitamin D3 & Fibroids*:
Research from multiple reputable studies (including the National Institutes of Health – NIH) shows that *low Vitamin D levels are associated with a higher risk of uterine fibroids*, especially among Black women.
Vitamin D plays a role in regulating cell growth, which may explain this association.

🔹 *DIM* *(Diindolylmethane) & Fibroids:*
DIM may help *support estrogen metabolism,* which can be beneficial for women with estrogen-sensitive conditions.
*However*, _DIM is *not* recognized by WHO as a fibroid-prevention supplement._
Evidence is supportive but *not WHO-endorsed.*

*WHO-Recognized Supplements:*
Currently, the World Health Organization *(WHO does NOT endorse any specific supplement for preventing or shrinking fibroids.*
This is a medical fact.

‎[21/11/2025, 08:48:23] ~ Lancelot: *READ TO THE END*

*🌅 GOOD MORNING FROM LANCE PHARMA* 

_*“Information is the quiet power that lifts destinies—*_
_*for the mind that knows becomes the life that grows.”*_

At *LANCE PHARMA*, we rise each day with one mission:
to empower you with knowledge, precision, and life-saving access to the medications that matter.
Because in a world where many walk blindly, the informed stand victorious.*Here is a few health tips below for the informed*

*⚕️ HEALTH CORNER — Diabetes With Cardiac Risk: Smarter Choices Save Lives*

When managing *Diabetes*, especially in patients who also have *heart disease or high cardiovascular risk*, the choice of medications matters more than ever.

Here’s why
The key guideline you’re looking for is from the American Diabetes Association (ADA),*in their 2020 Standards of Care*, released in late 2019, they recommended considering *SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists* for type 2 diabetes patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) or cardiovascular disease (CVD) instead of or before *sulfonylureas.*

 *Dapagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor)* and *GLP-1 agonists like Semaglutide* are often recommended over *Sulphonylureas*:

*💊 1. CARDIOPROTECTIVE EFFECTS (Proven Heart Protection)*

*Dapagliflozin* reduces risk of heart failure hospitalization.

*Semaglutide* reduces major cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke).

*Sulphonylureas do NOT offer heart protection*, and in some cases may increase risk of hypoglycemia-induced cardiac strain.

*💊 2. WEIGHT BENEFITS — Crucial for Heart & Blood Sugar*

*Semaglutide* promotes significant weight loss.

*Dapagliflozin* causes mild weight reduction through glucose excretion.

*Sulphonylureas often cause weight gain*, worsening insulin resistance and increasing cardiac risk.

*💊 3. HYPOGLYCEMIA RISK*

*Dapagliflozin & Semaglutide*: Very low risk of low blood sugar.

*Sulphonylureas*: High risk of hypoglycemia → can trigger dangerous heart rhythm problems in cardiac patients.

*💊 4. KIDNEY PROTECTION*

*Dapagliflozin* provides strong renal protection, slowing progression of diabetic kidney disease.

*Sulphonylureas* do not have this benefit.

*💊 5. LONG-TERM OUTCOMES*

Modern guidelines consistently place *SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 agonists* above Sulphonylureas for diabetic patients with cardiovascular risks, due to superior overall outcomes.

*❤️ HEALTH TIP OF THE DAY*

✔️ Prioritize medications that protect your heart — not just control sugar.
✔️ Combine medication with:

30 minutes of daily walking

Low-salt diet

Reduced refined sugar

Adequate hydration
✔️ Regularly monitor your *blood pressure, blood sugar, and kidney function.* ‎image omitted

‎[26/11/2025, 15:43:49] ~ Lancelot: *LANCE CONSULT SPOTLIGHT:“The Wisdom of the Waistline against Body Mass Index (BMI): Understanding the Fire Before You Fight It”*

Not every type of body fat is the same — and Tirzepatide understands the difference with precision.

*1️⃣ The Fat Tirzepatide Burns First*

Tirzepatide activates two powerful natural hormones:

*Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 (GLP-1)*

*Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide (GIP)*

These hormones work together to:

Reduce appetite

Improve the way your body uses insulin

Trigger *fatty acid oxidation*, which means the body begins burning stored fat for energy

Because *visceral fat* (the fat around your internal organs) is more biologically active, it reacts *quickly and strongly*.
This is why most people notice:
*🔥 A faster reduction in waist size*
*🔥 A steady reduction in subcutaneous fat* under the skin

Tirzepatide targets the *dangerous fat first* — the fat that threatens health.

*2️⃣ When You Do Not Need Tirzepatide*

Before considering Tirzepatide, it is important to understand whether your body carries:
🟧 Excess body fat
or
🟩 Healthy lean muscle

Use this global health standard:

*✔ World Health Organization (WHO) Waist-to-Height Ratio*

*Healthy*: Less than 0.50

*Borderline risk*: Between 0.50 and 0.55

*High health risk*: Greater than 0.55


_*This method detects hidden visceral fat better than weight or Body Mass Index.*_

*✔ Simple Muscle and Fat Check (Pinch Test)*

A large pinch of belly fat → *stored fat is dominant*

A small pinch with a round, firm stomach → *visceral fat is dominant*

A small pinch with a flat, firm abdomen → *lean muscle is dominant* → Tirzepatide is *not required*

You also do not need Tirzepatide if:

Your *waist-to-height ratio* is within the healthy range

You already have strong, healthy lean muscle mass

You are losing weight because of stress, dehydration, or poor nutrition (not true fat loss)

*3️⃣ Why This Wisdom Matters*

Tirzepatide is designed for metabolic protection, not cosmetic appearance.
It is most effective when the real enemy is visceral fat — the fat responsible for:

High blood pressure

Type 2 Diabetes

Elevated cholesterol

Heart strain

Joint inflammation and pain

*Visceral fat is the flame closest to the heart.*
*Tirzepatide is the steady fire that cools it down.*

*🌟 FINAL REFLECTION*

*“Know the truth of your body before you choose your flame.*
*Muscle builds your tomorrow.*
*Fat steals your strength.*
*Wisdom is choosing what deserves to burn.”*

If dangerous fat is threatening your future, Tirzepatide becomes your ally. ‎image omitted

This time, the discovery cut deeper. Cartons of 225 mg of Tramadol, Diazepam and cough syrup from a major pharmaceutical company(sorry, I won't mention). Drugs that are supposed to be tightly controlled, ending up in the hands of men who come to fight us fully intoxicated.

No wonder when you fire at them expecting a flood of blood, sometimes only a few drops appear. These drugs make them reckless, aggressive, and terrifyingly resilient.

Investigations began immediately. How do these substances go from regulated production lines to cartons in terrorist hands? Who is turning a blind eye?
Who is not doing his job?

This war is fought on many fronts. Money, logistics, weapons, and now drugs - a silent pillar no one wants to talk about. Until every hand feeding this war is exposed, until we confront this hidden force, the fight will never truly end.

On the front line, we face bullets, but out there, there are players quietly keeping the fire alive, and this pharmaceutical industries are playing the striker.

Those ones on the floor?

Don't worry, they are sleeping.

~ Kolawole Oludare Stephen

His wife understood the principle of building with a man. And I told him confidently that those same female colleagues he’s pitying today would not have looked at him twice if they were in his wife’s shoes five years ago.

He asked, “How?”

He replied, “USD 3,500.”

“And how many are they?”
He said, “Eight.”

Then I explained:
Give a USD 3,500 monthly job to eight men, and come back two years later — many, if not all, will be married.
Give that same opportunity to eight women, and the chances that they will still be single are very high.

He became curious and wanted to know why. So I broke it down:

A man earning USD 3,500 doesn’t mind marrying a woman earning USD 200 per month or even someone not working. His pool of potential partners is in the thousands.

On the other hand, a woman earning USD 3,500 usually doesn’t want to date a man earning less. And even if she does, she often won’t be fully happy with that decision.

Now think about it:
A man with a wide pool of 5,000 options still has the responsibility of approaching, proposing, convincing, and planning.
Meanwhile, a woman who wants a man earning more than she does must sit, hope, and wait for the right man to approach her — and even then, she’s still scanning for someone “better.”

So the real question is this:
How many men earning more than USD 3,500 are ready and willing to marry your colleagues?

Then I asked him,
“By the way, how many of your male colleagues are single?”

He said, “None.”

I told him, “You have your answer.”

The discussion ended there.

 " the creation of the post of consultant Pharmacist has generated professional crises in the hospital which has the potential to bring down the entire organisational structure that's as old as Hippocrates the father of medicine, in the treatment of patients with attendant catastrophic mortality and morbidity. We warm!!"
Now looking closely at  this statement, one will  notice no crises has emerged from the creation of the cadre. The crises they most likely are talking about are the ones generated in the meeting of medical doctors where they may argue, wail,cry and shout about a Cadre established by the FG to improve healthcare.

They wrote that professional growth of others "cross" their own growth. How?
Let me elucidate.
The medical doctor consultants became fellow of their own colleges and got appointments as consultants in the hospital to the Federal government. The hospital and FG pays for the consultation on matters concerning their  profession.
Another professional with a different college and different profession is also employed by the government that has now decided to hire them as consultant professionals on matters concerning their own profession.
The medical doctors are not pharmacists and they don't  do the job of a pharmacist.
The medical doctors are consulted for their medical expertise while the pharmacist is consulted for pharmaceutical expertise .
There is nothing like crossing here. 
The only crossing we can see here is one professional trying to cross the path of progress of other professionals probably due to ego or  ignorance or crass wickedness.
The petition came from Medical and Dental doctors in the Academia and these are people who have spent many years in the Academia and we are supposed to get knowledge and new teachings from them. It is not expected of them to try to redefine the term "Consultant".
It's never too late to learn and we should correct our brothers by telling them that consultant is "one who provides expert advice professionally in a specific area of knowledge".
There are consultants in medicine, pharmacy, nursing etc. and these are verifiable facts in countries like UK, America and Australia which we  can't ignore if we are talking about international best practices. 
For the avoidance of doubt, there is an American society of Consultant Pharmacists. Such bodies also exist in UK and Australia.
The personal attacks on  high ranking government officials as the OHSCF and Perm Secretary FMOH leave much to be desired.
These are offices well equipped and well versed in matters of establishment, cadres and schemes of service.

These offices did huge work slowly at different stages leading up the superior cadres for nurses and Pharmacists.
The issue of back door should be properly investigated especially as it's a huge insult on the  offices mentioned.

When did NAMDA start saving money for FG?
"The position of Consultant Pharmacist adds no iota of clinical value to the care of the patient".
This statement is one big reason for the downfall of healthcare in Nigeria and a huge need for overhaul of the leadership of healthcare in Nigeria. A medical academic, doesn't know , doesn't know that he doesn't know and doesn't care to find out the role of a consultant Pharmacist and the advantages on healthcare.
We have evidences of better patient outcomes when there is input from a consultant Pharmacist, everywhere but more in America and UK where the statistics from research have driven such countries into investing in Pharmaceutical care and Pharmacy consultancy.

‎[11/12/2025, 14:02:06] ~ Lancelot: *"The Tyranny of Time: The Medical Destiny of William Howard Taft, Untouched by the Grace of the GLP-1 Era.*

While there has never been a sitting *U.S. President* whose official cause of death was explicitly listed as "obesity-related complications," historians and medical experts often point to the case of *President William Howard Taft (1909–1913)*.

Taft was the heaviest President, reaching a weight over *300 pounds* (and possibly up to 340 lbs during his term). He suffered from severe medical issues highly associated with obesity, including sleep apnea, hypertension, and heart strain. He died in 1930 from heart disease, the symptoms of which were certainly aggravated by his extreme weight.

*✅⚕️ Semaglutide, Tirzepatide, and the Case of Taft*

The premise of Semaglutide potentially saving a historical figure like Taft is a powerful thought experiment that highlights the revolution in modern obesity medicine.

*✅1. The Challenge: What Taft Faced*

In the early 20th century, the treatments available for severe obesity were limited to calorie restriction, exercise, and sometimes dangerous surgical procedures. There were no effective pharmacological tools to manage the underlying hormones driving appetite and metabolism.

*✅2. The Solution: Incretins (Semaglutide)*

Semaglutide is a medication that belongs to a class known as *incretin mimetics*, specifically a *GLP-1 Receptor Agonist*.

* *What is an Incretin?*
    Incretins are hormones (like GLP-1 and GIP) naturally released by the gut after eating. They send signals to the pancreas to release insulin, slow gastric emptying (making you feel full longer), and tell the brain to reduce appetite.
* *Semaglutide's Action:* As a GLP-1 agonist, Semaglutide mimics the action of the natural GLP-1 hormone, but lasts much longer in the body. This dual action on the gut and brain leads to significant:
    *Weight Loss:* By reducing appetite and calorie intake.
    *Metabolic Improvement:* By lowering blood sugar (HbA1c) and improving insulin sensitivity. 

*✅3. Semaglutide as the "First Runner-Up"*

The context that names Semaglutide (a GLP-1 agonist) as the *"1st Runner-Up"* is based on the superior efficacy data of the newer drug:

* *Tirzepatide (The Champion):* This drug is a *dual agonist*, targeting both the *GLP-1* receptor and the *GIP* (Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide) receptor. By hitting two pathways, it generally achieves *higher rates of total weight loss* and slightly better HbA1c reduction, leading to its "Champion" status in overall efficacy.
* *Semaglutide (The Runner-Up):* While slightly less potent for weight loss than Tirzepatide, Semaglutide still delivers strong results and currently holds the *strongest evidence for cardiovascular benefits* (hence its high ranking in safety and cardiometabolic categories).

*✅4. Could It Have Saved Taft?*

Given the modern understanding of obesity as a chronic, hormonal disease, it is highly probable that a drug like Semaglutide could have **dramatically improved President Taft's quality of life and potentially extended it**.

* By achieving sustained weight loss, the strain on his heart and cardiovascular system would have been significantly reduced.
* The resulting decrease in hypertension and better management of blood sugar would have directly addressed the core metabolic issues that contribute to fatal complications like heart failure and stroke.

The challenge facing Taft was that the necessary hormonal tool simply did not exist in 1913. ‎image omitted

Incretins *outperform older drugs* in glucose control without hypoglycemia

Sulphonylureas are being *phased down*, not favored

[29/12/2025, 06:24:29] Sir Hope Onyemaechi: I have a friend named Segun. For three years, Segun was the "ghost" of our group. ​Every time we planned a hangout; a birthday dinner, a football match, or just drinks on a Friday night, Segun would be the first to say "I'll try to come" in the group chat.

But he never did.

He’d stop replying to messages by 6:00 PM and wouldn’t surface until the next morning with a "Sorry guys, I fell asleep" or "Something came up."

​Eventually, we stopped inviting him. We started calling him "unreliable." We even had a separate group chat without him because we felt he didn't value our friendship anymore.

"Success has entered his head," one of us said. "He’s too big for us now."

​Last year, my life hit a brick wall. ​I lost my job in the same month my mom needed surgery. I was drowning.

I called the active friends; the ones I went clubbing with every weekend. They were sympathetic, sure.

"Oh, so sorry bro," "God will provide," "I’m a bit tight this month, but let me see what I can do."

​Then they stopped picking up my calls. I guess I became too heavy for the fun group.

​One Tuesday night, around 11:00 PM, my doorbell rang. ​I opened it, and there was Segun. He wasn't wearing a designer shirt or looking big.

He looked tired. He was holding a nylon bag with some groceries and a small envelope.

​"I heard what happened," he said, walking in.

​I was defensive. "Oh, now you show up? You haven't picked my calls in months, Segun. You missed my housewarming, you missed my birthday..."

​He sat down on my sofa and sighed.
​"I know. And I’m sorry. But I wasn't at those parties because I’ve been working three shifts. My younger brother is in the university, my sister is doing her nursing program, and my dad’s pension hasn't been paid in two years. I am the only one, man."

​I went quiet.

​"I don't reply to the group chat at 7:00 PM because that’s when I start my night job as a delivery driver. I don't come for drinks because the money for one bottle of beer is my sister’s transport fare for a whole week. I didn't want to come and be the 'vibe killer' by telling you guys how much I’m struggling. So I stayed away."

​He placed the envelope on the table.

​"It’s not much. Just something to help with your mom’s meds. I’ve been saving it to fix my car’s brakes, but the car can wait. You’re my brother."

​I looked at the envelope, then at the man I had spent months bad-mouthing. The friends who "showed up" for the fun were nowhere to be found when the lights went out.

But the friend who was "too busy" was the only one who showed up at midnight.

See, we often measure friendship by presence at parties, but the truest friendships are measured by presence in those difficult times.

You shouldn't be too quick to judge the friend who has gone silent.

Sometimes, they are using all their energy just to keep their own head above water... and yet, they’d still dive in to save you if they saw you drowning.

​Real friendship isn't about who you see the most; it’s about who shows up when everyone else has an excuse.

‎[06/01/2026, 13:47:55] ~ Lancelot: *LANCE PHARMA SPOTLIGHT TODAY:* WHAT THE PLATES DEMANDS,THE PANCREAS PAYS THE PRICE......*

*🍫🍚🍝 THE SUGAR STORY WE DON’T SEE*

_How Everyday Nigerian Foods Quietly Stress the Pancreatic Beta Cells—and Where Modern Medicine Steps In_

When people hear “sugar causes obesity”, they often imagine table sugar or chocolate bars.
In reality, the greatest sugar burden in Nigeria does not come from sweets—it comes from how our staple foods turn into sugar inside the body.

To understand obesity, diabetes, and why Tirzepatide and Semaglutide exist, we must first understand beta-cell stress.
*🧠 THE BETA PANCREATIC CELLS: THE SILENT WORKERS*

Your pancreatic beta cells produce insulin—the hormone that moves sugar (glucose) from the blood into cells.

Small sugar rise meaning gentle insulin release while beta cells relax

Large, frequent sugar spikes result into  heavy insulin release and  beta cells get stressed

Obesity is not just “eating too much.”
It is repeated metabolic stress.

*🎨 THE COLOUR GLYCEMIC SCALE (EASY GUIDE)*

*🟢 GREEN (Low Stress)*
Slow sugar release, beta cells stay calm

*🟡 YELLOW (Moderate Stress)*
Noticeable insulin demand

*🔴 RED (High Stress)*
Rapid sugar spikes results to  beta-cell exhaustion and  fat storage

*🍫 1. AVERAGE CHOCOLATE BAR (50g)*

*Calories*: ~230–250 kcal

*Sugar*: ~25–27g (≈ 6–7 teaspoons)

*Glycemic Load*: 🟡 Yellow–🔴 Red

*Beta-cell stress: Short but sharp spike*

*📌 Truth*:
Chocolate causes a *quick insulin spike*, but it ends quickly.
It is *not eaten in kilograms*, so damage comes mainly from frequency, not volume.

*✅ Safe daily limit*:

*½ bar (25g)* occasionally

Prefer dark chocolate (≥70%)

*🥧 2. MEAT PIE (Nigerian bakery standard)*

*Calories*: 400–450 kcal

Refined flour + fat combo

*Hidden sugar equivalent*: ~8–10 teaspoons

*Glycemic stress*: 🔴 Red
*📌 Why dangerous:*
Refined flour + fat = prolonged insulin demand
This stresses beta cells longer than chocolate.

*✅ Safe limit:*

*½ meat pie per day*, not daily

Best as occasional food

*🍚 3. WHITE RICE (2 Nigerian serving spoons ≈ 300g cooked)*

*Calories*: ~390 kcal

*Sugar equivalent*: ~12–14 teaspoons

*Glycemic Index:* 🔴 Red

*📌 Critical truth:*
Rice is *not sweet*, but it turns into glucose *faster than sugar.*

📌 Nigeria vs global standard:

Japan: small bowls + fish + vegetables

Nigeria: large plates + stew + swallow → *double insulin stress*

*✅ Safe daily limit:*

*150–180g cooked (1 serving spoon)*

Combine with vegetables + protein

*🍝 4. SPAGHETTI / PASTA (White)*

*Calories*: ~350 kcal per large serving

*Glycemic Index*: 
🟡 Yellow  and
🔴 Red (overcooked)

📌 *Better than rice*, but *portion size* ruins it.

*✅ Safe limit:*

*120–150g cooked*

Never alone—add protein

*🍜 5. INDOMIE (1 pack)*

*Calories*: ~350 kcal

Refined carbs + oils

*Glycemic stress*: 🔴 Red

*📌 Problem:*
Liquid fats + refined starch = insulin overload

*✅ Safe limit:*

*½ pack*, not daily

Add eggs/vegetables to reduce spike

*🥛 6. DRINKING GARRI (1 large cup)*

*Calories*: ~300–400 kcal

*Fast glucose absorption*

*Glycemic stress*: 🔴🔴 Deep Red

*📌 Reality:*
Drinking garri bypasses chewing → instant sugar rush
This is one of the highest beta-cell stress foods in Nigeria.

*✅ Safe limit:*

½ small cup, occasionally

Never as daily habit

*🍲 7. FUFU / EBA / POUNDO (1 wrap ≈ 250–300g)*

*Calories*: ~400–500 kcal

*Glycemic Index*: 🔴 Red

📌 Key insight:
Swallow is not evil—but *portion size* is.

*📌 Golden standard comparison:*

Mediterranean cultures: small starch + large vegetables

Nigeria: large swallow + oily soup = insulin overload

*✅ Safe limit:*

*150–180g (small wrap)*

Soup must be vegetable-rich, not oil-heavy

*WHERE THE WORLD STEPS IN:*

*TIRZEPATIDE & SEMAGLUTIDE*

Modern medicine recognized a global truth:

> “The problem is not willpower.It is biology under constant insulin assault.”
🔹 Semaglutide (GLP-1)

Slows stomach emptying

Reduces appetite

Lowers sugar spikes

*Protects beta cells*


*🔹 Tirzepatide (GLP-1 + GIP) 🏆*

Stronger appetite control

Better insulin sensitivity

Greater fat loss

*Gold-standard metabolic reset*


📌 These drugs *do not replace discipline*
They *restore biological balance* after years of metabolic stress. ‎video omitted

[09/01/2026, 15:21:46] ~ ospx: Nestlé has recalled these baby products. 

So before you mix that next bottle for your baby, read this thread carefully as it concerns their well being. 

If you feed your baby NAN, SMA, or Alfamino, a toxic bacteria has been found in some batches. And you might have it in your house right now.

You see, Nestlé has issued a massive global recall for several baby formulas (products in the image) because they found a toxin called Cereulide (from Bacillus cereus bacteria) in some batches.

This toxin causes severe nausea and vomiting in babies. And the scary part is that boiling water does NOT kill it. The toxin is heat-resistant. So even if you prepare the formula correctly, if the powder itself is contaminated, your baby is at risk.

Now, NAFDAC has not released a specific alert for Nigeria yet. BUT our markets are porous. And people import ‘UK SMA’ and ‘Foreign NAN’ every single day. So if you buy your formula from supermarkets that stock imported goods, or you bought it abroad, you need to check the last stock to see if your tin look like any of those products.

If yes, go to Nestlé’s website (nestle.co.uk/en-gb/media/sm…) to check if your specific batch is affected.

If your batch code matches the ones on that list, please DO NOT USE IT.

And please, don't keep this information to yourself.

If you have a friend, sister, or neighbor who uses SMA, NAN, or Alfamino, retweet this or send this to them NOW.

You might be saving a baby from poisoning today.

He was to travel to the US the next day, January 7th, accompanied by Travelling Doctors. A team at Johns Hopkins was waiting to receive him in Baltimore. The Hopkins team had asked for a lumbar puncture test and an MRI. The Nigerian team had also decided to put in a 'central line' (used to administer iv medications)  in preparation for Nkanu's flight. Atlantis hospital referred us to Euracare Hospital, which was said to be the best place to have the procedures done.

The morning of the 6th, we left Atlantis hospital for Euracare, Nkanu carried in his father's arms. We were told he would need to be sedated to prevent him from moving during the MRI and the 'central line' procedure.

I was waiting just outside the theater. I saw people, including Dr M, rushing into the theater and immediately knew something had happened.

Some hours later, Nkanu was gone

It turns out that Nkanu was NEVER monitored after being given too much propofol. The anesthesiologist had just casually carried Nkanu on his shoulder to the theater, so nobody knows when exactly Nkanu became unresponsive.

[13/01/2026, 19:14:51] King Penet: Community pharmacies are recognised health facilities — ACPN 
Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria

By Chioma Obinna

The Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria, ACPN, has reaffirmed that community pharmacies are legally recognised health facilities in Nigeria, following a recent public debate on the scope of services provided within pharmacy practice.

In a press statement jointly signed by its National Chairman, Ambrose Ezeh and National Secretary,
Omokhafe Ashore leadership, the ACPN responded to comments credited to the President of the National Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria, AMLSN, Dr. Casmir Ifeanyi, which raised concerns about diagnostic activities within pharmacy premises.

The ACPN described the comments as a misunderstanding of existing health policies and regulatory frameworks guiding pharmacy practice in Nigeria.

According to the association, community pharmacies operate within clearly defined legal and professional boundaries and remain subject to oversight by relevant regulatory authorities.

The pharmacists’ body noted that point-of-care testing, particularly the use of Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) kits for conditions such as malaria, is encouraged by the Federal Ministry of Health as part of national disease control strategies.

The association explained that confirming malaria infection before dispensing antimalarial medicines aligns with the National Malaria Policy and helps to prevent drug misuse and resistance.

“Community pharmacies play a critical role in safeguarding patients by ensuring rational drug use, especially for common conditions that account for a large proportion of outpatient visits,” the statement said.

The ACPN further clarified that Nigerian law allows healthcare providers, including pharmacies, hospitals, and other stakeholders, to operate laboratory services where such facilities are duly registered and licensed by the appropriate regulatory bodies. It stressed, however, that community pharmacies without registered laboratory units are expected to comply strictly with existing laws and professional guidelines.

Citing the National Health Act of 2014, the association emphasized that pharmacies are officially recognised as health facilities and form an integral part of Nigeria’s healthcare delivery system.

_Related News_
_Nestlé infant formula in Nigeria safe, not part of UK recall — NAFDAC_

On the structure of modern pharmacy practice, the ACPN explained that the integration of limited retail or supermarket sections within some pharmacy outlets is an internationally accepted model designed to improve patient convenience and support holistic health outcomes. It noted that similar models exist in the United Kingdom, the United States, and other advanced health systems, where pharmacies combine professional services with access to health-related consumer goods.

The association also highlighted the historical contribution of pharmacy practice to healthcare innovation, pointing out that several widely used health and nutrition products originated from pharmacists’ work in community settings.

Reaffirming its commitment to collaboration, the ACPN described medical laboratory scientists as long-standing partners in healthcare delivery and expressed confidence that inter-professional cooperation remains essential for strengthening Nigeria’s health system.

Nigeria, PSN, and statutory regulatory councils to uphold good pharmacy practice, protect patient safety, and ensure compliance with national health laws and standards.

‎[14/01/2026, 19:04:53] King Penet: *ACPN Warns Against Misleading Portrayals Of Pharmacies In Nigeria* 

written by Chioma Umeha January 14, 2026


 *Pharmacy in Nigeria* 
 *… Calls For Respect Of* *Healthcare Boundaries* 

LAGOS – Pharmacists under the ACPN have pushed back against claims that community pharmacies double as “provision shops” or engage in unlawful medical laboratory practices, stressing that such portrayals are inaccurate and risk eroding trust in Nigeria’s healthcare system.

In a statement signed by its National Chairman, Ambrose Ezeh, and National Secretary, Omokhafe Ashore, the ACPN responded to a press statement credited to the leadership of the Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria (AMLSN).

The Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN) said it was concerned by the comments, noting that medical laboratory scientists have traditionally worked closely with pharmacists within Nigeria’s health sector.

The ACPN stated that where issues of professional boundaries or jurisdiction arise, they should be addressed through constructive dialogue rather than public statements capable of creating misunderstanding among healthcare professionals and the public.

 Addressing the allegation that pharmacies conduct medical tests illegally, the ACPN explained that registered pharmacy facilities are permitted to carry out approved point-of-care testing. It noted that the Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH) encourages the use of Rapid Diagnostic Test kits in pharmacies to confirm malaria infection before the dispensing of antimalarial medicines, in line with the National Malaria Policy.

According to the association, this approach helps to prevent the indiscriminate use of medicines, reduce the risk of drug resistance and protect the effectiveness of Artemisinin-based Combination Therapies, which remain the recommended treatment for malaria. The ACPN added that malaria accounts for a significant proportion of clinical visits in Nigeria, making such safeguards essential to public health.

The association further clarified that Nigerian law does not prohibit the registration of laboratory facilities within pharmacies, hospitals or as stand-alone medical laboratories, provided all regulatory requirements are met. It said some pharmacies have lawfully registered laboratories within their premises, while emphasising that pharmacies without such registration are not encouraged to engage in laboratory practice.

 Reacting to comments suggesting that pharmacies in Nigeria operate as provision stores, the ACPN explained that pharmacies are registered under various categories, including retail, wholesale, distribution, manufacturing, importing and scientific offices. While some retail pharmacies may include supermarket sections, the association said this does not diminish their status as healthcare facilities.

The ACPN noted that internationally, integrated pharmacy and supermarket models are common, citing examples from the United Kingdom and the United States, where major pharmacy chains operate alongside retail outlets and, in some cases, laboratory services. According to the association, such models are designed to improve access, convenience and holistic healthcare delivery.

The statement partly reads, “We make bold to say that in the United Kingdom, multiple chain outlets like Tesco, Asda,Sainsbury, and Boots all have formidable supermarket structures. In the United States, the likes of Walgreens, Walmart, CVS, etc all have fantastic supermarkets and Laboratories in their pharmacy set-up. These are standards that have been put in place to assist patients to enjoy a one-stop approach in their procurements for convenience. “Strategically, however, effective drug therapy management is complemented by balancing professional output with good nutritional values. A well-stocked pharmacy will therefore assist clients fuss patients to have a good spread of healthy foods with their drugs for optimal therapeutic outcomes.”

 The pharmacists also expressed concern over statements that could be interpreted as dismissive of certain professionals working in laboratory settings, warning that such remarks could strain professional relationships within the health sector.

The ACPN stressed that it values collaboration among healthcare professionals and does not believe the comments attributed to the AMLSN leadership reflect the views of all medical laboratory scientists. It reaffirmed its commitment, as an affiliate of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN), to working with all stakeholders to strengthen healthcare delivery in the country.

ACPN stressed that the views do not represent the interests of a wide generality of Medical Laboratory Scientists who are progressive partners of the pharmacists and its umbrella templates across board in the reformation of health services for the good of the common man in Nigeria.

Still condemning the views, he described it as ‘poor and undue,’ alleging that the write-up gives insights into writer’s “rejection even in his immediate domain of Medical Laboratory Science, as he obviously lacks facts, skills and talents to move that dynamic profession forward.”

 The association concluded by assuring Nigerians that community pharmacies remain recognised health facilities under the National Health Act 2014 and that relevant regulatory bodies will continue to ensure good pharmacy and healthcare practice.

 “Finally, we assure consumers of health that the ACPN and the requisite government professional regulatory councils involved in pharmacy practice will continue to ensure Good Pharmacy Practice within the ambit of registered Pharmacies in Nigeria,” it added. ‎image omitted

[16/01/2026, 14:23:18] King Penet: *The Chimamanda’s Case and The Sealed Lips of Pharmacists*

_“There is a time to speak and a time to be quiet_ ” – Ecclesiastes 3:7

The major news item in Nigeria in the past few days has been the death of Nkanu Nnamdi, the 21-month-old son of Nigeria’s famous writer, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie. Comments have been pouring in from medical experts (e.g., public health physicians and anaesthetists) and their umbrella body, the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), lawyers, and the lay public. Sadly, it seems to me that pharmacists (the professionals in whom all-round knowledge of drugs resides), have not been quiet. My apology if there has been a release without my knowledge.

The death is alleged to be due to an overdose of propofol, an intravenous general anaesthetic and sedative drug. No drug issue should be discussed without the participation of pharmacists. *If uninvited to comment, PSN, AHAPN and CPAN should push to comment.* In my view, the comment should focus on pharmaceutical care, the quality of the medicine and the positive difference pharmacists could make to clinical outcomes. We should indicate our availability to participate in any investigation. Matter-of-fact, it would be inappropriate to set up an investigative committee without a pharmacist.

In the meantime, I would expect pharmacists to dust up their pharmacology and remind themselves of the mechanisms of action, adverse effects, and possible degradation products of propofol, just so that something can be said when anyone asks. 

Being taciturn when the profession should be heard will not bring the desired recognition and its benefits. This again, is our chance!

*Ray I. Ozolua*
_Pharmacist/Pharmacologist/Toxicologist_
*University of Benin*

‎[24/01/2026, 07:07:54] Izibeya T Dr.SIT—Silver Ypgd: *Chimamanda’s Son Inquest:Lawal Urges Multidisciplinary Panel, Says Investigating Drugs Without Experts ‘Dangerous’*

By Adebola Lawal
 
A consultant clinical pharmacist, Pharmacist Adebola Lawal, has issued a strongly worded petition to the Lagos State Government, warning that the ongoing inquest into the tragic death of Chimamanda’s son risks being fatally compromised if pharmacists and nurses are excluded from the panel.  

Lawal, CEO of Hugeworth Pharmacy, a fast-growing integrative community pharmacy, declared that conscience and professional responsibility compelled him to speak out. He praised the government’s decision to institute an inquest as commendable and reflective of its commitment to justice and accountability. However, he cautioned that the credibility, depth, and usefulness of the panel’s findings would be fundamentally undermined if it remained dominated by a single professional group.  

“Healthcare delivery is a multidisciplinary system, not a doctor-only enterprise,” Lawal stated. “Any inquiry that limits itself to one professional group, especially in a case where drug therapy, medication use, administration, monitoring, and clinical decision-making are central issues, risks becoming superficial, biased, and ultimately ineffective.”  

*Pharmacists Must Be Included*

Lawal stressed that pharmacists are the only professionals trained and licensed as end-to-end experts on medicines. Their expertise spans drug manufacturing and quality assurance, storage and distribution, prescribing appropriateness, dosing and interactions, administration safety, adverse drug reaction monitoring, pharmacovigilance, and medication error analysis.  

He argued that any investigation involving possible medication-related harm cannot be complete without pharmacists. “To exclude them is to investigate drugs without drug experts,” he warned. “Such an exercise would amount to little more than a procedural formality, producing conclusions that may lack scientific rigour and clinical truth.”  

Lawal further noted that panels dominated by one professional group investigating its own members create room, intended or not, for defensive conclusions, professional solidarity, and historical patterns of blame-shifting. He said Nigeria’s healthcare system has suffered greatly from this culture, and the public is watching closely.  

*Nurses’ Perspective Is Indispensable*

The pharmacist also insisted that nurses must be included in the panel. He described nurses as the primary executors of bedside care, central to drug administration, patient monitoring, early detection of deterioration, escalation of care, and documentation of clinical events.  

“Their perspective is indispensable in reconstructing timelines, understanding real-time clinical decisions, and identifying systemic failures that doctors alone may neither see nor admit,” Lawal said.  

*A Call For Transparency And Public Trust*

Lawal emphasised that the inquest is not merely about one tragic death but a test of institutional integrity. He urged Lagos State to demonstrate that justice is not selective, cosmetic, or professional-group-centric.  

He warned that an investigation excluding pharmacists and nurses would struggle to earn public confidence, and its recommendations, no matter how well written, may be dismissed as incomplete or compromised.  

“Justice must not only be done; it must be seen to be done, thoroughly, independently, and competently,” Lawal declared. “Anything short of this risks reducing the entire exercise to a symbolic ritual with no meaningful outcome for the bereaved family or the Nigerian healthcare system.”  

*Nigeria’s Healthcare Crisis: Why Pharmacists Can No Longer Be Ignored*

In a broader critique of Nigeria’s healthcare system, Lawal warned that the country cannot make meaningful progress while systematically sidelining pharmacists. He argued that diagnosis alone does not save lives; medication use does. When medication counselling, interaction checks, and handling are wrong, the entire effort of diagnosis becomes meaningless.  

He highlighted Nigeria’s acute shortage of pharmacists, a crisis he said is being dangerously ignored by the leadership of the health sector. He accused the current Minister of Health of being unwilling to confront the issue, constrained by professional bias and self-interest as a physician rather than guided by evidence-based health systems thinking.  

Lawal cited real-world examples to underscore the dangers. In one case, a cardiologist co-prescribed clopidogrel with omeprazole. Both drugs are metabolised via the CYP2C19 enzyme pathway, but omeprazole inhibits the enzyme, significantly reducing the activation and effectiveness of clopidogrel. This interaction is well-documented and clinically significant. Had the prescription gone unchecked, the patient, already with a history of myocardial infarction, would have faced a high risk of another heart attack or sudden death. The fatal outcome was prevented only because a pharmacist intervened.  
In another troubling incident, an insulin-dependent diabetic patient was handed insulin by an endocrinologist without meaningful counselling. The patient, acting in good faith, repeatedly refrigerated, and at times even froze, the insulin after opening it. This denatured the protein structure, rendering it ineffective. The patient’s blood glucose remained uncontrolled, and no one initially understood why. The missing link was pharmaceutical care. Insulin, once opened, must be stored at room temperature, not frozen. This basic drug-handling knowledge falls squarely within the expertise of pharmacists.  

“These are not isolated incidents,” Lawal said. “They are symptoms of a broken system, a system that wrongly assumes that prescribing alone equals care.”  
 
*A Call for Presidential Action*

Lawal urged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to act decisively. He called for the current Minister of Health to be relieved of office and for the appointment of a competent, neutral health systems expert, preferably a health economist, without professional bias. Such a leader, he argued, would be capable of designing a truly multidisciplinary, patient-centred healthcare framework.  

“Until pharmacists are fully integrated into clinical care, policy formulation, and health leadership, Nigeria will remain trapped in this avoidable quagmire, where preventable medication errors continue to cost innocent lives,” Lawal warned. ‎image omitted

At *LANCE PHARMA*, we believe the future of healthcare logistics is not just fast — it is *intelligent, traceable, and predictive*. That’s why we are proudly building the *Bi-LANCE PRO App*, a next-generation system designed to transform how medications are tracked, managed, and delivered.

🔍 *Batch-Level Traceability Like Never Before*
We understand a common challenge: the _same medicine brand_ (like Panadol) can come in *different batches with different expiry dates*, yet many systems record only one expiry.

Bi-LANCE PRO captures every batch separately and links each one directly to:
✔ Supplier
✔ Invoice
✔ Exact expiry date

No confusion. Full traceability.

⏳ *FEFO Over FIFO — Because Expiry Matters More*
Most systems use *FIFO (First In, First Out)*.
But in pharma, *expiry date is more important than arrival date.*

Our system uses *FEFO (First Expiry, First Out)* to ensure:
✔ Near-expiry products are sold first
✔ Waste is reduced
✔ Financial losses are minimized
✔ Patient safety is protected

🧾 *Smart Barcode Receipt Automation*
We are introducing a Barcode Receipt Generator System that connects suppliers and clients instantly.

How it works:
1️⃣ Supplier fills a digital supply form
2️⃣ System generates a *barcoded receipt* automatically
3️⃣ Client receives an *instant email alert with receipt proof*
4️⃣ Document serves as *tax audit evidence* and traceable purchase record

Transparent. Accountable. Automated.

*🤖 Automation, OCR & Predictive Stock Intelligence*
We are integrating:
🔹 Automation to monitor stock and alerts

🔹 Predictive models powered by your real sales data

Our system helps you know:
📦 What to restock

All delivered in *weekly or monthly automated reports.*

‎[03/02/2026, 23:18:19] ~ Lancelot: *LANCE PHARMA SPOTLIGHT : ONE BITE, LITTLE TIME: THE ABUJA MYSTERY THAT REMINDS US LIFE IS FRAGILE*

_*How a single cobra strike can turn minutes into a race against time*_

In Abuja, Nigeria’s capital, the nation was rocked by the tragic death of *Ifunanya Nwangene Dies After Snake Bite in Abuja (Vanguard), a 26-year-old singer and The Voice Nigeria alumna,* who was bitten by a *snake identified by bystanders as a cobra* inside her home in *Lugbe* on January 31, 2026. 

According to *Vanguard News*
Videos shared online showed snake handlers removing the reptile from her residence as neighbours cried out that *“It is a King cobra!”* — a species known for potent neurotoxic venom.

*SECTION 2: Why Cobra Bites Are Extremely Dangerous*

Cobras—especially King Cobras—carry neurotoxic venom.
🔬 What does that mean in simple terms?

🟠The venom *attacks the nervous system*

🟠It *blocks communication between nerves and muscles*

The muscles that control *breathing* are often affected first

⚠️ This is why many victims don’t die from pain—but from *respiratory failure.*

*⏳ SECTION 3: The Timeline — How Fast Can Things Go Wrong?*

This is the part everyone must understand:

*⏱️ After a venomous cobra bite:*
*Within 30 minutes – 2 hours:*
Symptoms may begin (drooping eyelids, weakness, difficulty speaking or breathing)

*Within a few hours (2–6 hours):*
Breathing muscles may become paralyzed

*Without urgent medical care:*
The situation can become fatal

*👉 There is no “safe waiting time.”*
👉 Survival depends heavily on *how fast antivenom and respiratory support are given.*

*🚑 SECTION 4: What MUST Be Done for Survival (Golden Rules)*

If a snakebite happens—especially from a suspected cobra— *do this immediately:*

*✅ 1. Stay as calm as possible*
Panic increases heart rate, which spreads venom faster.

*✅ 2. Keep the bitten limb still and low*
Movement accelerates venom circulation.

*✅ 3. Remove rings, bangles, shoes, or tight clothing*
Swelling can cause further damage.

*✅ 4. Go STRAIGHT to a hospital with antivenom*
Not a chemist.
Not a prayer house first.
Not “let’s wait and see.”

*🏥 Antivenom + medical monitoring = the only proven lifesaving treatment.*

*🚫 SECTION 5: The Big Myth — “Home Remedies”*

The following are *dangerous myths*:

❌Cutting the wound

❌Sucking out venom

❌Tying tight tourniquets

❌Applying herbs, oils, or pastes

❌Using ice, electric shock, or alcohol

🚫 These *do not neutralize venom*
🚫 Some make the injury worse
🚫 Many deaths happen because people tried these first

> Nature made the venom powerful. Only medicine can stop it.

Stay alert.
Stay informed.
*And please—share this responsibly. 🐍🚑* ‎image omitted

‎[05/02/2026, 13:49:43] ~ Lancelot: *LANCE PHARMA SPOTLIGHT:“The Horse That Outsmarted the Snake: Secrets Behind Antivenom Production”*

Good morning, colleagues! Let’s dive into one of the most fascinating stories in pharmacology and toxinology — how *the mighty equine horse helps save human lives from venomous snakes.*

You might wonder: *Why a horse? Why not a more “immune” animal? Or why not snakes themselves?*

Here’s the science:

*1️⃣ Horses Are Not Immune — They’re Smartly Trained*

Horses are *not naturally immune to snake venom*. A bite from a cobra or green mamba could kill them if untreated. But here’s the trick: scientists give horses *tiny, carefully measured, gradually increasing doses of venom* — far smaller than what a snake injects in a real bite.

A *cobra injects about 100–300 mg of venom per bite*, enough to be lethal to humans.

In horses, the *starting dose is only micrograms to milligrams*, far below lethal levels, and is slowly increased over weeks. This stimulates the horse’s immune system to produce *antibodies* without causing harm.

This is called  *hyper immunization*, and it’s *specific to large mammals* like equines because of their *robust immune systems and ability to produce large volumes of plasma safely*. Small animals like rabbits or dogs don’t produce enough antibodies for mass antivenom production.

*2️⃣ Why Not Snakes or Other Animals?*

Snakes are *venom producers, not immune responders*. Using snakes or highly venom-sensitive animals like rodents or cats would be dangerous and inefficient — the animal could die before producing usable antibodies. Horses strike the balance: *big, strong, and capable of surviving incremental venom exposure*.

*3️⃣ The Venom Types: Cobra vs Green Mamba*

*Cobra venom*: Primarily *neurotoxic*, affecting nerve transmission and causing paralysis.

*Green mamba venom*: Highly potent *neurotoxic and cardiotoxic*, faster acting and more deadly per mg.

Both are *used to produce polyvalent antivenoms*, sometimes in combination, depending on the geographic target. Horses receive *venom cocktails in tiny, titrated doses* to generate broad-spectrum antibodies.

*4️⃣ How It Works*

Venom is injected *subcutaneously or intramuscularly* in escalating doses over weeks.

The horse’s immune system recognizes the toxins and produces *immunoglobulins (IgG).*

Plasma is collected, antibodies are purified, and voilà — *human antivenom is born.*

*5️⃣ Fun Pharmacist Fact*

The amount of venom injected into a horse is *thousands of times less than a lethal bite*, yet the antibodies produced can neutralize venom in humans — making this one of the most remarkable examples of turning poison into medicine.

So next time you hear “snake antivenom,” remember: *it’s the slow, calculated bravery of the horse that saves lives*, not the snake’s mercy.

*Pharmacist’s takeaway:* 
Antivenom production is a *careful interplay of toxin, immunity, and dosing* — a process that is as much art as science, ensuring both safety of the donor animal and efficacy for humans.

[06/02/2026, 13:18:56] King Penet: REPORT ON THE PETITION OF PHARM. KENNETH UJAH TO THE FEDERAL INVESTIGATION DEPARTMENT (FID) OF THE NIGERIA POLICE FORCE BY THE NATIONAL CHAIRMAN OF ACPN, PHARM. AMBROSE EZEH, AND THE NATIONAL SECRETARY, PHARM. OMOKHAFE ASHORE, ON ALLEGED CHARGES OF INCITEMENT, CYBERBULLYING, MISINFORMATION, CYBERCRIME, ETC., ARISING FROM THE POSTING OF INFORMATION ON ACPN FCT BRANCH ACTIVITIES ON ACPN NATIONAL WHATSAPP PLATFORMS

Warm greetings, esteemed colleagues.



Preamble

This report is necessitated by recent developments orchestrated by the Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh–led administration of the Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN), which appears to be deliberately targeted at the continuous destabilisation of the ACPN FCT Branch leadership. These actions have taken the form of what may best be described as individualised punitive tactics, carried out without transparency and without the knowledge of the dues-paying members of the Association.


Body of the Report

On 29th December 2025, I was invited for an interview by the Federal Investigation Department (FID), Force Headquarters, Abuja, following a petition authored by the National Chairman of ACPN, Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh, and the National Secretary, Pharm. Omokhafe Ashore.

The petition accused me of incitement, cyberbullying, misinformation, and cybercrime, allegedly arising from my posting of information relating to the activities of the duly elected Chairman of ACPN FCT Branch, Pharm. Aloba Olatunji Isaac, MAW, DCPHARM, OCPharm, on ACPN National WhatsApp platforms.

My experience at the FID can best be described as a complete exercise in futility. The entire process was embarrassing to our noble profession and practice as Community Pharmacists and amounted to a needless waste of Association funds.

Subsequently, both the petitioners and the petitioned were invited for a face-to-face meeting with FID officers on 20th January 2026, during which the following resolutions were reached:

1. There was no basis for the prosecution of Pharm. Kenneth Ujah by the Nigeria Police Force, as no evidence of misinformation, incitement, or cybercrime was found in any of the posts shared on the ACPN WhatsApp platforms. Rather, the matter was adjudged to be purely political in nature, a fact which Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh openly admitted during the meeting.


2. The National Chairman, Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh, was advised not to act against the will of the members of ACPN FCT Branch by supporting a candidate who did not conform to due electoral processes, regardless of the justification.


3. Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh was reminded of his role as a leader and encouraged to act as a father to all, refraining from actions that encourage or deepen divisions among members of the FCT Branch.


4. It was resolved that the National Chairman should procure a dedicated SIM card and mobile phone registered in the name of the Association for official use only, which should be transferable from one administration to another, in order to prevent the use of personal phone numbers for official ACPN communication platforms.


5. It was clearly stated that Pharm. Kenneth Ujah did not violate any provision of the ACPN Constitution by having access to the ACPN National WhatsApp announcement platform, since the platform was created using a personal SIM card.


6. Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh was advised that he was free to create another ACPN WhatsApp announcement platform, provided he complied fully with the resolution stated in item (4) above.


7. Finally, Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh was directed to formally withdraw the petition in writing.


Critical Questions to the National Chairman

In light of the foregoing, it is now appropriate for members to ask the National Chairman of ACPN, Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh, the following critical questions:

1. What exactly is his interest in the persistent attempts to undermine and destabilise ACPN FCT Branch?


2. Whose interests or personal ego is being served?


3. Repeated references are made to - “NEC said this” or “NEC said that.” - Can this NEC ever be clearly identified or unmasked?

4. This FID petition is the fourth police petition written by Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh against members of the Pharm. Aloba Olatunji Isaac –led  administration in FCT, all of which have failed. Yet, the petitions continue. Who bears the financial burden of these actions?

5. There are now indications of a proposed petition to the EFCC to investigate the IPC, despite the clear awareness that such a move would end in public embarrassment. Why persist in actions that only squander ACPN funds to satisfy unseen and unknown interests? Will the National Chairman ever render a comprehensive account of all police petitions and court cases instituted against ACPN state branches under his leadership?


Conclusion

It is now evident that the current National Chairman of ACPN, Pharm. Ambrose Ezeh, and the National Secretary, Pharm. Omokhafe Ashore, acted impulsively and without adequate guidance or proper understanding of the law by petitioning the FID to prosecute a fellow member without any supporting evidence.

Unlike the so-called investigative or disciplinary committees of ACPN, which have operated in reverse logic—working from answers to questions and recommending the placement of colleagues on an unlawful “dishonour list” (powers clearly outside the scope of ACPN)—the officers of the Federal Investigation Department demonstrated professionalism, objectivity, and due process.



Long live ACPN FCT Branch!
Long live ACPN!!
Long live PSN!!!



Pharm. Kenneth Ujah
Abuja

‎[07/02/2026, 09:18:46] ~ Lancelot: *LANCE PHARMA SPOTLIGHT:From Pills to Programs- How Software Is Quietly Becoming the New Drug*

For decades, pharmacy has revolved around molecules—tablets, injections, suspensions. But a silent shift is underway. Today, *software itself is being regulated, prescribed, and reimbursed like medicine*. Welcome to the era of *Digital Therapeutics (DTx)*.

This isn’t fitness apps or wellness trackers. These are *FDA-authorized software interventions* that prevent, manage, or treat disease—sometimes *with no active pharmaceutical ingredient at all.*

And yes, pharmacists are central to this revolution.

*When Software Becomes a Prescription*

The U.S. FDA now recognizes *Software as a Medical Device (SaMD)*, and several *digital therapeutics* already carry FDA authorization.

*🔹 reSET®️ (FDA-authorized)*

✅Indication: Substance Use Disorder (SUD)

✅What it does: Delivers cognitive behavioral therapy through a prescription app

✅Clinical impact: Improves abstinence rates when used alongside standard care

✅Why it matters to pharmacists: This is a _prescribable therapy_—with clinical outcomes—without a pill.

*🔹 reSET-O®️*

✅Indication: Opioid Use Disorder

✅Used alongside buprenorphine

✅Demonstrates how *digital therapeutics can act as drug extenders*, improving adherence and outcomes rather than replacing medicines.

*ADHD, Insomnia, and the End of “Drug-Only” Thinking*

*🔹 EndeavorRx®️ (FDA-authorized)*

✅Indication: Pediatric ADHD

✅Therapy delivered through a video-game-like interface

✅Proven to improve attention function

✅Pharmacist insight: This challenges the assumption that neuropsychiatric disorders must be treated only with stimulants.


*🔹 Somryst®️*

✅Indication: Chronic insomnia

✅Digital CBT-I therapy

✅Comparable efficacy to hypnotics—without dependency or tolerance

This raises a powerful question:

> What if the first-line “drug” for some conditions has no chemical structure at all?

*Why This Matters Deeply to Pharmacists*

Digital therapeutics are not replacing pharmacists—they are *expanding our clinical relevance.*

Pharmacists are uniquely positioned to:

Educate patients on *how and when to use DTx*

Integrate DTx with pharmacologic regimens

Monitor adherence, outcomes, and safety

Guide therapy selection where software + medicine outperform medicine alone


In short, pharmacists move from dispensing molecules to managing therapeutic systems.

*The Bigger Shift: From Medication to Medication Intelligence*

Software-based therapies introduce:

🟠Real-time data feedback

🟠Adaptive dosing recommendations

🟠Behavioral modification at scale

🟠Personalized therapy without increasing pill burden


This aligns with where healthcare is heading: ✔ Precision medicine
✔ Reduced adverse effects
✔ Outcome-based care

A pill acts after *ingestion*.
A program acts *continuously.*

*The Provocative Ending*

The pharmacy of the future will stock more than shelves.
It will manage *algorithms, interfaces, data, and outcomes.*

And the most dangerous question for pharmacists is not:

> “Will software replace drugs?”

But rather:

*_“Will pharmacists who ignore software be replaced?”_* ‎image omitted

*LANCE PHARMA | Logistics That Refuse to Hesitate*

_“The living remembers miracles;_
_the dead reminds us that logistics once hesitated.”_

_History is not cruel because medicine failed_ —
_history is cruel because *medicine arrived late.*_

Germany remembers its heroes.

It remembers *Dr. Gerhard Domagk*, who proved the power of sulfonamides, yet watched patients die in earlier years when *antibacterial drugs were unavailable or delayed*, turning simple infections into fatal sepsis.

It remembers wounded soldiers of the World Wars who survived bullets but died quietly from *untreated infections*, because *penicillin had not yet reached the frontline*, and logistics lagged behind discovery.
It remembers accident victims on the early Autobahns — lives that could have been saved *if paramedic response and emergency adrenaline, oxygen, or IV fluids* had arrived minutes earlier.

They didn’t die because medicine didn’t exist.
They died because *delivery hesitated.*

That pause —
that gap between _knowing and arriving_ —
is where lives were lost.

‎[09/02/2026, 20:45:16] Pharm. Austin YPGd: *To whom it may concern!!!* ‎image omitted
[09/02/2026, 21:48:13] Ovie David Delsu Ypgd: You all know Pharmacy today as a “ *regulated, noble, patient-centred profession.”* 
That is the public narrative.

 _It is clean._ 
 _It is reassuring._ 
 _And it is incomplete_ .

What has been sold to you is a curated truth—designed for conferences, CPD slides, and ceremonial white coats—while the real power structure of the profession operates quietly, deliberately, behind the curtain.

 _Let us state the uncomfortable fact plainly_ .

 Pharmacy did not lose relevance by accident.
It was engineered. 

There was a time when pharmacists were the undisputed custodians of medicines—formulation, dispensing, pricing, policy, access, and safety. That authority was not stolen overnight. *It was surrendered incrementally, negotiated away in boardrooms, traded for titles, committee seats, and the illusion of peace* .

Remember this period well: *the era of so-called “interprofessional harmony* .”

That harmony was never equal.

While pharmacists argued over nomenclature, dress codes, and association politics, other professionals occupied the spaces pharmacists abandoned—clinical authority, procurement control, policy influence, and public trust. By the time the profession realised what was happening, the doors were already locked.

Ask yourself, honestly: Who controls drug procurement at federal and state levels?
Who determines medicine pricing frameworks?
Who dominates hospital decision-making structures?
Who benefits most from donor funds and special health interventions?

 _The answers are inconvenient_ .

Another truth deliberately avoided: community pharmacy is used as the emotional shield of the profession while being economically strangled.

Community pharmacists are celebrated rhetorically and punished structurally. Policies speak of access while supply chains reward import cartels. Ethics are demanded in a system that makes ethical survival increasingly difficult.

If regulation were truly fair and transparent, many entities paraded as pharmaceutical giants would not survive a single rigorous audit. Enforcement is selective. Sanctions are negotiable. Compliance depends less on standards and more on proximity to power.

Hospital pharmacy tells the same story.

Pharmacists are labelled “core clinical team members” without clinical authority. They attend ward rounds where decisions are pre-made. They document interventions that rarely influence procurement or policy. It is participation without power—visibility without consequence.

Academia completes the cycle.

Thousands are trained annually using outdated curricula, released into an oversaturated market, and then blamed for the outcomes of a system that failed to evolve. Curriculum reform crawls. Industrial training remains largely symbolic.

Now to the issue everyone avoids: *control of pharmaceutical wealth.* 

Medicines generate billions, yet the average pharmacist remains trapped at subsistence level. This is not coincidence. Wealth concentration replaced collective advancement. A narrow elite controls import licences, distribution pipelines, and regulatory access, while the majority compete at retail level under degrading conditions.

Philanthropy appears when scrutiny rises.
Silence follows when attention fades.
Transparency is episodic.

 *Accountability is optional* .

And whenever reform is demanded, the same warning is issued: “Do not wash our dirty linen in public.”

That sentence has harmed pharmacy more than any external opposition.
Silence did not protect the profession.
It protected interests.

 _This is not an attack on pharmacy_ .
 _It is an intervention._ 

The future of pharmacy will not be secured by more titles, parallel associations, or ceremonial leadership. It will be secured by economic justice within the profession, transparent regulation, modernised training, equitable access to opportunity, and pharmacists reclaiming authority they voluntarily surrendered.

If pharmacists cannot benefit collectively from the wealth their profession generates, then the system is broken. And if that system resists reform, questioning it is not rebellion —it is responsibility.

No pharmacist is superior to another.
No sector owns the profession.
No generation has monopoly over relevance.

If pharmacy is to survive, truth must be allowed to breathe.

And if that truth unsettles some people, then it is doing precisely what it should.


©️ OKORO OVIE DAVID

[10/02/2026, 18:34:00] King Penet: Public Alert No. 05/2026.
Alert on the mop-up of counterfeit Dermazin (1% Silver Sulphadiazine) Cream.
#NAFDACAlerts

https://bit.ly/4r9Tnf5

NAFDAC is alerting healthcare providers and the public to the circulation of counterfeit Dermazin (1% Silver Sulphadiazine) Cream.

NAFDAC received a complaint from the legitimate Marketing Authorisation Holder, Taylek Drugs Company Limited, concerning the sale of this counterfeit product. The packaging of the falsified Dermazin Cream falsely claims that it is produced by Taylek Drugs Company Limited.

Risk Statement
The illegal marketing of medicinal products and counterfeit medicines is a significant health risk as it fails to ensure the safety, quality, and efficacy of these items, violating regulatory standards.

Healthcare professionals and consumers are advised to report any suspicion of the sale of substandard and falsified medicines or medical devices to the nearest NAFDAC office, call 0800-162-3322, or send an email to sf.alert@nafdac.gov.ng

For complaints, call the Reforms Unit on the following lines: 09097630506, 09097630507, or send an email to reforms@nafdac.gov.ng

_“A business without logistics is a body without circulation; ideas may exist, but life cannot flow.”_

History teaches us hard lessons about delay. During World War II, *German Field Marshal Erwin Rommel* depended on steady medical and supply lines across North Africa. When Allied forces disrupted logistics, even essential items — from fuel to quinine for malaria and other critical medical supplies — became scarce. The failure of supply chains weakened troops, cost momentum, and turned strength into vulnerability.

*The lesson is clear:*
It is not always the enemy that defeats a man — sometimes it is the delay.

In healthcare, that delay can be an inhaler not restocked, insulin not reordered, antibiotics not delivered on time. One postponed payment, one neglected order, one assumption that “it can wait” — and something precious is at risk.

To our valued clients:
When you prioritize timely payments and restocking, you are not just running a pharmacy — you are protecting someone’s breath, someone’s recovery, someone’s tomorrow.

To our medical professionals:
Negligence in supply is not a small oversight; it can cost trust, reputation, and even a life.

At *LANCE PHARMA*, we believe circulation must never stop.
Because when logistics flows efficiently, confidence grows, health is preserved, and lives are safeguarded.

‎[13/02/2026, 18:52:26] ~ Lancelot: *LANCE PHARMACOPOETICS*

*“Laughing in Chains: The Love and Martyrdom of Saint Valentine”*

In Rome there lived a merry priest, bold and kind,
Saint Valentine they called him, with a fearless mind.
While stern old Claudius II frowned and shouted, “No more weddings here!”
Valentine winked, “Where love is true, I have no fear.”
He married couples in secret rooms at night,
With candle flames dancing soft and bright.
He’d chuckle low, “A ring is small, yet strong—
For little keys can lock hearts long.”

He teased the guards, he joked with cheer,
“Even soldiers need sweethearts, my dear!”
For love is not gold, nor heavy to bear,
A loaf shared in two shows a heart that cares.
He’d say, “A tiny seed makes forests grow;
Small drops of rain make rivers flow.”
And lovers laughed in quiet delight,
While Rome slept blind to love that night.

But walls have ears and whispers fly,
Soon chains replaced his wedding cry.
In prison dark he kept his grin,
“Stone walls,” he said, “can’t cage love in.”
He healed a girl who could not see,
And signed a note, “From your Valentine,” tenderly.
For even in sorrow, hope would rise—
“The sun still shines,” he’d softly advise.

Yet power fears what it cannot control,
And swords are drawn against the soul.
On February’s cold and fateful morn,
His life was taken, his body torn.
The crowd grew silent, the laughter done—
Love’s faithful priest faced death alone.
But mark this truth the ages tell:
“They may kill the man, but love lives well.”
For though he died by cruel decree,
His name blooms still in memory.

Today, as the Honourable Commissioner for Health, Edo State, I officially declared a Lassa Fever Outbreak in our State following a concerning rise in confirmed cases.
We have recorded 29 confirmed cases with 6 deaths, with a notable increase in Etsako West and Esan West Local Government Areas. This trend requires urgent, coordinated, and decisive action.

In response:
An Incident Manager has been appointed to lead the emergency response.
A Case Manager has been designated to coordinate clinical management of patients.

All pillars of the Edo State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) have been fully activated.
The Director of Public Health will provide daily situation reports to my office to ensure transparency, accountability, and swift action.

Our response will focus on:
Rapid case identification and isolation
Strengthened surveillance and contact tracing
Community engagement and risk communication
Protection of healthcare workers
Environmental sanitation and rodent control.

I urge all Edo residents to take preventive measures seriously:
✔️ Maintain proper food storage
✔️ Keep homes and surroundings clean
✔️ Avoid contact with rodents and their droppings
✔️ Report symptoms such as persistent fever, sore throat, bleeding, weakness, or unexplained illness to the nearest health facility immediately
Lassa fever is preventable, and early presentation saves lives.

Edo State has successfully managed outbreaks in the past, and we will confront this one with the same courage, science-driven strategy, and unity.
Let us work together to protect our families and communities.
